h1: America's integrated mobile security infrastructure company.

body:
## We do not sell cameras. We deploy mobile security infrastructure.

Most providers stop at the box. We own the stack: solar-autonomous hardware, an ONVIF/RTSP cloud VMS running on AWS, and a 24/7 Security Operations Center staffed inside the United States. One contract. One support number. One accountability line when something goes wrong at 2 a.m.

We have been doing this since 2017. 500+ active deployments across 30+ states. Seven years of field data informing every firmware push.

## The problem with most "mobile security."

A trailer with a camera on it is not security. It is a recording device. Construction theft costs the industry more than $1B per year and less than 7% of stolen equipment is recovered (FBI). Retail organized crime is up 18% YoY (NRF). Cargo theft tops $15B annually. Footage after the fact does not solve any of that.

Active deterrence with human verification does. So does sub-3-second alerting. So does live audio challenge through a PA mounted to the unit. So does direct law enforcement dispatch with live video already in the officer's hand.

## What "integrated" actually means.

**Hardware.** Sky Guard MSU pairs thermal LWIR, 500ft ground radar, 4K multi-sensor, LPR, and active deterrence on a 22ft mast running on 600W of solar with 48+ hour battery reserve. Swift Deploy Trailer hits site in under 20 minutes, deployed by one person with no tools. Boundary Guard Pro covers 500+ linear feet of fence line with no blind spots.

**Cloud VMS.** AI VisionStream runs on AWS, US-only data residency, TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, RBAC and MFA standard, immutable 12-month audit log. ONVIF and RTSP compliant — bring your existing cameras or buy ours. LPR accuracy above 95% with alerts in under three seconds.

**SOC.** Our US-staffed Security Operations Center escalates verified threats in under 60 seconds. Live audio challenge through the trailer PA. Direct law enforcement dispatch with live video. 97% false alarm reduction. A full incident report per event, not a vague log entry.

## Proven ROI, not projected.

A national general contractor running a $28M Mid-Atlantic project deployed two Swift Deploy Trailers and three Solar Camera Poles. In 12 months:

- 73% theft reduction
- $0 insurance claims filed
- Monthly security cost dropped from $32,400 (manned guards) to $4,000
- $340,800 saved in year one

That is the case study we lead with because it is the math every operator runs in their head. We did not invent these numbers in a deck. They came off a real job.

## Compliance is a feature, not a sales objection.

NDAA Section 889 compliant. AWS Cloud Partner. US-only AWS regions. Assembled in Pikesville, Maryland — not Shenzhen. RBAC, MFA, immutable audit log, configurable 30/60/90-day cloud retention. If your federal, defense, utility, or critical-infrastructure customer asks the question, we already have the answer in writing.

## How we engage.

Lease from $1,500/mo (Swift Deploy) or $2,200/mo (Sky Guard). Purchase Sky Guard MSU from $38,000. Mix and match across a site. Add SOC monitoring per unit or per portfolio. Scale up for a six-month construction phase, scale down when the building goes vertical. The trailers redeploy. So does the contract.

faq.q: Do you require us to use your cameras?
faq.a: No. AI VisionStream is ONVIF and RTSP compliant. We integrate with existing camera fleets and add VDS hardware where it makes sense. Camera-agnostic is a technical commitment, not a marketing line.

faq.q: How fast does the SOC actually respond?
faq.a: Under 60 seconds from event trigger to live operator engagement. Operators issue live audio challenges through the trailer PA, then dispatch local law enforcement with live video streaming if the threat is verified. 97% of false alarms are filtered before they reach you.

faq.q: Is the hardware NDAA compliant?
faq.a: Yes — Section 889 compliant, assembled in Pikesville, MD. No prohibited components. Documentation provided on request for federal, defense, and critical infrastructure procurement.

faq.q: What does a typical deployment cost?
faq.a: Swift Deploy Trailer from $1,500/mo. Sky Guard MSU from $2,200/mo lease or $38,000 purchase. Most multi-unit construction sites run $4,000-$8,000/mo all-in with SOC monitoring — versus $25,000-$40,000/mo for manned guards.

faq.q: How long does deployment take?
faq.a: One person, no tools, under 20 minutes for Swift Deploy. Sky Guard MSU is comparable. We handle delivery, siting, and commissioning. Live in AI VisionStream the same day.

faq.q: Can I keep cameras live if a site loses power?
faq.a: Yes. Every mobile unit runs on solar with 36-48+ hour battery reserve. The cameras, the analytics, and the SOC link stay live through power outages, which is when most incidents happen.

body:
Vision Detection Systems is America's integrated mobile security infrastructure company. We design, assemble, deploy, and monitor the hardware. We operate the cloud VMS that ingests the video. We staff the SOC that responds when something moves on a perimeter at 3 AM. One vendor. One support number. One throat to choke when a unit goes offline at 2:14 AM on a Saturday.

That integration is the point. The site security industry fragmented decades ago into hardware vendors, software vendors, monitoring centers, and integrators who stitched them together with cable and hope. Customers pay for that fragmentation in finger-pointing, in unmonitored cameras, in 18-minute response times that should have been 47 seconds. We rebuilt the stack so the people who manufactured the unit are the same people who answer the radio when the operator hits the talk-down button.

## What we do

**Solar-autonomous mobile surveillance units.** Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, and Boundary Guard Pro — three platforms covering construction sites, perimeters, lots, yards, and remote infrastructure. No trenching. No grid hookup. Deploy in 4 hours.

**Camera-agnostic cloud VMS.** Hosted on AWS GovCloud-adjacent infrastructure. TLS 1.3 in transit. AES-256 at rest. US-only data residency. Integrates with existing IP cameras alongside VDS units — you are not locked into one hardware ecosystem.

**24/7 US-staffed Security Operations Center.** Live operators. Sub-60-second escalation on verified events. 97% false alarm reduction against industry baseline. Audio talk-down. Police dispatch with verified video evidence packets.

## What makes this different

We have 7 years of field data on units running in coastal humidity, desert heat, Mid-Atlantic winters, and active construction zones. We know what fails at month 14 and what fails at month 38, because we have units that have been running that long. We are not a Series A startup chasing a category. We are a hardware company that learned to run a SOC because the alternative was watching our cameras be ignored by third-party monitoring centers that charged $9 per signal and forwarded everything to the customer at 4:00 AM.

## What we have proven

On a $28M Mid-Atlantic GC project in 2024, our deployment saved the customer $340,800 in 12 months — measured against their prior year's loss, vandalism, and guard-staffing costs. That number is on the case study page with the methodology. It is not the average. It is one project. We publish it because the math is real and the customer signed off.

## What is non-negotiable

NDAA Section 889 compliance on every component. AWS-backed infrastructure with formal partner status. RBAC and MFA on every account. Documented data residency. SOC 2 Type II audit in progress with target completion Q4 2026. If your procurement team asks for a security questionnaire, we have one ready before the call ends.

heroSubhead: Camera-agnostic VMS, solar-autonomous hardware, and a 24/7 US Security Operations Center under one roof. Compared honestly against every major player in mobile surveillance, cloud video, and managed monitoring.
body:
## Why we publish honest comparisons

Most security vendor "vs." pages are sales theater. We take a different approach. Every page on this hub names a competitor, cites public incidents with dates and sources, lists the places that competitor genuinely beats VDS, and shows the places we beat them. If a competitor has the best mobile app in the category, we say so. If they had 150,000 cameras hacked in 2021, we say that too.

This hub indexes eleven detailed comparisons plus two architecture pages (rental vs. purchase, solar vs. diesel). Each page ships with a 12-18 row feature matrix, a sourced incident log, a total-cost-of-ownership math block, and a 3-step migration plan if you're switching to VDS.

## Pick your comparison

**Mobile surveillance and trailers**
- VDS vs. LVT — the largest mobile surveillance player with ~5,000 units deployed
- VDS vs. WCCTV — UK-origin construction rental specialist
- VDS vs. Flock Safety — ALPR network with a January 2026 breach exposing 67 cameras

**Cloud VMS and indoor video AI**
- VDS vs. Verkada — strong UX, $2.95M FTC settlement in 2024
- VDS vs. Spot AI — best-designed indoor video AI, no outdoor or SOC

**Managed monitoring services**
- VDS vs. Pro-Vigil — virtual guards, no first-party platform
- VDS vs. Stealth Monitoring / ECAM — 140,000+ cameras monitored, three brand names in 18 months

**Architecture and approach**
- VDS vs. Security Guards — $1,500-$2,200/mo per trailer vs. $60K-$110K/yr per FTE
- VDS vs. Fixed Cameras — wired install lead time, no redeployment
- Rental vs. Purchase — when to expense it, when to capitalize it
- Solar vs. Diesel — energy density, runtime, refueling cost

## How to use this hub

If you're evaluating two or three vendors at once, open them in tabs. Every matrix uses the same column order so you can compare across pages. If you want a single PDF with every matrix combined, hit the download button in the hero. If you want VDS plugged into your specific site list, book a 20-minute architecture call and bring a site address — we'll pre-pull satellite, sun angle, and cell coverage before the call.

## What we will not do

We won't compare on vibes. Every "where competitor wins" callout has to be defensible in front of that competitor's sales team. Every "where VDS wins" callout has a source — an FTC docket, a court filing, a city council vote, a manufacturer spec sheet, or a deployment of ours we can name on a call under NDA.

faq.q: Why include "where the competitor wins" sections at all?
faq.a: Because every honest evaluation has trade-offs, and pretending otherwise insults the buyer. If Verkada's mobile app is better than ours for a specific use case, you should know that before you sign with us. We'd rather lose a deal at the evaluation stage than 18 months in.

faq.q: How often do you update these pages?
faq.a: Quarterly minimum, plus any time a competitor ships a material product change or has a public incident with a date and a source. The Flock page was rewritten three times in Q1 2026 after the January exposure and follow-on city cancellations.

faq.q: Can I get a custom comparison against a vendor not listed here?
faq.a: Yes. Email the vendor name and your site type to sales@visiondetectionsystems.com and we'll build a one-pager within five business days. We've done custom comparisons against Eagle Eye Networks, Avigilon, Rhombus, Genetec, and Milestone in the past.

faq.q: Is the matrix data audited?
faq.a: Every competitor claim is sourced to a public document, press release, court filing, or product spec sheet as of the page's last revision date (shown at the page footer). If a row reads "not published," it means we couldn't find a public source — not that the feature doesn't exist.

finalCTAHeading: Pick a comparison, or skip the comparisons and book a call
finalCTABody: 20 minutes, one site address, no slide deck. We'll pull sun angle, cell coverage, and a preliminary unit count before you hang up.

Security directors at GCs, utility cooperatives, retail loss prevention, municipal procurement officers, event producers, and CFOs running the budget approval. If you're writing a spec or defending a line item, start here.

body:
## One platform. Industry-specific configurations.

We do not sell a generic camera package and call it a "solution." Every deployment starts with a site assessment, a threat profile, and a configuration sized to the actual risk — equipment theft on a construction site behaves differently than catalytic converter theft at a dealership or copper theft at a substation.

The underlying stack is the same across every vertical:

- **Solar-autonomous hardware** — Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, Boundary Guard Pro, Solar Camera Poles. No trenching. No utility hookup. Operational in 4 hours.
- **AI VisionStream cloud VMS** — intrusion zones, virtual tripwires, loitering and crowd detection, time-of-day rules, license plate recognition at 95%+ accuracy with sub-3-second alerts.
- **24/7 US Security Operations Center** — Pikesville, MD. <60-second escalation. 97% false alarm reduction. Live audio talk-down and direct law enforcement dispatch.

What changes per industry is camera placement, analytics rule sets, escalation thresholds, and which assets we point the lens at.

## Six primary verticals

**Construction** — General contractors, infrastructure projects, equipment yards. Copper, fuel, generators, tools. FBI estimates >$1B in annual theft with <7% recovery. Our Mid-Atlantic GC case study: $340,800 saved in 12 months, 73% theft reduction, $0 insurance claims.

**Utilities & Substations** — Off-grid substations, transmission yards, water treatment. NERC CIP-014 physical security alignment. Copper theft and vandalism are the dominant loss vectors; solar-autonomous deployment is a natural fit where utility hookups don't exist.

**Retail & Shopping Centers** — Multi-store loss prevention programs, parking lots, ORC and flash-mob response. NRF reports 18% YoY shoplifting increase and 67% of retailers citing transnational ORC involvement. LPR captures getaway plates within seconds.

**Auto Dealerships** — Catalytic converter theft, vehicle theft, after-hours liability. Rhodium is back to $10,400/oz in 2026 and converter claims remain elevated. Entry/exit LPR plus lot coverage closes the gap insurance won't.

**Parking Lots & Garages** — Operators (LAZ, ABM, ParkMobile-class) facing vehicle break-in, vandalism, and assault liability. Center-of-lot Sky Guard plus perimeter poles deliver coverage without trenching the asphalt.

**Government & Public Safety** — Federal, state, municipal property — parks, motor pools, public works yards, water districts. NDAA Section 889 compliant. Available via Sourcewell and GSA cooperative purchasing. This is private-property surveillance, not community-wide camera networks.

## Eleven additional verticals

Logistics & distribution yards. Cannabis cultivation and dispensaries. Marinas. Self-storage. Cold storage. Solar and wind farms. Mining and aggregates. Schools and campuses (private property only). Houses of worship. Multifamily residential. Critical infrastructure (telecom, data centers).

Each runs the same hardware and software stack with a different analytics rule set.

faq.q: Do you sell hardware only, or is the SOC required?
faq.a: You can purchase hardware outright or as a monthly service that includes the SOC, AI VisionStream cloud, maintenance, and cellular. About 90% of customers choose the monthly model because the SOC is what turns recorded video into prevented loss.

faq.q: Which vertical drives the most volume for VDS?
faq.a: Construction by deployment count, government by contract size. Both rely on the same hardware — Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, Solar Camera Poles — configured differently.

faq.q: My industry isn't listed. Do you serve it?
faq.a: Probably. The 17 verticals are where we have repeated playbooks. If you have a perimeter, valuable assets behind it, and limited or no fixed power, we can size a configuration. Book an assessment.

faq.q: How fast can you stand up a site?
faq.a: A Swift Deploy unit is operational in 4 hours from arrival. A multi-unit construction site or substation perimeter takes 1-3 days depending on scale.

finalCTAHeading: Find the configuration for your site
finalCTABody: Tell us your industry, site size, and current loss profile. We'll respond within 24 hours with a sized configuration and pricing.

heroSubhead: VDS works with security integrators, construction services firms, and regional resellers who want to sell solar-autonomous mobile surveillance backed by a 24/7 US SOC. Margin is real. Support is staffed. Training is included.
body:
## Why partner with VDS

The site security market is large, fragmented, and underserved by traditional fixed-camera integrators. Customers want a 24/7 monitored mobile unit they can deploy in 4 hours without trenching. Most integrators cannot build that themselves. We can. You sell the relationship. We deliver the integrated stack.

The economics work because we own the manufacturing, the VMS, and the SOC. There is no extra vendor between you and the customer outcome. When you escalate a customer issue, it goes to one company — ours.

## What partners get

- **Margin** that supports a real sales motion, not lead-gen pennies
- **Dedicated channel team** for deal support, scoping, and configuration
- **Training program** for sales and field staff, in-person in Pikesville or virtually
- **Marketing assets** — spec sheets, decks, customer-facing one-pagers, ROI calculators
- **Lead routing** — qualified leads in your territory get routed to you
- **Co-branding and white-label options** for high-volume integrators
- **Financing programs** for end customers — lease and multi-year options

## Two partner tiers

**Authorized Dealer.** Standard program. Quarterly commitment, MDF available, lead routing, sales and technical training. Best fit for regional integrators and construction services firms doing 12+ deployments per year.

**Strategic Partner.** White-label or co-branded units, dedicated account team, joint go-to-market planning, custom pricing. Best fit for national integrators, modular construction firms, and large GC service organizations doing 100+ deployments per year.

## What we look for in partners

- Existing customer relationships in our target segments (construction, perimeter, lot, energy, public sector adjacent)
- A working install and service capability, or willingness to subcontract VDS field services
- A direct line to your customers' security and operations decision-makers — not a reseller of resellers
- A clean compliance posture in your own operations (we will ask about NDAA, insurance, and licensing)

## Where to start

If you are a fit, the application process below takes about 20 minutes. We review applications within 5 business days. If we approve, onboarding takes about 30 days from contract signature to first deployment.

faq.q: Do I need to commit to a minimum deployment volume?
faq.a: Yes. Authorized Dealer minimum is 12 units per year. Strategic Partner is negotiated based on territory and pipeline.

faq.q: Can I sell VDS alongside other security brands?
faq.a: Yes. Most dealers do. We do not require exclusivity. We do require that VDS units are presented accurately and that customers are not steered to competing products mid-deal.

faq.q: What is the difference between a dealer and a referral partner?
faq.a: A dealer sells, supports, and maintains the customer relationship. A referral partner introduces leads and earns a referral fee. Both programs exist; the dealer program is the primary channel.

faq.q: Do you sell direct to end customers?
faq.a: Yes, in territories without an active dealer or for enterprise accounts above a threshold. Where a dealer is active in-territory, we route those leads to the dealer.

finalCTAHeading: Two paths. Pick one.
finalCTABody: Apply to become a dealer, or schedule a 30-minute partnership intro call to discuss territory, volume, and program fit.

heroSubhead: AWS-backed video management software, AI analytics, and a 24/7 US Security Operations Center — wired together by the same company that builds the trailers. Bring your ONVIF/RTSP cameras or ours.
body:
## Software-led, hardware-honest

Most "AI security platforms" are a UI wrapper over a third-party VMS, a third-party AI model, and a third-party monitoring center that bills hourly. AI VisionStream is one stack, built by one company, since 2017.

Camera-agnostic ingest. AWS US-only data residency. Analytics tuned on 7 years of field footage. A SOC in our building, not a contractor's. The mobile trailer in your parking lot runs the same software as the rooftop camera on your headquarters.

## What you get on day one

- **Camera-agnostic ingest** over ONVIF and RTSP. Axis, Hanwha, Bosch, and 40+ others. Bring what you own.
- **Rule-driven analytics**: intrusion zones, virtual tripwires, loitering windows, crowd thresholds, time-of-day rules.
- **License plate recognition** with 95%+ accuracy and sub-3-second alerts on hotlist matches.
- **24/7 US Security Operations Center** with under 60-second escalation, live audio talk-down, and direct LE dispatch with live video.
- **Mobile app** (iOS + Android) for live multi-camera view, alert acknowledgement, and two-way audio.
- **Integrations** with Lenel, Genetec, Brivo, Bold, Stages, ServiceNow, Jira, PagerDuty, and Slack.
- **30, 60, or 90-day cloud storage** with TLS 1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest.
- **Immutable 12-month audit log** on every user action, every alert, every camera event.

## Why one stack matters

Three vendors means three SLAs, three support queues, and three places to blame when an alert is missed at 2:47 a.m. We own the camera, the network, the cloud, the AI, and the operator. One number to call. One contract. One root-cause analysis.

## Compliance and privacy that holds up under audit

NDAA Section 889 compliant. AWS Cloud Partner. US-based operators. US-only AWS regions. No Dahua. No Hikvision. RBAC and MFA on every account. A 12-month audit trail you can export to your SIEM.

We do not publish a camera feed to the public internet. We do not sell footage. We do not run pattern-of-life databases on anyone driving by.

## Built for sites that move

Construction yards, multi-family developments, auto dealerships, logistics yards, retail rollouts, utility substations. Mobile trailers redeploy in under 30 minutes. Fixed-site installs pull video from the cameras you already paid for. The platform does not care which.

## How the pieces fit

[Diagram placeholder: Cameras → AI VisionStream cloud (AWS US) → Analytics + LPR → SOC operator → Mobile app + LE dispatch + Integrations]

Start with the [analytics engine](/platform/analytics). Layer on [LPR](/platform/lpr). Route the alerts through the [SOC](/platform/soc) or your own team via the [mobile app](/platform/mobile-app). Wire it into your stack through [integrations](/platform/integrations). Lock it down with [platform security](/platform/security).

faq.q: Do I have to replace my existing cameras?
faq.a: No. AI VisionStream ingests any ONVIF or RTSP camera that is not on the NDAA prohibited list (Dahua, Hikvision, and their OEMs). Most sites onboard their existing Axis, Hanwha, or Bosch fleet in under a day.

faq.q: Where is the video stored?
faq.a: AWS US-only regions. TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. Retention is configurable at 30, 60, or 90 days. Footage is never replicated outside the United States.

faq.q: Is the SOC in-house or contracted?
faq.a: In-house. US-based operators, employed by VDS, working from our facility. Average escalation time is under 60 seconds from alert to live operator action.

faq.q: How is this different from running Verkada or Flock?
faq.a: We are camera-agnostic, we publish our retention and encryption posture, and we do not expose camera feeds to the public internet. See our [compare page](/compare) for a side-by-side.

faq.q: What does it cost?
faq.a: Per-camera and per-site tiers starting at line-rate pricing published on [the pricing page](/platform/pricing). No hidden activation fees.

finalCTAHeading: See AI VisionStream on your own cameras.
finalCTABody: 20 minutes. Live operator demo. We ingest one of your existing camera feeds during the call.

body:
## Why we publish prices

The mobile surveillance industry runs on opacity. Vendors hide trailer rates behind sales gatekeepers, quote month-to-month customers different prices than fleet customers, and resist publishing platform tiers because comparison shopping kills margin. We've watched it for nine years.

Publishing prices is harder for us, easier for you. You can budget a project before scheduling a call. You can compare us against the competitor that won't tell you what their trailer costs. You can sign a delegated-authority PO without three rounds of negotiation. The trade is worth it.

Below is what we charge. Numbers are net of taxes and shipping. Volume, multi-year, dealer, and government pricing are all available — see the section that applies.

## Mobile Surveillance Trailers

Standard lease pricing. All trailers ship with the Standard platform tier included; SOC monitoring is a separate add-on so customers running their own monitoring desk don't pay for what they don't use.

| Trailer | Monthly Lease | Purchase | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Swift Deploy Trailer** | $1,500/mo | Contact | General site, 20 ft mast |
| **Boundary Guard Pro** | $1,800/mo | Contact | 500 ft linear fence-line |
| **Sky Guard MSU** | $2,200/mo | $38,000 | Wide-area, 30 ft mast |
| **Solar Camera Pole** | Custom | Custom | Fixed-point solar autonomous |

Lease terms: 3-month minimum. Month-to-month after the minimum. No annual prepay required. Standard ground freight is billed at cost; expedited and weekend deployments quoted separately. Full lease terms: [Leasing & Rentals →](/pricing/leasing-rentals)

Purchase terms: 1-year hardware warranty standard, 3-year extended available, platform and SOC sold separately as ongoing subscriptions. Full purchase terms: [Purchase Options →](/pricing/purchase-options)

## VDS Platform — per camera, per month

The VMS that runs on every VDS trailer (and on third-party cameras you already own). Camera-agnostic, AWS-hosted, NDAA compliant.

| Tier | Price | Video Retention | Best For |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | $39/cam/mo | 30 days cloud | Single-site, general surveillance |
| **Pro** | $69/cam/mo | 60 days cloud | Multi-site, analytics-driven |
| **Enterprise** | Custom | 90 days cloud, full feature set | Fleet, federal, regulated |

Standard includes: live view, motion alerts, mobile app, basic analytics, 5 user seats.
Pro adds: advanced analytics (intrusion, line-crossing, loitering, PPE), LPR per-lane add-on, API access, 25 user seats.
Enterprise adds: SSO, audit logging, custom retention, dedicated CSM, white-glove onboarding, unlimited seats.

Full tier breakdown: [Subscription Plans →](/pricing/subscription-plans)

## 24/7 Security Operations Center

VDS-staffed, US-based, ESA-compliant. <60-second escalation on verified events.

| Service | Price |
|---|---|
| **SOC Active Monitoring** | $399/site/month |
| **SOC Hotlist (LPR-only sites)** | Included with LPR product |
| **Customer playbook customization** | Included |
| **Voice-down audio talk-down** | Included where hardware supports |

SOC is priced per site, not per camera. One $399/mo fee covers however many cameras live at that site. Most customers add SOC after 30-60 days of self-monitoring; it's not required to use the platform.

## Volume, dealer, and government pricing

- **Fleet customers (5+ trailers):** standard volume tiers apply — talk to sales for the matrix
- **Dealers and integrators:** [Dealer Pricing →](/pricing/dealers)
- **Federal, state, and local government:** GSA-adjacent pricing available; NDAA Section 889 documentation provided
- **Education and nonprofit:** discounted platform tiers available

## What's not in these prices

- State and local sales tax (varies by deployment state)
- One-time freight (typically $400-$900 per trailer one-way)
- Optional Starlink uplink ($150/month/unit, available where cellular is unreliable)
- Custom integrations or API engineering (quoted as a SOW)
- Site survey travel for sites requiring on-site pre-deploy assessment

faq.q: Is everything really priced this transparently?
faq.a: Yes, with two exceptions: Enterprise platform tier and large-fleet trailer pricing are quote-based because the configurations vary too much to list a single number. Everything else on this page is the number you'll see on your invoice.

faq.q: Can I lease one trailer for one month?
faq.a: No. Three-month minimum. The cost of mobilizing a trailer, onboarding the SOC, and demobilizing makes single-month leases uneconomic for both sides.

faq.q: Do I have to use the VDS platform if I buy a trailer outright?
faq.a: Functionally yes — the trailer is integrated with the platform stack. Standard tier is required at minimum. You're not locked into Pro or Enterprise.

faq.q: How does pricing change at scale?
faq.a: Volume discounts kick in at 5 trailers and 50 cameras. Dealer pricing structure is published on the [Dealer Pricing](/pricing/dealers) page.

faq.q: Are prices subject to change?
faq.a: Posted prices are honored for new quotes issued within 90 days. Existing customers are protected by their contract terms — typically 12-month price lock on lease rates.

faq.q: Can I get a custom quote without going through sales?
faq.a: Use the quote builder. It generates a configured price you can take to procurement. A sales rep follows up only if you ask for one.

finalCTAHeading: Build your quote
finalCTABody: Pick the trailers, the cameras, and the SOC coverage. Get a configured price in two minutes.

- Right to opt out of certain processing
- Right to non-discrimination for exercising rights

Process for submitting verified requests and response timelines.

VDS operates exclusively in the United States. We are not a GDPR-scoped controller. EU data subjects who nonetheless interact with our public website may exercise rights through the same process described above.

VDS services are not directed to children under 16. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If we learn we have collected such information, we will delete it.

VDS maintains technical and organizational measures appropriate to the risk, including encryption in transit (TLS 1.3), encryption at rest (AES-256), access controls (RBAC and MFA), audit logging, and incident response procedures. See the Trust Center for detail.

We will post material changes to this policy on this page and update the "last updated" date. For changes that materially affect existing customers, we will provide notice via email and in-product notification.

heroSubhead: Tell us what you are deploying, where, and when. A real human responds within 2 business days with a quote that includes hardware, monitoring, and contract terms.
body:
## How this works

The quote process is two short forms. The first is what you are deploying. The second is who you are and how to reach you. We do not gate the quote behind a 14-question qualification form. We do not require you to answer "what is your budget" before showing you a number.

## Step 1: What you are deploying {#step-1}

[PLACEHOLDER — Step 1 form embed]

The first form asks:

- **Number of sites** — single site, 2–5 sites, 6–25 sites, 26+ sites
- **Sites per location** — how many units per typical site
- **Site type** — construction project, perimeter, lot/yard, energy/infrastructure, mixed
- **Timeline** — within 30 days, 30–90 days, 90+ days, evaluating only
- **Contract preference** — month-to-month, multi-year, operating lease, project-based, undecided
- **Special requirements** — NDAA attestation, federal contract, GovCloud, custom integration

Estimated time: 3 minutes.

## Step 2: Who you are

After step 1, you will be asked for:

- **Name and title**
- **Company name and industry**
- **Business email**
- **Phone (optional)** — used only for the quote conversation, not for sales sequences
- **Preferred response method** — email or phone
- **Anything else we should know** — open text field

Estimated time: 2 minutes.

## What happens after submission

- **Within 2 hours:** Confirmation email with a quote reference number
- **Within 1 business day:** Initial scoping email from a VDS sales rep with clarifying questions if any
- **Within 2 business days:** Quote document delivered by email — includes hardware MSRP, monthly monitoring, available terms, and any deployment-specific fees

The quote is good for 30 days. Pricing on the standard product lines does not change within that window. Custom-configured deployments may require a follow-up engineering review before the quote is finalized.

## What is in a VDS quote

A standard VDS quote document includes:

- **Configuration summary** — units, model, monitoring tier, contract term
- **Monthly recurring cost** — broken out by line item
- **One-time costs** — mobilization, custom configuration, training (if applicable)
- **Contract term and options** — month-to-month, multi-year, lease alternatives where applicable
- **Service level summary** — SOC response, support hours, replacement policy
- **Compliance attestations** — NDAA, AWS, encryption standards
- **Sample MSA section references** — for procurement teams who want to review terms before signing

Quotes are sent in PDF and editable formats for procurement processes that need to extract data.

## If you need a quote faster

Standard turnaround is 2 business days. Faster turnaround is available if you have an active emergency, an immediate-deployment timeline, or a procurement deadline. Note the urgency in the open-text field and we will prioritize. Same-day quotes happen, especially for direct-deployable single-site needs.

## If your situation is complex

Some deployments require a discovery call before we can quote accurately:

- Multi-site enterprise rollouts with bespoke integration requirements
- Federal contracts with specific clause requirements
- White-label or strategic partner configurations
- Custom hardware modifications

If your situation fits one of these, indicate it in step 1 and we will route you to the right team. The discovery call is free and typically takes 30 minutes.

## What we will not do

- We will not put you in a 30-day nurture sequence after a quote request
- We will not call your office five times in a week
- We will not pass your contact information to a third party
- We will not share pricing on competitors with you (we sell our product, not theirs)

faq.q: Do I need to talk to a sales rep before getting pricing?
faq.a: No. The quote is delivered by email. A call is offered, not required.

faq.q: Can I get standard product pricing without filling out the form?
faq.a: Yes. See the pricing page for current published MSRP on the three standard product lines.

faq.q: How accurate is the initial quote?
faq.a: For standard product, single-site or small-fleet deployments, the quote is final. For complex enterprise rollouts, the initial quote is a planning estimate; final pricing comes after the engineering scoping call.

faq.q: What if I am still evaluating and not ready to buy?

seoTitle: Schedule a Demo | VDS Mobile Security Platform
metaDescription: Book a 30-minute platform-led demo of the VDS VMS, SOC workflow, and mobile unit hardware. Live data, live operators, no slideware. Calendly booking
h1: 30 minutes. Live platform. Live SOC.
heroSubhead: We do not run slideware demos. You see the actual VMS with live data, watch an actual SOC operator workflow on a recorded event, and review the hardware up close. Book a slot below.
body:
## What the demo is

A 30-minute video call with a VDS sales engineer and, when relevant, a SOC supervisor or product manager. The agenda:

- **Minutes 0–5:** Your situation. What you are deploying, what you are evaluating against, what the timeline looks like.
- **Minutes 5–15:** Live VMS walkthrough. We log into a live demonstration tenant with anonymized real data. You see camera feeds, alerts, audit logs, RBAC, and reporting in their working state.
- **Minutes 15–22:** SOC workflow. We play through a recorded P1 incident — alert generation, AI pre-filter, operator triage, talk-down, dispatch — exactly as it ran with a real operator on a real customer event.
- **Minutes 22–28:** Hardware review. Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, Boundary Guard Pro shown on camera with deployment specs and field photos. We answer questions on solar autonomy, battery life, NDAA, and integration.
- **Minutes 28–30:** Next steps. Quote, technical scoping call, RFP response, or "we will follow up in 90 days" — whichever fits.

You will not see a slide deck unless you specifically ask. You will not be asked qualifying questions you already answered when booking.

## Booking

[PLACEHOLDER — Calendly embed for VDS demo booking]

The calendar above shows live availability for VDS sales engineers. Select a slot that works for your schedule. Most days have multiple openings; if nothing fits in the visible window, contact sales directly to find a custom time.

Bookings include automatic calendar invitation with a video call link, a 15-minute pre-demo questionnaire (optional), and a reminder 24 hours before the call.

## Who comes on the demo from your side

- **Decision-makers and influencers welcome.** Security director, operations VP, IT, finance, procurement — bring the team if relevant.
- **Technical buyers welcome.** Bring your IT or security architecture lead and we will go deep on the platform. Engineering joins the call by default if you flag "technical depth" in the booking notes.
- **Procurement and compliance welcome.** We will hand off to Trust Center documentation in real time if it is a compliance-led evaluation.

If you want a custom configuration on the demo — for example, integrating one of your existing camera streams into a sample tenant — flag this in the booking notes at least 24 hours in advance. We will set up the demo environment to match.

## What to have ready

Nothing required. Most useful, if you have them:

- A general sense of deployment count and timeline
- Your current site security cost baseline (guard hours, prior losses)
- Any specific compliance or technical requirements (NDAA, SSO, SIEM integration)

If you do not have these yet, the demo will help you scope them.

## After the demo

You will get an email within 1 business day with:

- Recording of the demo (if you opted in during the call)
- Documentation referenced during the call (Trust Center, NDAA, case studies)
- Next-step recommendation — quote, scoping call, RFP response, or "no follow-up needed"

We do not start a multi-touch nurture sequence after the demo. If you do not want follow-up, say so on the call. We track that flag and respect it.

## If the demo time slips

We get it. Reschedule from the original calendar invitation, or email sales directly. We will rebook within 48 hours.

## If the standard demo is not what you need

For executive briefings, RFP scoping sessions, technical deep-dives, or proof-of-concept discussions, contact sales directly and we will set up a longer-format session. Standard demo is 30 minutes; custom formats run 60–90 minutes with a specialized agenda.

faq.q: Is the demo really live, or is it a recorded walk-through?
faq.a: Live. We log into a working VMS tenant. The SOC workflow segment uses a recorded incident only because we cannot stage a live P1 event for demo purposes.

faq.q: Can I bring a team of 6 to the demo?
faq.a: Yes. The video call supports it. Larger groups (10+) should mention the audience in booking notes so we can format the session accordingly.

faq.q: Do you ever do on-site demos with actual hardware?
faq.a: Yes, for active enterprise opportunities and dealer prospects, we will travel to a customer site or have you visit Pikesville. This is a separate format from the standard demo; ask sales after the first call.

faq.q: Is the demo recorded?
faq.a: Only if you opt in at the start of the call. The recording is for your team's reference, not for our marketing.

faq.q: What if I just want to see the VMS without sitting through the rest?
faq.a: The VMS-only segment is the longest part of the standard demo. If you want to skip the SOC and hardware portions, say so in booking notes and we will adjust the agenda.

finalCTAHeading: 30 minutes of live platform. Pick a slot.
finalCTABody: Book through the calendar. If your situation needs a longer or custom format, contact sales directly.

metaDescription: Six services under one roof — rapid deployment, 24/7 US SOC monitoring, install, integration, managed security, and consulting

h1: Six services. One accountable team. Zero finger-pointing.
heroSubhead: Hardware, software, and a 24/7 US Security Operations Center built and operated by the same company. When something goes wrong on your site, one number gets you to the engineer who deployed the trailer and the operator watching the feed.
body:
Most security vendors sell one piece of the stack. You end up coordinating a hardware integrator, a monitoring center in another country, a VMS license, and a service contractor — four contracts, four invoices, four people pointing at each other when a camera goes dark at 2 a.m.

VDS does all of it. Hardware engineered and assembled in Pikesville, Maryland. A camera-agnostic VMS that integrates with the cameras you already own over ONVIF/RTSP. A US Security Operations Center staffed by people we trained, on payroll, sitting in a room we own. Site survey, install, maintenance, redeployment, and consulting — same team, same accountability.

## The six services

**Rapid Deployment** — Solar-autonomous mobile units on site within 72 hours of approval. No trenching, no permits, no utility coordination. One person stages a trailer in under 20 minutes. Used for active construction sites, lay-down yards, port terminals, utility substations, disaster response, and any location that needs a perimeter live before the power company shows up.

**24/7 Remote Monitoring** — In-house US SOC. AI flags an event, a trained operator verifies it within 60 seconds, talks the subject down over two-way audio, dispatches law enforcement with live video on the way, and writes a full incident report before clocking out. 97% false alarm reduction measured across the deployed fleet.

**Installation & Maintenance** — Licensed field technicians for permanent install, mast-mount, fixed-camera retrofits, and ongoing servicing. Quarterly preventive maintenance, firmware updates, lens cleanings, and redeployment when a site changes phase. We service what we sell and what you already own.

**System Integration** — VDS VMS speaks ONVIF, RTSP, and a published REST API. We integrate with access control (Genetec, Lenel, Avigilon, AMAG), alarm panels, ITSM platforms (ServiceNow, Jira), and ERP systems (SAP, Oracle). If you already have 200 cameras, we add the analytics layer and the monitoring service — no rip-and-replace.

**Managed Security Services** — Turnkey monthly contract: hardware, monitoring, maintenance, reporting, and replacement. One invoice, one SLA, one number to call. Most clients move from a $32,400/month guard contract to a $4,000/month managed service and keep more coverage.

## The case to study before you pick a vendor

A $28M Mid-Atlantic construction project replaced a guard service with VDS Managed Security. Twelve months later: $340,800 saved against the prior security budget, 73% reduction in theft incidents, zero insurance claims filed, monthly cost down from $32,400 to $4,000. Full incident logs, dispatch records, and ROI math available under NDA.

## Why one roof matters

When your perimeter is a single contract, the failure modes shrink. A camera goes offline and our SOC sees it before you do — and dispatches our field tech, not yours. An alarm trips at 3 a.m. and the operator already knows the site layout because our deployment engineer built the camera plan. A new phase opens on the construction project and the same crew redeploys the trailers — they don't bill discovery time.

That's the operating model. Pick the service that fits, or stack them.

faq.q: Do I have to buy all six services?
faq.a: No. Most clients start with Rapid Deployment plus 24/7 Monitoring and add integration or managed services as scope grows. Standalone SOC monitoring on cameras you already own is available — pricing is per camera, per month.

faq.q: Are your services available outside the 30 states where you're already deployed?
faq.a: Yes. Active deployments cover 30+ states; the trailer model and SOC operate nationwide. Service-level response times in non-deployed states depend on field tech coverage — we'll quote it during the site assessment.

faq.q: How fast can you get someone on a site?
faq.a: Site assessment within 48 hours of inquiry for most US locations. Trailer on the ground within 72 hours of contract signature. Permanent installs scope on a project-by-project basis.

faq.q: Is VDS NDAA Section 889 compliant?
faq.a: Yes. No banned components in any deployed unit. Compliance documentation is included with every quote and shipped with every trailer for federal, DoD, and critical-infrastructure procurement reviews.

faq.q: Who owns the footage and incident data?
faq.a: You do. VDS retains operational copies for SOC reference and contracted retention windows. Customer data is stored in AWS GovCloud or commercial AWS depending on contract — your choice.

finalCTAHeading: Start with a site assessment.
finalCTABody: 30-minute call with a deployment engineer. We map the perimeter, identify gaps, and price the right combination of services. No deck-only sales reps.

h1: Solutions: Cost Analysis and Decision Frameworks for Mobile Surveillance
heroSubhead: Six pages that answer the questions every security director asks before procurement: what does it cost, should we rent or buy, and what replaces a guard line item. Numbers, not narrative.
body:
At VDS, "solutions" is not a euphemism for product. It is a library of cost and decision pages built for people who are 30 days or less from buying mobile surveillance.

We sell three things together — solar-autonomous trailers, a camera-agnostic cloud VMS, and a 24/7 US-based Security Operations Center — and the procurement questions are predictable. How much does a trailer cost per month. How does $399/site/mo for SOC monitoring compare to $60K-$110K per FTE for a guard. Should we lease for opex or buy for capex. What does the break-even look like at month 24.

These pages exist because most security vendors won't publish numbers. We will.

## What you'll find here

**Cost pages** — full pricing for each line item, including what's included in the rate, what costs extra, and how to model annual TCO. We publish our own numbers ($1,500-$2,200/mo for trailers, $39-$69/cam/mo for platform, $399/site/mo for SOC) and benchmark against industry rentals ($1,200-$3,400/mo).

**Decision pages** — frameworks for the three buy-side decisions that drive 80% of our discovery calls: remote monitoring vs guards, rent vs buy, and which trailer config matches the site.

**Case studies** — full deployments with measured outcomes. The hero case ($28M Mid-Atlantic GC) cut security spend from $32,400/mo to $4,000/mo, reduced theft 73%, and filed zero insurance claims over 12 months. That's $340,800 saved in year one on a single project.

## The six pages

1. [Mobile Surveillance Trailer Cost](/solutions/mobile-surveillance-trailer-cost) — purchase ($30K-$60K) and rental ($1,200-$3,400/mo) ranges, what's included, annual TCO model.
2. [Remote Video Monitoring Cost](/solutions/remote-video-monitoring-cost) — per-site, per-camera, and per-hour pricing for managed SOC services.
3. [MSU Rental Cost](/solutions/mobile-surveillance-trailer-rental-cost) — short-term vs long-term rental economics, deposit, lead time, redeployment fees.
4. [Remote Monitoring vs Security Guards](/solutions/remote-monitoring-vs-security-guards) — side-by-side cost ($4,800/year vs $60K-$110K/FTE), coverage, evidence, and response-time matrices.
5. [Buy vs Rent Mobile Surveillance Trailer](/solutions/buy-vs-rent-mobile-surveillance-trailer) — break-even math (purchase ~ 24 months of rental at typical configs) and the decision tree.
6. [Case Study Examples](/solutions/case-study-example) — measured outcomes across construction, retail, logistics, and utility deployments.

## Who these pages are for

Construction security directors costing a new project. Retail loss prevention leaders trying to defend a budget request. Logistics ops managers replacing guards at a yard. Utility and municipal procurement officers comparing trailer rentals to a capex purchase.

If you are comparing vendors, the pricing tables here are accurate as of this quarter and updated against published competitor rates. If you are building an internal business case, the TCO models and break-even calculators are the same ones we use on discovery calls.

If you are not 30 days from a decision, our resources library has technical specs, deployment guides, and the full case studies cited above. Start there.

## Why we publish numbers

Two reasons. First: the security industry runs on "request a quote" friction because most vendors are uncompetitive on price and don't want to show it. We are competitive and our rates are public. Second: a buyer who shows up to a discovery call already knowing the math closes 4x faster. We optimize for that buyer.

faq.q: Is pricing on these pages current?
faq.a: Yes. Rates are reviewed quarterly. Configurations beyond the standard SKUs (Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy Trailer, Boundary Guard Pro) are quoted on a per-site basis.

faq.q: Do you publish these numbers because you're cheap or because you're confident?
faq.a: Confident. Our SOC operators, NDAA-compliant hardware, and integrated VMS are priced against the full-stack alternative (separate hardware vendor + separate VMS + separate monitoring service), not against the cheapest trailer on Craigslist.

faq.q: Can I get a custom TCO model for my site?
faq.a: Yes. Send camera count, site duration, and coverage hours and we'll return a 12- and 36-month TCO with rent and buy scenarios.

faq.q: How current is the case study data?
faq.a: All published outcomes are from deployments within the last 36 months. The Mid-Atlantic GC numbers are independently verified by the customer's risk team.

finalCTAHeading: Bring numbers to your next procurement meeting
finalCTABody: Send your site details. We'll return a quote, a TCO model, and a recommended configuration in 48 hours.

h1: We hire people who build things and answer the phone.
heroSubhead: VDS is a hardware company with a 24/7 monitoring operation. The work is hands-on, the customers are real, and the chain of command is short. Open roles are listed below. Speculative resumes welcome.
body:
## What it is like to work here

VDS is small enough that you will meet the founders in your first week and large enough that you will not be doing three jobs at once. Headcount is in the 25–50 range. Decisions get made fast. Customer problems get answered fast. The work is operational, not theoretical.

Engineering ships firmware to units in the field — the kind that get vandalized, baked in 105°F sun, and rained on. Operations runs a 24/7 SOC with measurable response time targets. Sales talks to GCs, facility managers, and dealers who will tell you in plain language whether the product solves their problem. Manufacturing assembles units in Pikesville and inspects every chassis before it ships.

What we hire for, in order:
1. Will the person do the work
2. Can the person be trusted with a customer relationship
3. Does the person have the specific skills the role requires

That order is intentional.

## Compensation and benefits

- Competitive base salary, calibrated to role and experience
- Health, dental, and vision insurance (employer-contributing)
- 401(k) with company match after 6 months
- Paid time off, paid holidays, and paid parental leave
- Tools, equipment, and certifications relevant to the role, fully reimbursed
- Continuing education stipend for technical certifications

## Open roles {#open-roles}

### Hardware Assembly Technician
**Location:** Pikesville, MD (on-site)
**Type:** Full-time

Build, test, and inspect VDS mobile surveillance units on the Pikesville assembly line. Solar arrays, battery banks, camera modules, control electronics, cellular uplinks, and chassis. Read a wiring diagram, follow a build sequence, use a torque wrench, document a build sheet.

**What we need:**
- 2+ years assembly, electromechanical, or electrical work
- Comfortable with hand tools, basic soldering, and 12V/24V DC wiring
- Able to read schematics and follow written build procedures
- Detail-oriented; documents and labels work as it goes
- Lift 50 lbs, work in a shop environment with PPE

**What is nice to have:**
- Background in solar installation, RV/marine electrical, or fleet vehicle build-out
- Familiarity with low-voltage IP camera systems

**To apply:** Email resume to careers@visiondetectionsystems.com with subject "Hardware Assembly Technician."

### Administrative Coordinator
**Location:** Pikesville, MD (on-site)
**Type:** Full-time

Keep the operations side of VDS running. Customer billing coordination, vendor invoice processing, shipping coordination with the SOC and dealer channel, executive scheduling support, office logistics. This is the role where, if you do it well, the entire company runs better.

**What we need:**
- 3+ years administrative or operations coordination experience
- Excellent written communication and follow-through
- Comfortable with QuickBooks, Google Workspace, and a ticketing system (we use HubSpot)
- Ability to keep confidential information confidential
- Self-directed; you will not be micromanaged

**What is nice to have:**
- Background in B2B services, security industry, construction services, or fleet operations
- Notary commission

**To apply:** Email resume to careers@visiondetectionsystems.com with subject "Administrative Coordinator."

### Other roles — speculative resumes welcome

We hire continuously across:

- **Security Operations Center operators** — 24/7 shifts, US-staffed only, paid training
- **Firmware and embedded engineering** — Linux on edge devices, C/C++, low-power systems
- **Cloud platform engineering** — AWS, React, Node.js, video pipelines at scale
- **Field service technicians** — regional, US-based, drive a service truck, fix what is in the field
- **Account executives and dealer channel managers** — security industry experience preferred
- **Customer success managers** — own enterprise renewals and expansion

If your background fits one of these and there is no posted role, send a resume with the area of interest in the subject line. We respond within 5 business days.

## How hiring works

1. Resume submission via email
2. 30-minute phone screen with the hiring manager
3. 45–60 minute role-specific interview (technical, operational, or scenario-based)
4. On-site visit to Pikesville for final-round candidates (travel reimbursed for out-of-area candidates)
5. Reference check and offer

We do not run multi-day interview loops. We do not give homework assignments longer than 2 hours. We give a decision within one week of the final interview.

- We do not negotiate compensation through agencies on roles we did not retain them for
- We do not accept resumes for roles where you did not personally submit
- We do not require non-compete agreements as a condition of employment

h1: Close the three gaps in site security.
heroSubhead: Most sites are protected by a fence, a sign, and a hope. We build the layer between those and the actual response.
heroStats: Founded 2017 · 500+ deployments · 30+ states · 7 years of field data
body:
## Why VDS exists

In 2017, the founders walked job sites where the security plan was a guard in a folding chair, a camera nobody was watching, and a sign that said "Premises Under Surveillance." When something happened — copper theft, equipment vandalism, an after-hours break-in — the response time averaged 18 to 40 minutes. By then the trailer was empty.

That gap between "we have cameras" and "someone is actually doing something about this right now" is the problem we set out to fix.

## The three gaps

We started VDS because site security in the field has three structural failures, and most vendors only address one.

**1. Cost.** Permanent fiber-trenched, hardwired surveillance costs $40K–$120K per acre and takes weeks to install. For a 90-day construction project or a seasonal yard, that math never works. Sites stay uncovered, and losses get written into the budget as "shrinkage."

**2. Blind spots.** Fixed cameras see a fence line. They do not see the lot, the staging area, the back row of equipment, or the access road. Guards see one quadrant at a time. Most sites are 60–80% un-monitored at any given moment.

**3. Response time.** Even when something is captured on camera, the average time from event to dispatched response is 18+ minutes industry-wide. Footage is great for insurance. It is not security.

## What we built

VDS is built as a manufacturer, not a reseller. We assemble our hardware in Pikesville, MD — Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, Boundary Guard Pro, solar camera poles, guard booths, cooling stations, light trailers. We run the cloud VMS (AI VisionStream) on AWS. We staff our own 24/7 SOC in the US.

That stack matters because the three gaps are connected. You cannot fix response time if your camera vendor, your cloud vendor, and your monitoring vendor are three different companies pointing at each other. You cannot guarantee NDAA compliance if you are reselling whatever the distributor had in stock. You cannot keep pricing predictable if every layer is marked up by someone else.

So we own the layers. One number to call. One company accountable for the outcome.

## What "integrated mobile security infrastructure" actually means

It means the camera, the power source, the chassis, the network, the VMS, and the human watching the screen at 3 AM all answer to the same company. It means a Sky Guard MSU deployed in Arizona and one deployed in Maine pull data into the same platform, get monitored by the same SOC, and run on the same audit log. It means when a customer asks "who is watching this site right now," the answer is a name, not a vendor chain.

## The commitments

These are the things we do not compromise on, regardless of price pressure or growth pressure.

- **Manufacturer, not reseller.** We assemble. We integrate. We program. We own the warranty.
- **Genuine NDAA Section 889.** Every camera, every component — not "NDAA-compatible" marketing language.
- **In-house US SOC.** Not contracted offshore. <60s escalation, 97% false alarm reduction.
- **Your data is yours.** US-only data residency, TLS 1.3 / AES-256, 12-month audit log, no third-party data sale, ever.
- **Camera-agnostic platform.** If a customer has existing cameras that meet our compliance baseline, they integrate. We do not lock customers into our hardware.

## Where we are going

7 years of field data tells us where the next gaps are: edge AI for specific threat classes, faster deploy times, lower watts-per-channel, and tighter integration with the responders who actually show up. That is the roadmap. The mission has not changed: close the three gaps, and be the company you can actually call.

faq.q: Is VDS a security guard company?
faq.a: No. We build the mobile security infrastructure — hardware, cloud VMS, and 24/7 SOC monitoring — that makes guard services either unnecessary or far more effective. Our SOC handles detection and escalation; on-site response is dispatched through your existing guard provider or local law enforcement.

faq.q: Why does manufacturing in the US matter for security?
faq.a: NDAA Section 889 compliance is only meaningful if you can trace components. When you assemble in-house, you control the bill of materials, the firmware, and the supply chain. Resellers cannot make that guarantee — they ship what their distributors ship.

faq.q: How is VDS different from a camera vendor or a VMS vendor?
faq.a: Camera vendors sell you cameras. VMS vendors sell you software. Guard companies sell you hours. We are the only company that owns all three layers — and that's the only way to fix response time end-to-end.

faq.q: Where are you headquartered?
faq.a: Pikesville, Maryland. Founded 2017. All hardware is assembled here. The SOC is staffed in the US.

VDS hardware and AI VisionStream are fully NDAA Section 889 compliant. Written compliance documentation available for all federal, state, and regulated procurement programs.

## What Is NDAA Section 889?

The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) Section 889 was enacted as part of the 2019 National Defense Authorization Act to address national security concerns regarding telecommunications and video surveillance equipment. Section 889 prohibits federal agencies from procuring or using equipment and services from companies that utilize covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment from five specific manufacturers: Huawei Technologies, ZTE Corporation, Hytera Communications, Hangzhou Hikvision, and Dahua Technology.

The law contains two critical parts: Part A prevents federal agencies from directly purchasing equipment from these restricted manufacturers, while Part B extends the prohibition to federal contractors, preventing them from using this equipment anywhere in their operations. Part B became effective August 13, 2020, and applies to any organization seeking federal contracts or grants.

Beyond federal procurement, NDAA Section 889 compliance requirements have extended to state and local government agencies receiving federal funding, creating widespread impact across public sector surveillance and security programs. Many regulated industries now require NDAA compliance as a standard procurement criterion.

## Who NDAA Section 889 Affects

NDAA Section 889 compliance requirements extend across multiple sectors and procurement programs:

  • Federal Agencies — All executive departments including DOD, DHS, GSA, and their procurement programs must verify contractor compliance before award
  • State and Local Government — Agencies receiving federal funding through grants, cooperative agreements, or federal program participation must demonstrate compliance
  • Federal Contractors and Subcontractors — Any organization bidding on federal contracts must certify that they do not use restricted equipment in their operations
  • Critical Infrastructure Operators — Power, water, transportation, and communication networks often require NDAA compliance for security system procurements
  • Public Safety Agencies — Law enforcement, emergency management, and public safety organizations receiving federal grants must meet compliance standards
  • Regulated Procurement Programs — GSA schedule, cooperative purchasing agreements, and state contract vehicles increasingly require NDAA compliance certification
## Risks of Non-Compliance

Organizations that fail to meet NDAA Section 889 requirements face significant procurement and operational consequences. Contract disqualification represents the most immediate risk — procurement teams cannot award contracts to vendors who cannot certify compliance, regardless of technical capabilities or pricing advantages.

Federal contractors face suspension or debarment from all federal contracting opportunities if found using restricted equipment. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) requires contractors to remove any covered equipment from their systems, creating costly operational disruption and potential security gaps during transition periods.

Criminal penalties apply to organizations that provide false certifications regarding their compliance status. Procurement audits increasingly require component-level documentation to verify compliance claims, making inadequate due diligence a significant legal and business risk.

Beyond regulatory consequences, non-compliant security systems may require complete replacement if discovered during contract performance, creating budget overruns and coverage gaps that expose facilities to security incidents during system transitions.

## How VDS Meets NDAA Section 889 ### Hardware Supply Chain

VDS maintains a fully audited hardware supply chain free from all Section 889-restricted manufacturers. Our mobile surveillance trailers, solar camera poles, and fixed surveillance units contain no components from Huawei, ZTE, Hikvision, Dahua, or Hytera. Written attestation letters documenting supply chain compliance are available on request for all procurement programs.

Camera sensors, video processors, cellular modems, and connectivity modules are sourced exclusively from compliant suppliers with documented component traceability. All surveillance hardware is assembled in our Maryland facility under controlled manufacturing processes that maintain compliance integrity throughout production and deployment.

### AI VisionStream Software Platform

The AI VisionStream platform operates on Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure with no restricted software manufacturers in the technology stack. Video analytics, cloud storage, user management, and API integrations utilize only compliant software libraries and services. AWS GovCloud deployment options are available for highest-classification government installations requiring additional security controls.

All software development, cloud hosting, and data processing occurs within compliant infrastructure, ensuring that video data, AI processing, and user access management meet Section 889 requirements from capture through evidence export.

### Documentation Package

VDS procurement support includes comprehensive compliance documentation for federal, state, and regulated purchasing programs. Our documentation package provides written NDAA Section 889 compliance attestation letters signed by executive management, component-level supply chain documentation upon request, and direct procurement support for GSA schedule, cooperative purchasing, and state contract vehicle processes.

Direct manufacturer relationships eliminate third-party channel partner compliance complexity, providing procurement teams with clear accountability and documentation trails. Most compliance packages are delivered within 48 hours of request, supporting tight procurement timelines and proposal deadlines.

## Product Coverage

All VDS products and services meet NDAA Section 889 compliance requirements:

Compliance extends across all service offerings including remote video monitoring, deployment logistics, video retrieval support, and technical assistance. Our Security Operations Center (SOC) utilizes only compliant hardware and software for incident verification and escalation processes.

## Federal and State Procurement Programs

VDS actively participates in federal and state procurement programs with full NDAA compliance documentation. Our GSA schedule participation provides federal agencies with pre-vetted pricing and compliance verification, streamlining procurement processes for mobile surveillance trailers and monitoring services.

State contract vehicles and cooperative purchasing agreements receive the same compliance documentation and pricing transparency, enabling state and local agencies to leverage federal-level procurement efficiency while meeting their own compliance requirements. Procurement teams receive dedicated support for compliance questions, technical specifications, and program requirements throughout the evaluation and award process.

Most procurement inquiries receive comprehensive compliance packages and technical proposals within 48 hours, supporting aggressive procurement timelines and budget cycles. Direct manufacturer engagement eliminates reseller markups and compliance uncertainties common in security system procurements.

## Ongoing Compliance Monitoring

VDS maintains continuous monitoring of supply chain compliance through quarterly supplier audits and component traceability reviews. Supply chain changes undergo compliance verification before implementation, ensuring that hardware updates, software releases, and service modifications maintain Section 889 compliance throughout product lifecycles.

Regulatory updates and guidance changes are tracked through federal procurement channels, with compliance documentation updated to reflect current requirements. This proactive approach ensures that existing deployments and new installations continue meeting compliance standards as regulations evolve.

Client compliance support extends beyond initial procurement to include compliance verification for contract renewals, system expansions, and regulatory audits. Written compliance confirmations are available throughout service relationships to support ongoing procurement and compliance requirements.

## NDAA Compliance FAQ ### What is NDAA Section 889?

NDAA Section 889 is federal legislation that prohibits government agencies and federal contractors from using telecommunications and video surveillance equipment from five specific manufacturers: Huawei, ZTE, Hikvision, Dahua, and Hytera. The law applies to federal agencies directly and extends to contractors, subcontractors, and organizations receiving federal funding.

### Which surveillance camera brands are banned under NDAA Section 889?

Section 889 specifically restricts equipment from Hangzhou Hikvision Digital Technology and Dahua Technology Company, along with telecommunications equipment from Huawei Technologies, ZTE Corporation, and Hytera Communications Corporation. The restriction applies to equipment manufactured by these companies or containing their components.

### Does NDAA compliance apply to state and local government?

Yes, NDAA Section 889 applies to state and local government agencies that receive federal funding through grants, cooperative agreements, or federal program participation. Many state procurement programs now require NDAA compliance regardless of federal funding to maintain consistent security standards across government operations.

### How do I verify that security equipment is NDAA compliant?

Request written compliance attestation letters from manufacturers documenting that their hardware and software contain no components from restricted manufacturers. Verify that suppliers can provide component-level documentation and maintain compliant supply chains. Work directly with manufacturers rather than resellers to ensure compliance accountability.

### Can VDS provide written NDAA compliance documentation for procurement?

Yes, VDS provides comprehensive NDAA Section 889 compliance documentation including signed attestation letters, component-level supply chain documentation, and procurement support for federal, state, and cooperative purchasing programs. Most compliance packages are delivered within 48 hours of request.

## Procurement Support and Documentation

For procurement teams requiring NDAA compliance verification and documentation, VDS provides direct manufacturer support throughout the evaluation and procurement process. Our compliance team works with federal agencies, state governments, and regulated organizations to provide comprehensive documentation packages that meet specific procurement requirements and timelines.

Most compliance packages are delivered within 48 hours of initial contact, including written attestation letters, technical specifications, and procurement guidance. Contact VDS for NDAA compliance documentation and procurement support.

heroStats: Pikesville, MD · Assembled in USA · NDAA 889 traceable · Same-facility service parts
body:
## Why a plant page

Most security companies do not have a plant. They have a warehouse, a procurement team, and a label-maker. When something fails, the answer is a ticket to a distributor and a four-week lead time on a part that came from someone else's container.

We are not that. This page exists because the difference matters — for compliance, for service, and for the customers who ask, fairly, "where does this come from?"

## What happens at the Pikesville facility

The plant covers chassis integration, electrical assembly, mast and solar mounting, programming and firmware loading, and final QC. Every unit that ships to a customer was on the floor here first.

**Chassis and frame integration.** Trailer chassis arrive from US suppliers. VDS technicians complete the structural integration — mast mounts, equipment bay framing, weatherproofing, and finish work.

**Solar and power systems.** Solar panels are sourced from named NDAA-compliant vendors. Battery banks, charge controllers, and DC distribution are wired and tested on-bench before installation in the unit. Each system is load-tested for the duty cycle it will see in the field.

**Camera and sensor integration.** Cameras (from named NDAA-compliant manufacturers — full list available on request) are mounted, aligned, and weather-sealed. Thermal sensors, radar where specified, and audio deterrents are integrated and bench-tested.

**Programming and platform provisioning.** Each unit is provisioned onto AI VisionStream at the plant. Site templates, alarm zones, and SOC rule sets are pre-loaded. Cellular modems are activated and connectivity verified before shipment.

**Quality control and inspection.** Every unit passes a multi-point inspection: structural, electrical, optical alignment, network handshake to AWS, SOC visibility test, and 72-hour burn-in for solar-power-cycle stability. Inspection records are tied to the unit serial number and retained for the life of the asset.

## In-house vs. sourced

We are honest about what we make and what we buy. The line matters for traceability.

**Done at VDS:** chassis integration, mast assemblies, electrical and DC systems, weatherproofing, programming and firmware, camera mounting and alignment, platform provisioning, QC and burn-in, packaging and shipping.

**Sourced from named vendors:** raw trailer chassis (US suppliers), solar panels (NDAA-compliant US/allied vendors), cameras (named NDAA-compliant manufacturers), batteries (US/allied), cellular modems (US carriers, NDAA-compliant hardware). Vendor list is documented per unit and available to compliance-sensitive customers under NDA.

## Why this matters

**NDAA Section 889 traceability.** Compliance is not a sticker. It is a bill of materials you can defend in front of a federal contracting officer. Because we control assembly, we control the BOM — and we can produce documentation per unit, per serial number, on request.

**Faster service parts.** A camera or power module that fails in Texas does not wait on a container from overseas. Replacements ship from Pikesville, typically same-day or next-day for service-contracted accounts. The same techs who built the unit support it in the field.

**US jobs.** The plant employs technicians, electricians, programmers, and QC inspectors locally. Every unit that ships funds those roles. We are not abstract about this — manufacturing in Maryland is a deliberate choice, and it costs more than offshore assembly. The trade is worth it.

**Iteration speed.** Field feedback loops back into the next production run. When the SOC notices a pattern — a camera angle that creates false alarms, a power profile that fails in shoulder-season cold — engineering changes the next build. Resellers cannot do this. Manufacturers can.

## Visiting the plant

Customers and prospects are welcome to tour the facility. We schedule tours weekly. You will see the floor, meet the team, and watch a unit go through QC. Federal and utility customers conducting compliance audits get a structured walkthrough with documentation.

## Working at the plant

We hire technicians, electricians, network engineers, programmers, and QC inspectors. If you build things with your hands and care that they work in -20F at 3 AM, the roles are open.

faq.a: Pikesville, Maryland — the same campus as VDS headquarters. Address is shared after a tour or interview is scheduled.

faq.a: Yes. Every serial number maps to a bill of materials, an inspection record, and a vendor compliance statement. Documentation is provided with shipment and re-issued on request.

faq.a: Yes, within the platform. Custom mast heights, sensor packages, paint, and branding are common. Full custom chassis work is evaluated case-by-case — talk to engineering.

faq.a: SOC sees the failure in real time. Service parts ship from Pikesville. For service-contracted units, hardware replacement is typically 24-hour turnaround in CONUS; software and connectivity issues are typically resolved in under 2 hours.
