## What white label means at VDS

White labeling at VDS is not a sticker on a chassis. It is a manufacturing and operations integration that lets a high-volume partner sell VDS technology under their own brand without exposing VDS as the upstream provider — while still benefiting from VDS engineering, VMS, and SOC operations.

**On the hardware side:** Chassis paint, vinyl wrap, and weatherproof badging in your colors and logo. Custom signage and contact information. Optional custom mounting hardware for specific use cases. We do not white-label internal components; the engineering remains standard VDS and remains under our warranty and support.

**On the software side:** VMS branding (logo, color palette, customer-facing labels, mobile app icon). Custom domain (yourcompany.cloud.example) with SSL. Optional custom user invitation emails and customer notifications under your brand.

**On the operations side:** Custom SOC operator script that addresses your customer in your brand voice, custom call-out language during talk-down events, custom escalation procedures aligned to your customer agreements.

**On the contract side:** Your customer signs a contract with you, not with VDS. VDS is the unnamed subcontractor under your master agreement.

## What does not get white-labeled

- **Underlying engineering documentation.** Component data sheets, certifications, NDAA attestations remain VDS-branded. Customers who ask for this documentation see VDS authorship.
- **SOC 2 and security audit reports.** These are issued to VDS as the underlying processor.
- **AWS hosting.** The platform is on AWS under VDS's account. Custom AWS account hosting is available at the strategic-partner level with separate pricing.
- **Regulatory compliance attestations.** NDAA, FCC, and other regulatory documents reference VDS as the manufacturer of record.

For customers who ask "who actually makes this," your sales staff will be trained on the standard disclosure language. We do not require you to lie about the upstream relationship; the program is about brand presentation, not concealment.

## Who this is for

The white-label program is built for:

- **National security integrators** deploying mobile units across multiple regions
- **Modular construction and trailer rental firms** integrating surveillance into a broader rental offering
- **Specialty service firms** in energy, infrastructure, or events with established brand equity
- **Private label resellers** with existing customer relationships in our target verticals

Minimum annual volume: 100 units. Below that, the standard dealer program with co-branding options is the better fit.

## Commercial structure

- **Custom unit pricing** tied to annual volume commitment, separate from standard dealer pricing
- **Custom MRR share** on monitoring services
- **Tooling and setup fees** for one-time chassis customization, VMS branding setup, and SOC script development — typically amortized over the volume commitment
- **Annual minimum** committed in writing; below-commitment performance triggers pricing review at renewal

Specific pricing is negotiated. Expect the conversation to involve volume forecasts, geography, customer profile, and your existing operations.

## Onboarding timeline

White-label onboarding takes 60–90 days from contract signature, depending on customization scope:

- **Days 1–14:** Brand asset collection, design review, VMS customization spec
- **Days 15–30:** Chassis design proof, VMS staging environment setup
- **Days 31–60:** First production units, SOC operator script development and certification
- **Days 61–90:** First customer deployment under your brand

- A real brand and a real customer base — this is not a vehicle for arbitrage or quick reselling
- A capable sales and support organization that can stand behind a customer-facing brand
- Adherence to VDS quality and operational standards in customer communications

metaDescription: Intrusion zones, virtual tripwires, loitering, crowd, and time-of-day rules running on 7 years of field-tuned models. Sub-3-second alerts.
h1: Rules you draw. Alerts that fire in under 3 seconds.
heroSubhead: Draw a polygon. Set a schedule. Get a verified alert when a human, vehicle, or object crosses the line. Models trained on 7 years of field footage from 500+ active sites.
body:
## Five rule types that cover 95% of real-world security events

Most "AI detection" pages list 40 features and ship 4. We ship 5 rule types because those 5 catch the events that actually drive incident reports.

### Intrusion zones
Draw a polygon on the camera view. Set who is allowed in it (no one, vehicles only, people only) and when. Alert fires when the rule is broken. Sensitivity is per-zone, not global.

### Virtual tripwires
A directional line across an entry point, fence gap, or loading bay. Alert fires only when crossed in the direction you specify. Bi-directional is also supported.

### Loitering
Tag a zone with a dwell threshold (e.g., person stationary for 90 seconds). Catches casing behavior at ATMs, parking structures, and dealership lots without firing on every customer who walks through.

### Crowd thresholds
Alert when more than N people enter a zone within a window. Used for retail flash-rob detection, protest perimeter awareness, and occupancy compliance.

### Time-of-day rules
Every rule above can be scheduled. A loading dock that is legitimate from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. and an intrusion target from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. is a single camera with two rule sets, not two configurations.

## Tuned on field data, not stock datasets

The classifier was trained on 7 years of footage from active VDS deployments — construction yards in the rain, dealership lots at 3 a.m., apartment garages, substations. Stock COCO models can't tell a tarp from a person at 80 feet. Ours can.

## False-alarm reduction: 97%

Every analytic alert is reviewed by a SOC operator before it escalates to the customer. Animals, blowing debris, headlights, and shadows are filtered out. The result: customers see verified events, not raw model output.

## Built for the platform, not bolted on

Analytics rules are configured in the same console as users, retention, and SOC routing. Changes apply in seconds. Every rule edit is logged in the [12-month audit trail](/platform/security).

faq.q: How fast does an alert reach a person?
faq.a: Detection to model output is sub-3-second. Detection to verified SOC operator is under 60 seconds on average.

faq.q: Can I run rules on cameras I already own?
faq.a: Yes — any ONVIF or RTSP camera not on the NDAA prohibited list. See [camera-agnostic ingest](/platform).

faq.q: What is the false-positive rate?
faq.a: Verified alerts to customers see a 97% reduction in false positives versus raw motion or unverified AI alerts. The SOC layer is the difference.

faq.q: Can I run rules differently on weekdays vs. weekends?
faq.a: Yes. Schedules are per-rule, per-camera, with full day-of-week and time-of-day granularity.

finalCTAHeading: Watch a rule fire on your own camera.
finalCTABody: Send us an RTSP URL. We will configure an intrusion zone live during the demo.

seoTitle: Alerts Engine | Tiers, Escalation, Filtering | VDS
metaDescription: Three-tier alert engine with rule-based escalation, SOC verification, and 97% false-positive reduction. Sub-3-second detection, under-60-second response.
h1: Three tiers. One workflow. 97% fewer false alarms.
heroSubhead: Every alert flows through detection, verification, and escalation. Tiered routing sends informational events to dashboards, action events to your phone, and critical events to a SOC operator who is already watching.
body:
## The three tiers

### Tier 1 — Informational
Logged to the dashboard. No push, no operator. Used for after-hours camera health, low-confidence motion, and audit-only rule firings.

### Tier 2 — Action
Push notification to designated users via the mobile app and integrations (Slack, Teams, email, SMS). One-tap acknowledge. Optional escalation to Tier 3 if not acknowledged within a configurable window (default 5 minutes).

### Tier 3 — Critical
Routed simultaneously to:
- The SOC console for verified operator response
- The mobile app for designated on-call users
- The configured ACS or alarm central if linked
- Pre-authorized LE dispatch where applicable

Tier 3 is the SLA tier — under 60-second operator escalation, full incident report on close.

## What drives the 97% false-alarm reduction

1. **Model filtering** — sub-3-second classification rejects animals, debris, headlights, and shadow movement
2. **Rule context** — schedules and authorized-actor lists suppress legitimate activity
3. **SOC verification** — every Tier 3 alert is reviewed by a human before customer escalation

Raw model output to verified customer alert ratio runs around 33:1 in active production deployments. The model fires often. The customer hears about it rarely. The right events get through every time.

## Per-rule routing

Every rule can route to a different tier, a different user group, a different integration. A loading dock intrusion at 3 a.m. wakes the SOC. A loitering event at the front entrance during business hours opens a Slack thread. Same camera, different rules, different paths.

## Acknowledgement and audit

Every alert has a state: open, acknowledged, escalated, resolved, dismissed. State transitions are logged with timestamp and actor. Resolution requires a disposition code from a configurable list. The 12-month audit log catches every move.

## Retention and replay

Alert clips are retained on the platform's standard cadence (30/60/90 days). Critical alerts can be tagged for extended retention up to 1 year. Replay is available from the alert detail view with frame-by-frame stepping and clip export.

faq.q: How do I tune false-positive rates on a noisy camera?
faq.a: Tier 1 logging plus rule-confidence sliders. We run a 7-day shake-out on every new rule and report the tuning recommendations.

faq.q: Can I bypass the SOC and route alerts directly to my own team?
faq.a: Yes — disable SOC routing per rule or per site. The alert engine is independent of the SOC tier.

faq.q: What is the maximum number of rules per camera?
faq.a: 32 per camera, 256 per site. We have not seen a deployment exceed half of that.

faq.q: Are alerts delivered if the camera's internet drops?
faq.a: On-trailer deployments buffer detection locally and forward when connectivity restores. Fixed-site deployments depend on the site's network design — we will spec a cellular failover during pre-deployment.

finalCTAHeading: See alert routing on your own rules.
finalCTABody: We will configure a Tier 3 rule and trigger it live during the demo.
notes: Flow diagram of three tiers belongs above the fold. Tier 3 metrics tied back to the SOC SLA.

metaDescription: REST API, webhooks, mobile SDK, and Postman collection for AI VisionStream. OAuth2 + API keys. Build ITSM, BIM, and PSIM integrations.
h1: REST API, Webhooks, and SDK for AI VisionStream
heroSubhead: Pull events, push clips, subscribe to webhooks, and embed live video in your own application. OAuth2 and API key authentication. Postman collection included.
heroStats: REST + Webhooks • OAuth2 / API keys • iOS + Android SDK • Rate-limited at 100 req/sec
body:
AI VisionStream exposes a versioned REST API plus webhook subscriptions plus a native mobile SDK. If your team builds software — ITSM, PSIM, BIM/CDE, custom operations dashboards — you do not have to screen-scrape our UI.

## API surface

Current stable version: `v2`. Base URL: `https://api.visionstream.us/v2`.

Endpoint families:

- **Events** — list, filter, and stream AI events (LPR, intrusion, tripwire, loitering, crowd)
- **Cameras** — inventory, health, ONVIF capability discovery
- **Sites** — site metadata, group membership, geocoordinates
- **Clips** — generate time-bounded exports, retrieve signed URLs, fetch chain-of-custody records
- **Users** — RBAC management, MFA status, SSO mapping
- **Audit** — query the immutable 12-month log
- **Health** — device-level battery, solar input, cellular RSRP, uptime

Responses are JSON. Errors follow RFC 7807 (Problem Details). Pagination is cursor-based; do not assume offset.

## Webhooks

Subscribe a URL; receive POST callbacks within ~250ms of the underlying event. Payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a tenant-scoped secret — verify the `X-VisionStream-Signature` header before processing.

Subscribable event types:

- `event.lpr.matched` — plate matched a watch list
- `event.lpr.detected` — plate read, no list match
- `event.intrusion.entered` / `event.intrusion.exited`
- `event.tripwire.crossed`
- `event.loitering.threshold`
- `device.health.degraded` / `device.health.recovered`
- `device.tamper.detected`
- `clip.export.ready` — async clip generation completed

Retry policy: exponential backoff, 3 attempts over 5 minutes. Dead-letter inspection available in the developer console.

## Mobile SDK

Native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) SDKs ship as Swift Package Manager and Maven artifacts. Capabilities:

- Authenticate with OAuth2 or API key
- Embed live H.265 video views with hardware decode
- Subscribe to events over WebSocket
- Trigger audio talk-down on speaker-equipped cameras
- Generate and share clips with chain-of-custody preserved

Sample apps in both languages ship with the SDK. Minimum supported versions: iOS 15, Android 10.

## Authentication

Two methods, pick per integration:

- **OAuth2 (authorization code + PKCE)** — for end-user-facing apps. Standard scopes: `events:read`, `clips:write`, `cameras:read`, `audit:read`, `admin:*`.
- **API keys** — for server-to-server. Scoped per integration, rotatable without downtime, audit-logged on every call.

API keys are issued from the Developer Console. Each key has an environment label (production / staging), an owner email, and a last-used timestamp.

## Rate limits

Standard tier: 100 requests per second per tenant, 6,000 per minute, burst to 200 for 10 seconds. Webhook receive volume is unlimited.

429 responses include `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers. If you need higher limits — typical for video-wall or PSIM integrations polling 200+ cameras — contact us; enterprise tier raises the ceiling to 1,000/sec.

## Example use cases

- **ITSM integration (ServiceNow, Jira Service Management)** — open a ticket automatically when a `device.health.degraded` webhook fires. Auto-close on `device.health.recovered`.
- **Custom operations dashboard** — pull LPR events into a Grafana panel for a logistics yard, plot dwell time per truck.
- **BIM/CDE integration (Autodesk Construction Cloud, Procore)** — link camera coverage zones to BIM model elements; tag site safety incidents to specific building areas.
- **PSIM (Genetec, Milestone, Lenel)** — forward events into an existing command-and-control system without ripping out the upstream investment.
- **Insurance reporting** — pull a 90-day incident summary per site as part of a quarterly carrier package.

## Documentation and support

Full reference at `developers.visionstream.us`. Postman collection downloadable from the same URL. Developer support is included with any production tenant — direct Slack Connect channel for paid plans.

faq.q: Is the API stable?
faq.a: v2 is the current stable version. v1 is deprecated and end-of-life 2026-12-31. Breaking changes are announced 180 days in advance.

faq.q: Can I get a sandbox tenant?
faq.a: Yes. Sandbox tenants include 4 simulated cameras with deterministic event streams for integration testing. No production data risk.

faq.q: Are webhooks delivered exactly once?
faq.a: At-least-once. Use the `event_id` field to deduplicate on your end.

faq.q: What happens to integrations when retention rolls over?
faq.a: Events older than your retention tier return 410 Gone with the event ID intact. Pull and persist events you need long-term.

faq.q: Is there a usage cost for the API?
faq.a: Not at standard tier. Enterprise tier (above 1,000 req/sec) is quoted per integration.

finalCTAHeading: Build on AI VisionStream
finalCTABody: Request API access and we will provision a sandbox tenant, ship you the Postman collection, and route you to a solutions engineer.

seoTitle: Platform Security & Compliance | NDAA, AWS US-Only | VDS
metaDescription: NDAA Section 889 compliant. AWS US-only. TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. RBAC, MFA, and an immutable 12-month audit log.
h1: Security posture, written down. Verifiable on audit day.
heroSubhead: NDAA 889 compliant. AWS US-only data residency. TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. RBAC, MFA, and a 12-month immutable audit log. We publish it because we built it that way.
body:
## Data residency

100% of customer video, metadata, and platform data lives in AWS US regions (us-east and us-west). No replication outside the United States. No third-party CDN for video playback. No offshore support access to customer tenants.

## Encryption

- **In transit:** TLS 1.3 between camera, cloud, and client. RTSP streams are wrapped in TLS at the ingest gateway.
- **At rest:** AES-256 on all stored video and metadata, with AWS KMS-managed keys.
- **Key rotation:** automatic on a 90-day cycle.

## Identity and access

- **MFA** required on every account. TOTP and WebAuthn (hardware key) supported.
- **RBAC** at the user, site, and camera level. Pre-built roles plus custom role definition.
- **SSO** via SAML 2.0 and OIDC. Okta, Azure AD, and Google Workspace tested.
- **Session expiration** configurable per-tenant, default 8 hours.
- **Device registration** for mobile clients with revocation per device.

## Audit log

Every user action, every alert event, every camera state change, every rule edit, every clip share — logged in an immutable 12-month audit trail. Exportable to JSON, CSV, or your SIEM via webhook. Required for SOC 2 customers. Available on every tier.

## Network and supply chain

- **NDAA Section 889 compliant.** No Dahua, no Hikvision, no Lorex, no Huawei in our supply chain or in supported third-party cameras.
- **AWS Cloud Partner** — infrastructure benefits from AWS shared-responsibility controls.
- **Assembled in Pikesville, Maryland.**
- **Penetration tested annually** by an independent third party. Report available under NDA.

## What we will not do

- We will not publish your camera feeds to a public web page
- We will not leave a camera reachable from the open internet
- We will not sell or share customer footage
- We will not run a pattern-of-life database across customer plates
- We will not store data outside the United States

These are not aspirational. They are architectural. If you want the specifics, the security packet runs 28 pages.

## Vulnerability disclosure

Coordinated disclosure at security@visiondetectionsystems.com. We publish CVE-class advisories to customers within 72 hours of confirmation, with mitigation guidance.

faq.q: Are you SOC 2 certified?
faq.a: SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA. Audit cycle is annual.

faq.q: Can I bring my own KMS key?
faq.a: Customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS are available on enterprise tiers.

faq.q: How long is the audit log retained?
faq.a: 12 months by default, with extended retention available on request. Exports can be archived indefinitely by the customer.

faq.q: Have you had a security incident?
faq.a: No customer-facing breach to date. We publish an annual transparency report at /trust.

faq.q: How does this compare to other VMS platforms?
faq.a: We publish our posture. Several large competitors have had public breaches in the last 5 years — see /compare for specifics.

finalCTABody: We will send the full architecture diagram, encryption posture, RBAC model, and pen-test summary under NDA.

seoTitle: Cloud Video Surveillance | AI VisionStream VMS | VDS
metaDescription: Cloud video surveillance built on AWS. Camera-agnostic ONVIF/RTSP, 30/60/90-day retention, multi-site single pane, TLS 1.3, AES-256, US-only.
h1: Cloud Video Surveillance Without an On-Site Recorder
heroSubhead: AWS-backed VMS. Camera-agnostic over ONVIF and RTSP. Multi-site view in one browser tab. No DVR, no NVR, no Windows server in a closet.
heroStats: AWS Cloud Partner • TLS 1.3 / AES-256 • 30/60/90-day retention • Sub-3-second alerts
body:
AI VisionStream is the video management system inside every VDS deployment. It runs on AWS in US-only regions, ingests ONVIF and RTSP streams from any compliant camera, and presents 500+ deployments across 30+ states through a single browser session.

## What "cloud-native" actually means here

There is no headend appliance on your site. No NVR to reimage, no Windows Server patch cycle, no SD card to fail at month nine. Cameras stream to the edge unit on the trailer or building, which buffers locally and forwards to AWS over encrypted cellular, 5G, or wired uplink. Recording, AI inference, user management, and storage all live in the cloud.

Practical consequences:

- Add a site by shipping hardware. No headend configuration on the customer LAN.
- A failed camera does not take down a site. The other cameras keep recording.
- Firmware and VMS updates ship from us. No truck roll required.
- Bandwidth-constrained sites use H.265 with adaptive bitrate; storage cost stays predictable.

## Camera-agnostic

AI VisionStream is ONVIF Profile S/T and RTSP compliant. If a camera speaks either protocol — and 95%+ of fixed IP cameras manufactured after 2018 do — it integrates. We have customers running Axis, Hanwha, Bosch, Hikvision, Dahua, Pelco, Avigilon, Ubiquiti, and a long tail of OEM rebrands on the same tenant. NDAA Section 889 compliance is tracked per camera; the platform itself is unrestricted.

## Multi-site single pane

One login, every site. Filter by region, site group, camera type, or status. Pre-built map view plots devices over satellite imagery. A regional loss-prevention manager covering 40 retail locations gets the same interface as a one-trailer construction project.

User permissions are role-based (RBAC) with optional MFA enforcement at the tenant level. Typical role hierarchy: Tenant Admin, Site Manager, Operator, Viewer, External Auditor. Every login, view, export, and share-link action writes to an immutable 12-month audit log.

## Retention tiers

Pick per camera, per site, or per tenant:

- **30 days** — operational review, day-to-day incident response, lowest cost
- **60 days** — most common default for retail, logistics, and construction
- **90 days** — healthcare, finance, government, and litigation-sensitive deployments

Need longer? 1-year and 7-year evidence holds are available as add-ons, billed by GB/month. Retention is enforced server-side; users cannot delete recordings before policy expiry.

## AI events, not just recording

The same stream that records is analyzed in real time:

- **License plate recognition** at 95%+ accuracy with sub-3-second alert delivery
- **Intrusion zones** with polygon geometry and time-of-day rules
- **Virtual tripwires** with directionality (in, out, both)
- **Loitering detection** with dwell-time thresholds
- **Crowd / occupancy counting** with min-max alerting

Events route to the VDS 24/7 SOC, to customer SMS/email/webhook, or to a third-party PSIM via our REST API.

## Security posture

- TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest
- US-only AWS regions (us-east-1, us-west-2 primary)
- MFA available tenant-wide, enforceable by role
- SAML SSO supported (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace)
- 12-month immutable audit log, exportable for compliance review
- SOC 2 Type II controls inherited from AWS; VDS SOC 2 report available under NDA

## Cost model

Per-camera, per-month subscription. Storage is included up to the retention tier you select. Bandwidth is included. Software updates are included. No per-event fees, no per-user seat fees, no API call metering at standard tier.

faq.q: Do I need to replace my existing cameras?
faq.a: No, if they speak ONVIF or RTSP. We onboard the existing fleet, validate stream quality, and add cameras only where coverage gaps exist.

faq.q: What happens if the cellular link drops?
faq.a: The edge unit buffers locally up to 72 hours depending on configuration. Footage syncs to cloud when the link restores. SOC is notified at the 5-minute mark.

faq.q: Can I export footage for law enforcement?
faq.a: Yes. Operators with export rights generate a time-bounded clip; the system writes a chain-of-custody record including the requesting user, timestamp, and SHA-256 hash of the export.

faq.q: Is data ever stored outside the US?
faq.a: No. All processing and storage occurs in US AWS regions. No offshore support access to recorded video.

faq.q: How is this different from a traditional VMS?
faq.a: No on-site server, no port forwarding, no annual license renewal cycle, no headend to fail. Updates ship from AWS, not a USB stick.

finalCTABody: 30-minute live demo with your floor plan and camera count. We will show retention, AI events, audit log, and user permissions on actual deployments.

heroSubhead: 95%+ read accuracy on US plates from any compatible camera. Hotlist alerts route directly to the SOC. No public camera feed. No pattern-of-life database.
body:
## What "95%+ accuracy" actually means

Measured on US plates, at angles up to 30 degrees, at speeds up to 35 mph, in mixed lighting. Reads include state inference. Numbers come from production deployments across 30+ states, not a single test lane.

## How the workflow runs

1. Camera captures the plate.
2. Model reads it in under 3 seconds.
3. Plate is matched against your hotlist (BOLO list, banned vehicles, watchlist).
4. On match, alert routes to the [SOC](/platform/soc) and to your mobile app simultaneously.
5. SOC operator verifies, escalates to LE if applicable, and files a full incident report.

## Hotlist management

- Upload by CSV, API, or manual entry
- Set per-list rules (alert only, alert and dispatch, alert and audio challenge)
- Tag plates with notes for SOC context
- Set expiration dates per plate
- Every edit logged in the 12-month audit trail

## What we will not do

- We will not expose your plate reads to other customers
- We will not aggregate plate reads into a national pattern-of-life database
- We will not publish your camera feed to the open internet
- We will not store plate data outside US AWS regions

If those sentences sound pointed, it is because several "public safety camera" platforms do the opposite. Read our [security and privacy posture](/platform/security).

## Works with the cameras you have

LPR runs on any compatible ONVIF/RTSP camera meeting basic resolution and shutter specs (most modern 4MP cameras qualify). No proprietary LPR camera required. We will spec the right lens and angle for your lane during pre-deployment.

faq.q: What plate formats are supported?
faq.a: All 50 US states and Canadian provinces. Vanity plates, motorcycle plates, and dealer plates are read.

faq.q: How is hotlist matching different from a public ALPR network?
faq.a: Your hotlist is yours. It is not shared with other customers, law enforcement agencies, or third parties unless you explicitly authorize a dispatch on a specific match.

faq.q: Do you sell or share plate data?
faq.a: No. Plate data lives in your tenant, in US AWS regions, with 30/60/90-day retention you control.

faq.q: Can LPR run on a mobile trailer?
faq.a: Yes. Solar-autonomous trailers run the same LPR stack as fixed-site cameras. Same accuracy, same sub-3-second read time.

metaDescription: In-house US operators, under 60-second escalation, live audio talk-down, direct LE dispatch with video. 97% false-alarm reduction.
h1: A US operator on every alert. Under 60 seconds. Every time.
heroSubhead: VDS-employed operators, working from our facility, watching your alerts 24/7. They verify the event, talk down through the trailer PA, and dispatch police with live video when it is real.
body:
## What happens in the 60 seconds after an alert

1. **T+0s** — Camera detects an event. Model classifies it. Rule fires.
2. **T+3s** — Alert lands in the SOC console with live video and rule context.
3. **T+15s** — Operator opens the camera feed, reviews 10 seconds of pre-event buffer.
4. **T+30s** — Operator either dismisses (animal, debris) or escalates.
5. **T+45s** — On escalation: operator activates live audio talk-down through the trailer PA, sends mobile push to your team, opens a dispatch line to local LE if pre-authorized.
6. **T+60s** — Customer is on the alert. LE has been notified with live video link if applicable. Incident report has been started.

## Audio talk-down is a real deterrent

A live operator saying "I can see you in the blue jacket near the white Ford. Police have been notified. Leave the property now" stops 8 out of 10 attempted incidents before LE arrives. Recorded loops do not. Verified humans do.

## Direct law enforcement coordination

Where allowed, our operators have direct dial lines to dispatch in the jurisdiction. We send a CAD-compatible incident summary plus a live video link. LE arrives knowing what they are walking into.

## Every event has a report

After resolution, the customer receives a full incident report:

- Timestamps for detection, escalation, and resolution
- Operator actions taken
- Audio transcript if talk-down was used
- LE case number if dispatched
- Linked video clips
- Recommendations for rule tuning

Reports live in the platform and export to PDF, CSV, or your SIEM.

## Why in-house matters

Contracted monitoring centers handle dozens of disparate customer platforms with operators who learn a new UI every shift. Our operators are trained on AI VisionStream because it is the only thing they run. They know the rule library. They know the integrations. They know your site layout if you have been deployed for more than 30 days.

faq.q: Are the operators VDS employees or contracted?
faq.a: VDS employees, in our facility, in the United States. No offshoring, no sub-contracting.

faq.q: What is the average escalation time?
faq.a: Under 60 seconds from detection to verified operator action. We report this metric monthly to every customer.

faq.q: Can I disable SOC monitoring and use my own team?
faq.a: Yes. The mobile app and alert engine work standalone. SOC is an optional service tier — see [pricing](/platform/pricing).

faq.q: Will the SOC dispatch police without my approval?
faq.a: Only on pre-authorized event types in pre-authorized jurisdictions. Everything else routes to your designated contact first. Authorization rules are configured per-site and logged.

faq.q: How does talk-down work on a fixed-site install?
faq.a: If the site has compatible PA hardware (IP speakers, intercom, or amplifier with a network input), our operators speak live through the same channel. We will spec it during pre-deployment.

finalCTABody: We can patch a live feed from our console into the call so you see how an alert actually moves.

body:
## Who this is for

The VDS dealer program is built for security integrators, low-voltage contractors, and managed service providers who already sell to commercial end customers and want to add mobile surveillance and a hosted VMS to the offering. It's not a referral program — dealers transact, fulfill, and own the customer relationship.

If you're looking to refer leads to VDS for a commission, that's our separate referral program. Ask sales.

## Volume tiers

Dealer pricing is structured around trailing-12-month volume. Tiers reset every January 1; new dealers start at Tier 1 and move up based on actual closed volume.

| Tier | Annual Volume | Trailer Discount | Platform Discount | MDF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1 — Authorized** | $0-$100K | 12% off list | 10% off list | — |
| **Tier 2 — Preferred** | $100K-$500K | 18% off list | 15% off list | 1% of revenue |
| **Tier 3 — Premier** | $500K-$2M | 25% off list | 20% off list | 2% of revenue |
| **Tier 4 — Strategic** | $2M+ | Negotiated | Negotiated | 3% of revenue |

Discounts apply to the published list prices on [the main pricing page](/pricing). MDF (Marketing Development Funds) accrues quarterly, paid as co-op against approved marketing spend or as bill credits.

## MAP policy

Minimum Advertised Price is published with the program and enforced. Dealers may discount in private quotes — that's normal commercial behavior — but advertised pricing (website, public ads, public proposals) must hold the line at MAP or above. The reason is structural: published prices on the VDS main pricing page are the floor. Dealers undercutting public pricing in public is what creates the race-to-the-bottom dynamic that destroys margin for everyone.

MAP violations get a written warning on the first incident. Two violations in a 12-month window suspends program eligibility for 90 days. Three suspends indefinitely.

## What dealers get

**Wholesale pricing.** Per the tier table above, applied to any line item on a customer order — trailers, platform subscriptions, SOC monitoring, accessories.

**Dealer portal.** Quote builder, order entry, deal registration, marketing assets, training, and commission/MDF tracking. The portal is self-serve. Most orders never require a sales call.

**Deal registration.** Register a deal with VDS and lock pricing for 90 days, protecting you from another dealer or direct sale undercutting your work-in-flight. Approved registrations get a 5% additional discount on top of tier pricing.

**Technical training and certification.** Free online certification path for sales and field tech roles. Certified Field Tech is the prerequisite for billing customer-facing installs through the dealer channel.

**Marketing assets.** Co-branded brochures, web pages, slide decks, case studies. Customizable with your logo and contact info.

**Marketing Development Funds.** Quarterly accrual at the tier rate, redeemable against approved campaigns (trade shows, paid ads, content production) or as account credit.

**Demo trailer program.** Dealers at Tier 2+ can request a loaner trailer for customer demos. Loan period is 14 days. One loan per quarter at Tier 2, unlimited at Tier 3+.

## What dealers commit to

- Sell only the trailers and platform tiers listed on the current VDS lineup
- Honor MAP on all public pricing and advertising
- Complete the Authorized certification within 90 days of program entry
- Maintain commercial general liability and E&O insurance with VDS named as additional insured
- Use deal registration for any opportunity over $25K
- Submit a forecast and pipeline review quarterly (15-minute call, sales team driven)

## Co-marketing and lead-share

VDS routes inbound leads to dealers based on geography, vertical specialty, and tier. Tier 3 and Tier 4 dealers get first right of refusal on inbound leads in their territory. Tier 1 and Tier 2 dealers get leads on a round-robin basis after Tier 3/4 declines.

Outbound demand-gen co-investment (paid media, trade shows, event sponsorships) is available to Tier 2+ dealers via MDF and proposal-based campaign funding.

## How to apply

The dealer application is short. We're looking for:

- An active business with a security or low-voltage integration history
- General liability insurance ($1M minimum, $2M preferred)
- A named technical contact and a named sales contact
- Brief overview of your geographic and vertical focus

Most applications are approved within 5 business days. We'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff to walk through the portal, deal registration, and certification before your first quote goes out.

faq.q: Can I sell into any geography?
faq.a: Yes, but lead routing favors dealers with a documented presence in the region. There's no exclusive territory in the program at any tier.

faq.q: What if my customer wants direct VDS support?
faq.a: Standard platform support is direct from VDS regardless of who sold the deployment. Implementation, on-site service, and account management can stay with you or transition to VDS direct — customer's choice.

faq.q: Do I have to white-label the platform?
faq.a: No. The platform is VDS-branded. Dealer co-branding is available on customer-facing portals at Tier 3+ if the dealer specifically wants it.

faq.q: Can I bundle VDS with other products?
faq.a: Yes, as long as the VDS components meet MAP. Most dealers bundle trailers with access control, alarm panels, or fence detection from other manufacturers — that's normal.

faq.q: What happens if I drop volume tier?
faq.a: Tiers are based on trailing 12 months and recalculated quarterly. If you drop a tier, you keep the higher tier's pricing on existing in-flight quotes (registered deals), but new quotes price at the new tier. We don't retroactively re-bill.

finalCTAHeading: Join the dealer program
finalCTABody: Apply, get certified, start quoting. Most dealers issue their first VDS quote within 30 days of application approval.

seoTitle: Mobile Surveillance Trailer Leasing & Rentals | VDS Pricing
metaDescription: VDS trailer leasing terms — 3-month minimum, month-to-month after, includes platform, SOC optional. Short-term event rentals and multi-year fleet leases.
h1: Lease a Trailer Without Surprise Charges
heroSubhead: Standard 3-month minimum, month-to-month after. Hardware, platform, freight on a quote, and a 7-business-day standard lead time. Long-term and short-term options below.
body:
## Standard lease terms

VDS trailer leases are designed to be readable in five minutes. The terms below apply to every lease unless you negotiate an enterprise master agreement.

| Term | Value |
|---|---|
| **Minimum term** | 3 months |
| **After minimum** | Month-to-month, 30-day notice to cancel |
| **Security deposit** | One month's lease, refundable |
| **Lead time (standard)** | 5-10 business days |
| **Lead time (expedited)** | 48-72 hours, premium applies |
| **Freight** | Billed at cost, both ways |
| **Relocation between sites** | Free, 48-hour notice required |
| **Platform included** | Standard tier ($39/cam/mo equivalent) |
| **SOC monitoring** | Optional, $399/site/mo |

No setup fees. No activation fees. No "platform onboarding" fees. The lease number on your quote is what you pay every month for the trailer itself.

## What's included with every lease

- **Hardware** — trailer, mast, cameras, solar, batteries, cellular hardware
- **Platform access** — Standard tier subscription bundled with the lease price
- **Standard maintenance** — firmware updates, remote diagnostics, parts replacement
- **Cellular data** — dual-carrier LTE/5G, unlimited data on standard plans
- **Cloud storage** — 30-day video retention on AWS US-East/West
- **NDAA compliance documentation** — provided with every unit

## What's not included

- SOC active monitoring ($399/site/month, add or remove anytime after the first 30 days)
- Starlink uplink ($150/month, optional)
- On-site service calls beyond standard maintenance (T&M, only billed when a non-VDS cause requires truck roll)
- Customer-caused damage (covered by deposit + insurance)
- Platform upgrades to Pro or Enterprise

## Short-term and event rentals

For events, temporary jobsites, and incident-response deployments, we lease trailers under three months at a premium. Common use cases: festivals, sporting events, film sets, disaster recovery operations, temporary lay-down yards for major projects.

| Term | Pricing |
|---|---|
| **30 days** | 1.5x standard monthly rate |
| **60 days** | 1.25x standard monthly rate |
| **90+ days** | Standard rate |

Short-term rentals include the same hardware, platform, and freight handling as standard leases. SOC monitoring is highly recommended for events and is available on a per-night basis if a full month doesn't fit.

## Long-term and multi-year fleets

Multi-trailer, multi-year deployments get materially better economics. Common structures:

- **12-month commit:** 5% discount off standard lease rate
- **24-month commit:** 10% discount, includes one free trailer swap mid-term
- **36-month commit:** 15% discount, includes platform Pro tier upgrade
- **Fleet (5+ trailers):** volume matrix, negotiated MSA

Fleet customers also get a dedicated CSM, quarterly site review, and prioritized service scheduling.

## Lead time, in detail

Standard: **5-10 business days** from signed lease to on-site, including SOC onboarding and customer playbook configuration.

Expedited: **48-72 hours** for active incident response. We hold a small inventory of staged trailers in three regional depots (Mid-Atlantic, Southeast, West) for exactly this purpose. Expedited freight and overtime mobilization fees apply.

Multi-unit deployments of 3+ trailers may extend lead time depending on the trailer configuration. We'll quote the exact date with the quote.

## Early termination

If you cancel after the 3-month minimum, you owe nothing beyond the current month. Cancel mid-month and the remainder of that month is billed.

If you cancel during the minimum term, the remaining months of the minimum are payable. There is no separate ETF on top of that.

If you signed a multi-year commit, early termination is governed by your MSA — typically a glide-path payment that reflects unrecovered mobilization cost.

## Damage, loss, and insurance

Standard leases require the customer to maintain general liability and property coverage naming VDS as additional insured. We provide a sample certificate. Normal wear and tear is on us; customer-caused damage (vehicle strikes, vandalism beyond what the trailer self-deters, theft of the trailer itself) is on the customer.

faq.q: Can I really cancel month-to-month after 90 days?
faq.a: Yes. Give us 30 days' notice and pay the current month. No fees, no clawbacks.

faq.q: What if a trailer fails or underperforms?
faq.a: We swap it. Standard service-level expectation is a replacement on-site within 72 hours for a hardware failure that takes the unit offline. SOC monitors uptime continuously, so we usually know before you do.

faq.q: Do you lease used trailers at a discount?
faq.a: No. Every leased trailer is a current-revision, fully serviced unit. We retire trailers from the lease pool at end-of-service-life and sell them through a separate channel.

faq.q: Can I lease just the cameras, not the trailer?
faq.a: That's a platform-only deployment with customer-supplied cameras — see [Subscription Plans](/pricing/subscription-plans). Different product.

faq.q: Can I lease-to-own?
faq.a: Yes, on Sky Guard MSU. Standard lease-to-own runs 36 months at $2,200/mo with a $500 buyout at end of term. Other trailers quote-based.

finalCTAHeading: Lease a trailer
finalCTABody: Quote in one business day. Trailer on site in 5-10 business days. Cancel any month after 90 days.

seoTitle: Buy a Mobile Surveillance Trailer | VDS Purchase Pricing
metaDescription: Buy a VDS trailer outright. Sky Guard MSU at $38,000. Capex vs opex breakdown, warranty terms, and post-sale service plans.
h1: Buy Outright When the Math Works
heroSubhead: For deployments that outlive a lease, ownership is the right answer. Sky Guard MSU at $38,000, full warranty, and a service plan that doesn't disappear after the PO clears.
body:
## When purchase beats lease

Lease economics work best for deployments under 30 months. Above that, the math typically flips toward purchase. We've watched customers run the spreadsheet — here's the rule of thumb:

| Deployment horizon | Recommended model |
|---|---|
| <12 months | Lease, no question |
| 12-30 months | Lease, with optional buyout at end of term |
| 30+ months, single site | Purchase |
| Fleet, mobile across multiple sites | Lease (the flexibility outweighs the savings) |
| Capex-only budget cycles | Purchase, regardless of horizon |

The break-even on Sky Guard MSU is roughly 18 months — $2,200 × 17.3 months = $38,000. After 18 months of ownership, every additional month is platform + maintenance only.

## What you pay for

The purchase price is hardware. Software and monitoring are sold separately as ongoing subscriptions, the same way they would be on a leased trailer. This keeps the capex number clean for finance teams and avoids bundling software cost into a depreciable asset.

| Item | Price | Type |
|---|---|---|
| **Sky Guard MSU** | $38,000 | One-time, capex |
| **Swift Deploy Trailer** | Contact | One-time, capex |
| **Boundary Guard Pro** | Contact | One-time, capex |
| **Solar Camera Pole** | Custom | One-time, capex |
| **VDS Platform (Standard)** | $39/cam/mo | Recurring, opex |
| **SOC Active Monitoring** | $399/site/mo | Recurring, opex |
| **Extended Warranty (3-year)** | 12% of purchase price | One-time, capex |
| **White-glove deployment** | $1,500/unit | One-time |

## Capex vs opex — how customers actually decide

The choice usually comes down to four factors:

**Budget structure.** Many enterprise security buyers have capex authority but limited opex. Trailers as a capex line are easier to approve than recurring lease payments. Government, education, and federal buyers in particular often prefer purchase for budget cycle reasons.

**Deployment longevity.** Single-site, permanent or near-permanent deployments — a port, a substation, a long-cycle data center build — favor purchase. Roving construction, event security, and disaster response favor lease.

**Refresh strategy.** Owning a trailer means owning the refresh decision. Cameras improve. Solar improves. Cellular standards shift (4G → 5G → whatever's next). Lease customers refresh implicitly when we update the lease pool. Purchase customers refresh when they decide to.

**Tax treatment.** Section 179 expensing and bonus depreciation may make purchase materially more attractive in a given tax year. We're not your CPA — talk to yours.

## Warranty terms

**Standard warranty (included, 12 months):**
- All trailer hardware against manufacturing defect
- Cameras, mast, solar panels, batteries, cellular hardware
- Excludes: customer-caused damage, acts of nature beyond design spec, neglect
- Parts shipped within 48 hours; labor billed at standard rate

**Extended warranty (optional, 3-year):**
- 12% of purchase price, paid up front
- Same coverage as standard, extended to 36 months total
- Adds 50% labor allowance on covered repairs
- Adds one free battery bank replacement at year 3

**Lifetime platform compatibility:**
We commit, in writing, that any trailer purchased from us will remain platform-compatible for a minimum of 7 years from delivery. Older trailers may not get every new feature, but they will not be EOL'd off the platform short of that horizon.

## Post-sale service

Ownership means you own the maintenance. We offer three service tiers for trailer owners:

| Plan | Price | What's covered |
|---|---|---|
| **Self-serve** | $0 | Remote firmware updates, platform support, parts at list |
| **Standard service** | $99/unit/mo | Above + 50% parts discount + 2 service calls/year included |
| **Premium service** | $249/unit/mo | Above + unlimited service calls + 4-hour response SLA + annual on-site PM |

Most purchase customers run Standard service. Premium is typical for fleet owners with mission-critical deployments where downtime cost exceeds the plan price.

## Trade-in

If you bought a trailer from us 4+ years ago and want to refresh, we offer trade-in credit toward a new unit. Typical trade-in value on a Sky Guard MSU is 25-40% of original purchase price depending on age and condition. Quoted per unit on inspection.

faq.q: Can I finance the purchase?
faq.a: Yes. We work with two equipment financing partners for terms up to 60 months. Rates are credit-dependent. Most purchase customers, though, are using existing capex budget — financing tends to make the lease math more attractive than purchase math.

faq.q: What happens to platform features I bought when a new tier launches?
faq.a: New features land on existing platform tiers per the published roadmap. You don't lose anything by buying today. You may want to upgrade tier later if a Pro-tier feature becomes important.

faq.q: Can I sell a trailer I bought from VDS?
faq.a: Yes. It's your property. We'll re-onboard the new owner to the platform on standard terms. We don't charge a transfer fee, but the new owner becomes responsible for the platform subscription from the transfer date.

faq.q: What's the difference between Sky Guard purchase and lease-to-own?
faq.a: Purchase is one payment, ownership immediately. Lease-to-own is 36 monthly payments with a $500 buyout — total cost is higher, but the cash-flow profile fits some budgets better.

faq.q: Are purchase orders accepted, or do I need to prepay?
faq.a: Net-30 POs accepted for customers with approved credit. Standard for federal, state, and Fortune 1000 buyers. New customers may be asked for 50% deposit on the first unit.

finalCTAHeading: Buy a trailer
finalCTABody: Quote, PO, build, ship. Typical purchase cycle is 4-6 weeks from PO. Service plan starts on delivery.

seoTitle: VDS Platform Subscription Plans | Standard, Pro, Enterprise
metaDescription: VDS platform pricing — Standard $39, Pro $69, Enterprise custom. Camera-agnostic VMS with 30/60/90-day retention. SOC add-on $399/site/mo.
h1: Platform Subscriptions, Per Camera, Per Month
heroSubhead: One pricing axis: how many cameras, which tier. Three tiers. No hidden seat fees, no analytics paywall on tier 1, no surprises on the invoice.
body:
## How platform pricing works

One dimension: per camera, per month, at the tier you pick. A 12-camera site on Pro is $69 × 12 = $828/month. A 40-camera campus on Standard is $39 × 40 = $1,560/month. There's no per-seat fee, no per-event fee, no analytics module to unlock at extra cost.

You can mix tiers across a fleet but not within a site — every camera at one physical site runs the same tier. This is a practical limit, not a billing trick; the analytics pipeline runs per-site for a reason.

## The three tiers

| | Standard | Pro | Enterprise |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Price** | $39/cam/mo | $69/cam/mo | Custom |
| **Cloud video retention** | 30 days | 60 days | 90 days (extendable) |
| **Live view (web + mobile)** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Motion alerts** | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| **Basic analytics** | Person, vehicle | Person, vehicle | Person, vehicle |
| **Advanced analytics** | — | Intrusion, line-cross, loitering, PPE, crowding | All Pro + custom models |
| **LPR (per lane)** | — | $89/lane/mo add | Included up to fleet cap |
| **API access** | Read-only | Full read/write | Full + webhooks + SDK |
| **User seats** | 5 | 25 | Unlimited |
| **SSO (SAML/OIDC)** | — | — | Yes |
| **Audit logging** | Basic | Detailed | Forensic-grade |
| **Customer success** | Email + chat | Email + chat + scheduled calls | Dedicated CSM |
| **Onboarding** | Self-serve + docs | Standard onboarding call | White-glove |
| **Uptime SLA** | 99.5% | 99.9% | 99.95% |

## Which tier fits

**Standard ($39/cam/mo).** Single-site customers, general surveillance, no analytics requirements beyond person/vehicle motion. This is the right tier for the small construction site, the auto lot, the self-storage facility, the rural property. It's not stripped down — it's a complete VMS with 30-day retention and a real mobile app.

**Pro ($69/cam/mo).** The tier most multi-site customers settle on. Advanced analytics (line-crossing, loitering, PPE, crowd density) turn the platform from a recording system into a detection system. API access enables integration with dispatch, access control, and ticketing. Pro is the default tier on VDS trailer fleets running across 5+ sites.

**Enterprise (custom).** SSO, full audit logging, custom retention beyond 90 days, custom analytic models, and a dedicated CSM. Required for most federal contracts, regulated industries (utilities, healthcare, financial), and customers running 100+ cameras. Pricing is configuration-dependent — expect $50-$80/cam/mo equivalent in most configurations.

## SOC add-on

Every tier supports adding the VDS Security Operations Center for **$399/site/month**. SOC is priced per site, not per camera, so a 30-camera site costs the same to monitor as a 5-camera site.

What you get for $399:
- 24/7 live monitoring of priority alerts
- <60-second escalation on verified events
- Voice-down talk-down where hardware supports
- Direct dispatch coordination with your designated responders (police, internal security, on-call)
- Customer playbook configuration (what counts as priority, who gets called when)
- Weekly event summary report

The SOC is staffed in the US, trained on the VDS platform, and operating under ESA monitoring standards. Adding or removing SOC mid-subscription requires only a 30-day notice.

## Retention windows and why they matter

Retention isn't just a number — it's what determines whether you can answer the questions that come up two months after an incident.

- **30 days (Standard)** — fine for routine surveillance, investigations that surface within a month, and customers who plan to download evidence as soon as something happens
- **60 days (Pro)** — covers most insurance claim windows, employee dispute investigations, and the typical interval before a previously-unnoticed incident gets reported
- **90+ days (Enterprise)** — required for many regulated industries, federal contracts, and long-cycle dispute resolution

Customers can pull video to local archive at any time. Retention applies to cloud-resident video only.

## Billing, terms, and changes

- **Billing cycle:** monthly, invoiced on the 1st
- **Payment:** ACH preferred, credit card accepted up to $10K/month
- **Tier changes:** upgrade anytime (prorated), downgrade at next billing cycle
- **Add/remove cameras:** anytime, prorated
- **Cancellation:** 30-day notice, no early termination fees on month-to-month
- **Annual prepay discount:** 10% off list when paid 12 months in advance

## Volume pricing

| Cameras | Standard | Pro |
|---|---|---|
| 1-49 | $39 | $69 |
| 50-149 | $35 | $62 |
| 150-499 | $32 | $56 |
| 500+ | Enterprise | Enterprise |

Volume tiers apply across a single billed entity. Multi-entity arrangements (parent company with subsidiaries) are quoted at the consolidated count.

faq.q: Can I use my own cameras?
faq.a: Yes. The VDS platform is camera-agnostic — any ONVIF Profile-S/T camera works. We support most major brands and have documented integrations for Axis, Hanwha, Avigilon, Bosch, and others.

faq.q: What if I'm on Standard and want one Pro feature?
faq.a: Upgrade the whole site to Pro. There's no per-feature unlock — the analytics pipeline runs site-wide.

faq.q: Is there a free trial?
faq.a: Yes, 14 days on Standard or Pro for new customers, on up to 4 cameras. Enterprise has a structured proof-of-concept program instead.

faq.q: Where is video stored?
faq.a: AWS US-East and US-West, depending on customer region. Enterprise customers can request specific regions. We're an AWS Partner Network member.

faq.q: Do I get a price increase notice?
faq.a: Yes. Existing customers get 90 days' notice on any list price change, with the option to lock the prior price for an additional 12 months at signing.

finalCTAHeading: Pick a plan
finalCTABody: Start with Standard or Pro, change tiers any time, cancel any month. Enterprise customers, talk to sales.
notes: Pricing transparency on platform tiers is the strongest differentiator vs Verkada/Eagle Eye. Lead with the comparison.

body:
## Trailers do not fail. Mounts, batteries, and signage do.

Seven years of deployments tell us where field failures actually come from. The camera works. The cloud works. The unit gets clipped by a forklift, the battery cycles past 1,500 charges, or somebody steals the signage. This catalog is the parts that fix those problems before they become a service call.

## Catalog

**Anti-tamper kits.** Tamper-evident enclosures, lock upgrades, GPS tracking for mobile units, vibration alerting.

**Additional batteries.** Battery bank upgrades for sites with shading, high cellular draw, or extreme cold cycles.

**LPR add-on.** Retrofit LPR onto Swift Deploy and Solar Pole units. 95%+ accuracy, sub-3-second alerts.

**Signage.** Warning, surveillance, and trespass signage — printed, posted, and rated for outdoor multi-year exposure.

**K-rail and barrier mounts.** Mount cameras and lights to concrete K-rail without trenching or core drilling.

**Cellular and Starlink upgrades.** Backhaul redundancy and Starlink kits for remote sites.

**Spare parts.** Camera modules, mast hardware, solar panels, charge controllers, replacement panels. Same-week shipping from Pikesville, MD.

## How accessories integrate

Every add-on is built for the same AI VisionStream and SOC pipeline as the base unit. LPR retrofitted to a Swift Deploy reports to the same audit log as a Sky Guard's factory LPR. Anti-tamper triggers route through the same SOC operators.

faq.q: Can I retrofit LPR onto a Swift Deploy I already have?
faq.a: Yes. Factory and field-retrofit LPR perform to the same 95%+ accuracy and sub-3-second alert spec.

faq.q: Do you ship parts to customers who do not run a VDS lease?
faq.a: Yes — we sell parts and accessories to the broader market. Compatibility documentation provided on request.

faq.q: How fast do spares ship?
faq.a: Same-week from Pikesville for in-stock items. Critical-path items can ship next-day on request.

faq.q: Are the anti-tamper kits NDAA compliant?
faq.a: Yes. All VDS accessories are Section 889 compliant.

seoTitle: Boundary Guard Pro — 500ft Fence Line Coverage | VDS
metaDescription: 500+ linear feet of perimeter coverage with no blind spots. Solar-autonomous, AI analytics, US SOC monitoring. From $1,800/mo.
announcementBar: NDAA compliant. Assembled in Pikesville, MD.
h1: Boundary Guard Pro. 500+ feet of fence line, no blind spots.
heroSubhead: A single PTZ leaves gaps along long fence lines. Boundary Guard Pro is engineered for linear perimeters — 500+ feet of overlapping coverage from one solar-autonomous unit. From $1,800/mo.
body:
## Most trailers solve a point. This one solves a line.

A PTZ trailer is excellent at covering one location and useless at covering a 600ft fence line. Operators have to pan to a problem after motion is already in progress. By the time the camera is on the intruder, the intruder is at the fence.

Boundary Guard Pro is built around overlapping fixed sensors plus PTZ for verification. The whole fence is in frame the whole time. Motion triggers the right sensor; PTZ snaps to the event for high-detail capture and SOC verification.

## How the coverage works

- **Multi-sensor array** covers 500+ linear feet without gaps
- **Overlapping fields** mean intrusion at any point along the line triggers verified detection within seconds
- **PTZ verification** auto-cues to the alerted sensor
- **AI analytics** filter wildlife, weather, and vehicle pass-bys

## Power and form factor

- Solar-autonomous, multi-day battery reserve
- IP66 enclosure
- -20F to 120F operating range
- Dual-SIM cellular backhaul
- AI VisionStream integration standard
- ONVIF/RTSP compliant

## Pricing

- Lease: from **$1,800/mo** including AI VisionStream
- SOC monitoring optional, priced per unit
- Multi-unit and multi-month discounts available

## Where it earns its keep

Long construction fence lines. Material yards. Solar farm perimeters. Utility substations. Quarries. Logistics yards. Anywhere "we need to watch the whole fence, not just the gate" is the requirement.

A typical 1,000ft perimeter runs two Boundary Guard Pro units for full coverage. A 2,000ft perimeter runs three units staggered. We will scope it.

faq.q: Why not just put two Swift Deploy trailers along a fence?
faq.a: You can, and many customers do. Two Swift Deploy units cover the line but leave coverage gaps between them. Boundary Guard Pro covers the line continuously from a single unit, with PTZ verification on each event. Lower per-foot cost on long perimeters.

faq.q: Can I run Boundary Guard alongside Sky Guard MSU?
faq.a: Yes. Common pattern: Sky Guard on the high-value gate or yard with thermal and radar, Boundary Guard on the long fence runs. Both feed the same AI VisionStream and SOC.

faq.q: How is detection different from a typical PIR or motion sensor fence?
faq.a: Camera-based detection with AI classifiers means an alert comes with video evidence and is filtered for wildlife and vegetation. PIR fences alarm on everything; this alarms on what matters.

faq.q: Does the SOC monitor all 500 feet?
faq.a: Yes. Every alerted segment triggers an operator review with video. Live audio challenge through PA on the unit. 97% false alarm reduction.

finalCTAHeading: Spec a perimeter quote.
finalCTABody: Send us your fence line length and threat profile. We will scope unit count and pricing in 24 hours.

h1: Guard booths built for the climate and the threat profile.
heroSubhead: Heavy-gauge steel construction, HVAC standard, bullet-resistant options available. Use them manned, unmanned with VDS hardware, or both.

h1: License Plate Recognition Cameras for Accurate Vehicle Identification
heroSubhead: A purpose-built LPR camera, the VDS platform, and SOC verification — packaged as one buyable system. 95%+ first-pass read accuracy at vehicle speeds up to 50 mph.
body:
License plate recognition cameras help commercial teams identify vehicles automatically, trigger alerts for plates of interest, and generate searchable reporting for investigations, access control, and operational oversight.

Unlike general surveillance cameras, LPR systems are only valuable when they produce two outcomes consistently: readable plate captures and a workflow that turns plate data into action.



## What License Plate Recognition Cameras Do

License Plate Recognition (LPR) is a surveillance capability that captures a vehicle’s license plate, converts the plate image into text, and makes that information usable for search, alerting, and reporting.

Organizations use LPR cameras to:

Log vehicles entering or exiting a location

Alert on watchlists (authorized vs unauthorized plates)

Support investigations with time-stamped evidence

Reduce manual gatehouse/security checks

Improve site accountability across multiple locations

When buyers search “LPR camera,” “license plate camera,” or “automatic license plate reader,” they’re typically trying to solve one of these problems:

“We need to know which vehicles are on-site and when”

“We need fast alerts for unauthorized or repeat offender vehicles”

“We need evidence we can retrieve quickly without reviewing hours of footage”



## How License Plate Recognition Works

A commercial LPR system usually follows a simple workflow:

Capture At A Predictable Point

The camera captures plates at entrances/exits or chokepoints where vehicle movement is consistent.

Optimize The Plate Image

Settings (exposure, shutter speed) and lighting determine whether the plate is readable.

Ocr Reads The Characters

Optical Character Recognition converts the plate image into searchable text.

Match Against Lists Or Filters

Plates can be checked against allow/deny lists, hotlists, or operational filters.

Trigger Alerts And Generate Reports

Alerts notify the right team; reports document the event with time, location, and associated video.



## What Data Can LPR Capture (and What It Can’t)

LPR is most valuable when expectations are clear. A properly configured deployment can capture reliable “plate events” that are searchable, reportable, and usable for alerts. But performance depends on placement, lighting, vehicle speed, and the platform package you deploy.



### What LPR Can Capture

Plate number (core output)

Plate image (evidence snapshot for verification)

Timestamp (date/time of the plate event)

Location context (site, lane/entry point, or camera name)

Camera/device ID (useful for multi-site reporting and audits)

Event history (searchable plate reads across time and locations)



### Alerts, Watchlists, and Operational Workflows

Watchlists (allowlist/denylist or “plates of interest”)

Real-time alerts when a watchlisted plate is detected

Search and reporting (full or partial plate searches, filters by date/time and location)

Evidence-ready exports (plate event + related images/clips, based on retention settings)



### Optional Vehicle Attributes

Direction of travel (in/out, lane direction)

Vehicle type/classification (e.g., car vs truck)

Make/model/color (available in some deployments depending on platform + analytics package; validate per configuration)



### What LPR Can’t Reliably Capture

Plates that aren’t visible (mud, damage, obstructions, plate covers, bike racks, trailers)

Consistent reads at extreme angles or long distances

Reliable reads in poor lighting without proper setup (headlight glare, backlighting, low-light corners)

High-speed reads in uncontrolled lanes without the right angle/settings

Driver identity (LPR identifies vehicles via plates, not people)

Perfect accuracy in every condition (read rate depends on environment and configuration)



### How to Improve Data Quality: Quick Requirements Checklist

Define the capture point (entrances/exits or chokepoints with predictable movement)

Control angles and distance (ensure the plate is large enough in-frame to read)

Design for night performance (plate readability, not just “a visible scene”)

Define what happens on a match (who gets alerted, escalation steps, reporting)

Confirm retention needs (how long plate events and related footage must be stored)



## LPR Camera Accuracy Requirements

If you want LPR to work in real conditions, this is the section that matters most. Most underperforming LPR deployments fail for predictable reasons: bad angles, uncontrolled lighting, or plates too small in frame.



### Placement and angle

LPR works best at chokepoints:

Entry and exit lanes

Gate approaches

Yard access points

Drive lanes that naturally slow vehicles

Why it matters: plates need to be large enough in-frame and captured at a usable angle. Wide “overview” placement is great for context, but it often fails for consistent plate capture.



### Vehicle speed and distance

Speed changes the capture requirements:

Faster vehicles need tighter placement and settings designed to reduce motion blur.

Longer capture distances make plates too small and reduce OCR reliability.

If you can control speed at entry points, LPR success rates typically improve significantly.



### Lighting and nighttime performance

Night is where LPR projects win or lose. Common failure modes include:

Headlight glare washing out plate detail

Underexposure in poorly lit lanes

High contrast scenes (bright fixtures + dark shadows)

LPR cameras often require purpose-built lighting and careful placement to preserve detail at night.

Camera settings (shutter and exposure)

Even high-end cameras can fail if settings are wrong:

Shutter too slow = motion blur

Exposure too bright = reflective plate washout

Exposure too dark = unreadable characters

For a more in-depth guide, explore the perfect setting guide for license plate recognition cameras.



## Where LPR Cameras Work Best

LPR produces the best ROI when vehicles must pass through predictable paths and when there’s a clear outcome tied to plate capture.



### Parking And Access Control

Use LPR to:

Log entry/exit events automatically

Alert on unauthorized plates

Support enforcement and dispute resolution

Reduce manual checks and friction at gates



### Logistics Yards And Warehouses

Use LPR to:

Track truck movements and timestamps

Verify deliveries and departures

Improve perimeter accountability

Support investigations after incidents



### Construction sites and temporary operations

Use LPR to:

Log vehicles entering and exiting job sites

Identify repeat unauthorized vehicles

Support incident timelines when theft occurs

Improve oversight across multiple projects

If you’re deploying security quickly on changing sites, LPR is commonly paired with mobile surveillance trailers.



### Municipal and Public Safety Applications

Use LPR for:

Vehicle-of-interest alerting

Corridor-based monitoring where fixed infrastructure exists

Evidence support for investigations and public safety initiatives



## Alerts, Watchlists, and Reporting Workflows

LPR becomes operationally valuable when alerts and reporting are defined.

A practical LPR workflow answers:

What triggers an alert (watchlist hit, time window, location rule)?

Who is notified (security, property manager, dispatch, law enforcement liaison)?

What is the escalation path (verify → notify → respond → report)?

What report is generated (plate, timestamp, camera/location, associated video)?

If you need verified response and standardized reporting across sites, LPR is often paired with remote video surveillance monitoring.



## LPR Deployment Options: Fixed, Mobile, or Hybri

Buyers typically choose one of three approaches:



### Fixed LPR installations

Best for:

Permanent facilities

Controlled entry/exit lanes

Stable lighting and infrastructure



### Mobile LPR deployments

Best for:

Temporary risk periods

Construction sites that change weekly

Locations without ready infrastructure

Fast deployment needs after incidents

Internal link: mobile surveillance trailers → /products/mobile-surveillance-trailers/



### Hybrid approach

Common in the field:

Use mobile deployments immediately for rapid coverage

Transition to fixed infrastructure once the site stabilizes

Keep workflows and reporting consistent across both



## What Affects Pricing and Scope

Pricing and scope depend on how you plan to use LPR. Key factors include:

Number of capture points (entrances, exits, chokepoints)

Vehicle speed and lane design (affects placement and settings)

Lighting requirements (night performance is a major driver)

Alerting and monitoring requirements (hours covered, escalation, reporting)

Data retention expectations (how long records must be stored)

Multi-site needs (standardization, permissions, centralized reporting)

Procurement model also matters. Many organizations compare:

Purchase (long-term ownership)

Lease (capex vs opex flexibility)

Rental (short-term or temporary risk periods)



## License Plate Recognition Camera FAQs

What is the difference between an LPR camera and an LPR system?

An LPR camera captures plate images. An LPR system includes the camera plus OCR software, searchable history, alerts/watchlists, and reporting workflows.

What affects license plate recognition accuracy the most?

Placement at chokepoints, vehicle speed, lighting (especially at night), and correct shutter/exposure settings are the biggest drivers of accuracy.

Can LPR work at night?

Yes, but nighttime performance depends on glare control, lighting design, and settings that preserve plate detail without washout.

Where should LPR cameras be installed for best results?

Entrances, exits, and lanes where vehicles slow down are the most reliable capture locations.

Can LPR trigger alerts for unauthorized vehicles?

Yes. Most commercial systems can run watchlists (authorized vs unauthorized plates) and generate alerts based on site rules.

Can LPR be deployed on mobile surveillance trailers?

Yes. LPR is commonly paired with rapid deployment platforms for construction sites, temporary risk periods, and locations without ready infrastructure.

MAKE THESE TESTIMONIALS SPECIFIC TO THE MOBILE SURVEILLANCE PRODUCT



## Protect Every Vehicle Entry—With Real-Time LPR Alerts.

Get an LPR solution that captures plates reliably at entrances and chokepoints, flags vehicles of interest, and creates searchable reports your team can act on—day or night.

faq.a: Yes, but accuracy will be camera-dependent. We support LPR on any ONVIF Profile-S camera through the platform. If you want the 95%+ accuracy numbers, use the purpose-built LPR camera.

faq.q: How many lanes does a typical site need?
faq.a: One per direction of travel you want to capture. A two-way driveway is two lanes. A four-bay loading dock is typically two to four lanes depending on geometry.

faq.q: Does the system store driver images?
faq.a: The LPR camera captures the plate, not the driver. If you want driver capture, pair LPR with a standard overview camera; the platform correlates the two streams.

faq.q: Is there a public records / FOIA concern?
faq.a: For private commercial customers, plate data is private business data. For public-sector customers, plate data may be subject to state public records laws — we configure retention and access accordingly, and provide documentation for compliance review.

body:
Remote surveillance trailer solutions give teams fast, flexible site security coverage without waiting on permanent installation. If you need to deter theft, document incidents, and improve response on a temporary or changing site, a mobile surveillance trailer provides rapid deployment coverage paired with platform visibility and optional remote monitoring.



## What is a Remote Surveillance Trailer?

A remote surveillance trailer is a mobile, deployable security system designed to provide camera coverage where permanent infrastructure isn’t practical—or where speed matters most. It typically supports:

Fast site coverage without permanent installation

Operation across varying site conditions

Centralized access through a cloud platform

Optional monitoring and alert workflows depending on the deployment model



## Remote Surveillance Trailer vs Mobile Security Trailer

Buyers often use “mobile security trailer” and “remote surveillance trailer” interchangeably. In practice:

Remote surveillance trailer emphasizes access, visibility, and remote operations.

Mobile security trailer emphasizes deterrence and rapid deployment for site protection. If your risk is after-hours access, repeated theft, or temporary high exposure, a trailer solution is often the fastest path to meaningful coverage.



## Key Features of Our Mobile Surveillance Trailers



### Rapid Deployment for Temporary or Evolving Sites

Secure construction phases, parking lots, events, and incident response without waiting on permanent installs.



### Solar-powered with Battery Backup for Off-grid Coverage

Maintain continuous monitoring in remote locations and power-limited sites.



### 4G/5G Connectivity for Instant, Wireless Operation

Get video access and alerts without relying on site Wi-Fi—ideal for remote jobsites.



### Built-in Compatibility with VisionStream and AI Analytics

Centralize visibility, alerts, and reporting—then layer analytics to reduce noise and speed response.



### Modular Designs for Flexible Configurations

Choose camera packages and accessories based on your risk—scale from one site to multi-location coverage.



## Where Mobile Surveillance Trailers Work Best



### Construction Sites

Construction sites change weekly, and risk often spikes during early phases and after-hours. A trailer provides fast coverage for equipment, perimeters, and access points without slowing progress.

Best-fit outcomes:

Deter theft and unauthorized entry

Document incidents with usable evidence

Support site oversight across multiple projects



### Parking Lots and Shopping Centers

Parking lots are large, exposed environments where visibility and response matter. Trailers help cover drive lanes, entrances, and high-risk zones, especially during peak periods or elevated risk.

Best-fit outcomes:

Reduce vandalism and vehicle-related incidents

Improve visibility in low-coverage areas

Support retail and property operations with faster incident review

Support perimeter coverage
