body:
## Quick answers about mobile surveillance, AI video, and VDS

Every answer below is sourced from VDS field operations across 30+ states and 500+ active deployments. If you don't see your question, [request a quote](/request-a-quote) and a VDS specialist will respond within one business hour.

## Products & Pricing

### How much does a mobile surveillance trailer cost?

VDS mobile surveillance trailers rent from $1,500 to $2,200 per month depending on configuration. Purchase prices start at $38,000 for the Sky Guard MSU. Pricing includes the trailer, AI VisionStream platform access, and the option to add 24/7 SOC monitoring at $399 per site per month.

### What is the difference between the Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, and Boundary Guard Pro?

Sky Guard MSU ($2,200/mo) is the flagship — thermal LWIR, 500ft ground radar, 4K cameras, LPR, and active deterrence in one solar-autonomous unit. Swift Deploy ($1,500/mo) is the most popular — HD PTZ with 30x zoom, deploys in under 20 minutes by one person. Boundary Guard Pro ($1,800/mo) covers 500+ linear feet of fence-line with no blind spots.

### Do you offer rental or only purchase?

Both. Rentals start at $1,500 per month with a 3-month minimum term. Purchase pricing for the Sky Guard MSU starts at $38,000. Most customers start with rental and switch to purchase after 24+ months of operation.

### How long is the minimum rental term?

Three months for standard rental. We offer shorter terms (1-2 months) for events and seasonal use, priced per-week.

### What does the monthly rental include?

Trailer hardware, AI VisionStream platform access (cloud VMS, AI analytics, mobile app), 30-day cloud storage, cellular connectivity, and standard tech support. The 24/7 SOC monitoring is a $399/site/mo add-on.

### Is there a setup fee or installation charge?

There is no setup fee for rentals. We include site survey, transport, install, and decommission in the rental price within our 30-state service area. Out-of-area deployments may include logistics costs.

## Deployment & Operations

### How fast can VDS deploy to my site?

Most sites are operational within 72 hours of contract signing in our 30-state service area. Same-day or 24-hour deployment is available in the MD/DC/N. VA region from our Pikesville HQ. The trailer itself sets up in under 20 minutes by one person with no tools.

### Do I need power or internet at the site?

No. VDS trailers are solar-autonomous with 36-48+ hour battery backup. Connectivity is via multi-carrier cellular (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, FirstNet) with optional Starlink satellite failover for remote sites.

### How many cameras come on each trailer?

Sky Guard MSU: 4K multi-sensor camera (multiple lenses) + LWIR thermal + radar. Swift Deploy: HD PTZ with 30x optical zoom, dual-spectrum night vision. Boundary Guard Pro: multi-camera linear configuration covering 500+ linear feet.

### What happens if a trailer is vandalized or stolen?

Active deterrence (strobes, audio talk-down) is triggered before damage. Tamper sensors alert the SOC. GPS tracking on every unit. Insurance is included in rental; purchase customers add a comprehensive policy.

### Can the trailer move with the project?

Yes. Trailers are designed for redeployment. We handle the move logistics in-house. Typical redeployment within 24-72 hours of request.

### How long is the battery autonomy on cloudy days?

Sky Guard MSU: 48+ hours. Swift Deploy: 36+ hours. Both rated to -20°F and 120°F. In extended cloudy conditions, optional grid hookup, generator, or fuel cell can supplement solar.

## AI VisionStream Platform

### What is AI VisionStream?

AI VisionStream is VDS's cloud video management system (VMS). It ingests video from VDS trailers and any third-party ONVIF/RTSP camera, runs AI analytics (intrusion zones, virtual tripwires, loitering, crowd, LPR, time-of-day rules), and routes alerts to your team or our 24/7 US SOC. Hosted on AWS US-only data residency.

### Does VDS work with the cameras I already have?

Yes. AI VisionStream is camera-agnostic and supports any ONVIF/RTSP camera (Axis, Hanwha, Bosch, etc.). We do not support Dahua or Hikvision because they are restricted under NDAA Section 889.

### Where is video stored?

AWS US-only data residency. TLS 1.3 in transit. AES-256 at rest. Retention tiers: 30-day, 60-day, or 90-day. Immutable 12-month audit log of all platform access.

### What is the accuracy of the LPR system?

95%+ plate read accuracy under standard conditions, with sub-3-second alerts on hotlist matches. Day/night, multi-angle, and weather-tolerant.

### Is there a mobile app?

Yes. iOS and Android. Live multi-camera view, alert acknowledgement, two-way audio talk-down through the trailer PA, and incident clip sharing.

### Does VDS integrate with my existing access control or alarm system?

Yes. Integrations available for Lenel, Genetec, Brivo, Bold, Stages, ServiceNow, Jira, PagerDuty, Slack, and standard webhooks. Custom API available.

## 24/7 SOC Monitoring

### What is the SOC response time?

Under 60 seconds from alert to operator acknowledgement. AI pre-filtering reduces false alarms by 97%. Confirmed threats trigger audio talk-down through the trailer PA and direct law enforcement dispatch with live video shared.

### Is the SOC staffed by US-based operators?

Yes. 100% US-based, in-house operators. No overseas outsourcing. The SOC is staffed 24/7/365.

### What happens after an alert?

Operator verifies via live video. Triggers audio talk-down (a recorded or live voice through the trailer PA). If the threat persists, operator dispatches law enforcement with live video stream. A full incident report is filed for every event with timestamps, video clips, and operator actions.

### Can my team monitor instead of using the VDS SOC?

Yes. The platform includes a SOC console for your security team. Many customers run a hybrid model — their team handles business-hours, VDS SOC covers nights and weekends.

## Compliance & Trust

### Is VDS NDAA Section 889 compliant?

Yes. All VDS hardware is NDAA Section 889 compliant, assembled in Pikesville, MD. We do not use Dahua or Hikvision components. Compliance documentation is available on request for federal, utility, and state procurement.

### Do you have SOC 2 certification?

SOC 2 Type II audit is in progress. Target completion: late 2026. Current security posture: AWS Cloud Partner with US-only data residency, TLS 1.3, AES-256 at rest, RBAC with MFA, immutable 12-month audit log.

### Is the data ever sold or shared with third parties?

No. Customer data is never sold. Footage is not shared with third parties (including law enforcement) without your authorization. Each customer's data is isolated; we do not pool customer data into a public network.

### Is VDS available on Sourcewell, GSA, or other cooperative purchasing contracts?

Yes. VDS is available through Sourcewell. GSA Schedule pending. State contracts available in MD, VA, TX, FL, PA (COSTARS). Contact procurement@visiondetectionsystems.com for cooperative purchasing inquiries.

## Industries

### Does VDS work for construction sites?

Yes. Construction is VDS's largest industry. The hero case study: a $28M Mid-Atlantic project saved $340,800 in 12 months using 2 Swift Deploy trailers + 3 Solar Camera Poles — 73% theft reduction, zero insurance claims.

### Can VDS protect utility substations and meet NERC CIP-014?

Yes. Sky Guard MSU is configured for substation deployment with thermal LWIR + radar + 4K cameras + LPR. NDAA Section 889 compliance and immutable audit log support NERC CIP-014 documentation requirements.

### Do you serve retailers facing organized retail crime (ORC)?

Yes. We deploy Swift Deploy trailers in retail parking lots with LPR to capture getaway vehicle plates. NRF reports 18% YoY shoplifting growth with 67% of retailers identifying transnational ORC group involvement since 2024.

### Is VDS appropriate for municipal or government use?

Yes — for private-property and government-facility security (parks, motor pools, public works yards, evidence storage exteriors). VDS is not a Flock-style public-surveillance ALPR network — we secure your facilities, not citizen movement.

### Do you support events and short-term deployments?

Yes. Festival, concert, parking, and vendor-village deployments from 3 days to 3 months. Per-week pricing available. Hurricane-season redeployment is a common Florida/Texas use case — pull off-site before the storm, redeploy after.

## Comparisons

### How is VDS different from LVT (LiveView Technologies)?

VDS is camera-agnostic; LVT is hardware-locked. Bring your own cameras and the AI VisionStream platform integrates them. VDS pricing is transparent; LVT charges $38K-$52K plus mandatory cloud subscription. VDS is built in the US in Pikesville, MD.

### How is VDS different from Flock Safety?

VDS is private-property security. Flock is community-network ALPR. Your VDS cameras stream to your account on AWS US-only — never to a national fusion network. Reference January 2026 Flock public camera exposure event affecting 67 cameras.

### How is VDS different from Verkada?

VDS is camera-agnostic and includes outdoor solar-autonomous hardware Verkada does not make. VDS includes a 24/7 in-house SOC. Verkada hardware is locked-in with $199-$1,799 per camera per year license fees.

### How is VDS different from Pro-Vigil or Stealth Monitoring?

Pro-Vigil and Stealth (now ECAM) are monitoring services. VDS owns the hardware, the AI platform, and the SOC end-to-end. Single-vendor accountability across the entire surveillance stack.

### Is VDS cheaper than security guards?

Yes. A single 24/7 guard FTE costs $60,000-$110,000 per year in 2026. A VDS Sky Guard MSU plus SOC is approximately $31,000 per year — and the trailer captures evidence guards do not. Documented ROI: a $28M Mid-Atlantic GC cut security costs from $32,400/mo to $4,000/mo.

### What is the difference between mobile surveillance trailers and fixed cameras?

Fixed cameras are wired, permanent, and require power + network. Mobile trailers are solar-autonomous, redeployable, and operational in under 20 minutes. For project-based sites (construction, events), trailers eliminate install lead-times and follow the work.

h1: Mobile Surveillance & AI Video Glossary
heroSubhead: Sixty-plus definitions covering the language of mobile surveillance trailers, AI video analytics, compliance frameworks, and security operations.
body:
## A definitive glossary of mobile surveillance and AI video security

From NDAA Section 889 to ONVIF and LPR — the terms below define the language of modern site security. Use this glossary to navigate VDS documentation, RFP responses, and procurement conversations.

Bookmark this page or [request a quote](/request-a-quote) to talk to a specialist who speaks every term below in plain English.

## A

### ALPR / Automatic License Plate Recognition

Same technology as LPR. Cameras with optical character recognition that read license plates in real time and compare against a hotlist database. VDS uses LPR with 95%+ accuracy and sub-3-second alerts.

### Audio Talk-Down

A live or recorded voice broadcast through a trailer's PA speaker when a threat is detected. Used by SOC operators to challenge intruders before law enforcement arrives. A core component of active deterrence.

### AES-256

Advanced Encryption Standard with a 256-bit key. The encryption used by VDS for all video and metadata stored at rest. Industry standard for federal and financial-sector data.

### AWS / Amazon Web Services

Cloud computing platform hosting AI VisionStream. VDS uses US-only AWS regions for data residency. VDS is an AWS Cloud Partner.

## B

### BIPA / Biometric Information Privacy Act

Illinois law (2008) governing biometric data collection. VDS does not use facial recognition or biometric matching, so VDS deployments are BIPA-friendly in Illinois.

### Boundary Guard Pro

A VDS fence-line surveillance unit covering 500+ linear feet with no blind spots. Multi-camera configuration. Starting at $1,800/mo.

## C

### Camera-Agnostic

The ability for a video management system (VMS) to accept video from cameras made by any manufacturer that supports the ONVIF or RTSP open standards. AI VisionStream is camera-agnostic — use VDS cameras or any ONVIF/RTSP camera you already own.

### Cargo Theft

Theft of goods in transit or in storage. US logistics industry loses over $15 billion per year to cargo theft. Hot spots: ports, distribution centers, truck yards.

### Catalytic Converter Theft

Theft of catalytic converters from vehicles for the precious metals inside (platinum, palladium, rhodium). Rhodium hit $10,400/oz in 2026. State Farm catalytic converter claims peaked at 45,000 in 2022.

### Cellular Failover

Multi-carrier cellular connectivity (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile, FirstNet) that automatically switches to the strongest available signal. VDS trailers also support optional Starlink satellite failover for remote sites.

### Chain of Custody

Documented trail proving who has accessed video evidence, when, and what they did with it. VDS provides an immutable 12-month audit log for every event.

### Construction Theft

Theft of materials, equipment, and copper from active construction sites. The FBI estimates US construction theft exceeds $1 billion per year, and less than 7% of stolen equipment is ever recovered.

### Copper Theft

Theft of copper wire, pipe, and grounding from construction sites, substations, and abandoned buildings. Driven by copper commodity prices. A common VDS use case for utilities.

### CCPA / California Consumer Privacy Act

California law (2018) granting consumers data privacy rights. VDS deployments respect CCPA: customer data is not sold and is isolated per customer.

## D

### Device Health Monitoring

Proactive monitoring of trailer battery state, solar input, cellular signal, camera uptime, and tamper sensors. VDS alerts before failure rather than after.

### DVR / Digital Video Recorder

Older on-site recording device using analog cameras. Largely replaced by NVRs and cloud VMS. VDS does not use DVRs.

## E

### E-E-A-T

Google's Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness rating framework. Used in Search Quality Rater Guidelines and AEO models.

### Edge Computing

Running AI analytics on the camera or trailer (the 'edge') rather than uploading raw video to the cloud. Lower bandwidth use, faster alerts. VDS uses edge analytics on Sky Guard MSU and Swift Deploy.

## F

### False Alarm

An alert triggered by a non-threat (wildlife, weather, headlights, shadows). VDS AI VisionStream filters 97% of false alarms before they reach a SOC operator.

### FERPA

Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act. US federal law protecting student education records. VDS deployments on K-12 and higher-ed campuses respect FERPA — exterior-only surveillance, no classroom interior.

### Fisheye Camera

A wide-angle camera with a 360-degree horizontal field of view. Used for area surveillance where a single camera covers a parking lot or open yard.

## G

### GSA Schedule

General Services Administration purchasing contract used by federal agencies. VDS GSA Schedule is pending.

## H

### HIPAA

Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act. US health data privacy law. VDS deployments at healthcare facilities are exterior-only (parking lots, ER approaches, behavioral health perimeter); no clinical interior monitoring.

## I

### IP66

Ingress Protection rating: 6 = totally dust-tight, 6 = protected against powerful water jets. VDS hardware is rated IP66 for outdoor durability.

### Intrusion Zone

A virtual perimeter drawn on the camera view. Triggers an alert when a person or vehicle crosses into it. Configurable by time of day.

## L

### LPR / License Plate Recognition

Camera-based OCR reading of vehicle license plates. VDS LPR achieves 95%+ accuracy with sub-3-second alerts on hotlist matches. Used in construction, retail, auto dealers, and parking.

### Loitering Detection

AI analytic that alerts when a person or vehicle stays in an area longer than a configured threshold. Useful for parking lots and storefronts.

### LWIR / Long-Wave Infrared

Thermal imaging in the 8-14 micrometer range. Detects heat from bodies and vehicles in total darkness and through smoke or light fog. Standard on the Sky Guard MSU.

## M

### MFA / Multi-Factor Authentication

Login security requiring a second factor beyond a password (typically a code from a phone or hardware token). Required for all AI VisionStream user accounts.

### MSU / Mobile Surveillance Unit

Industry term for a self-contained surveillance unit (typically trailer-mounted, solar-powered) deployable to any site. VDS Sky Guard MSU is the flagship MSU.

## N

### NDAA Section 889

Section 889 of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019. Prohibits federal agencies and contractors from using video surveillance gear from named Chinese manufacturers (Dahua, Hikvision, Hytera, Huawei, ZTE). VDS hardware is NDAA Section 889 compliant.

### NERC CIP-014

North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection Standard 014 — physical security requirements for high-impact transmission substations. VDS Sky Guard MSU is configured to support NERC CIP-014 documentation requirements.

### NVR / Network Video Recorder

On-site recording device using IP cameras. Largely being replaced by cloud VMS. VDS does not require NVRs — the AI VisionStream cloud VMS is the system of record.

## O

### ONVIF

Open Network Video Interface Forum. The open standard that lets IP cameras from different manufacturers work with the same VMS. VDS AI VisionStream supports any ONVIF camera.

### Open Graph (OG)

Meta tag protocol used by Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack, and others to control how a page appears when shared. Every VDS page includes OG title, description, image, and type.

### ORC / Organized Retail Crime

Coordinated theft of retail goods by groups for resale, often involving flash-mob smash-and-grab events. NRF reports 18% YoY growth and 67% of retailers reporting transnational ORC involvement since 2024.

## P

### Pikesville, MD

VDS headquarters and assembly facility. Located in the Baltimore-DC metro area. All VDS hardware is assembled at the Pikesville plant.

### PTZ / Pan-Tilt-Zoom Camera

A motorized camera that can pan, tilt, and zoom remotely. The Swift Deploy trailer uses a PTZ with 30x optical zoom.

## R

### RBAC / Role-Based Access Control

User permission model where access is determined by role (e.g., Admin, Operator, Viewer). VDS AI VisionStream enforces RBAC on every account.

### Remote Video Monitoring (RVM)

Service in which trained operators watch live camera feeds remotely and respond to events. VDS RVM is delivered by a 24/7 in-house US-based SOC.

### Robots.txt

Plain-text file at the root of a website that tells search engine crawlers which URLs to crawl or skip. VDS robots.txt allows all primary pages and points to the XML sitemap.

### RTSP / Real-Time Streaming Protocol

Open protocol for streaming video from IP cameras. VDS AI VisionStream supports RTSP ingest from third-party cameras.

## S

### Schema.org

Standardized vocabulary for structured data on web pages. VDS uses Schema.org markup (Organization, Product, Article, FAQPage, LocalBusiness, etc.) for SEO and AEO.

### Sky Guard MSU

VDS flagship mobile surveillance unit. Combines LWIR thermal, 500ft ground radar, 4K multi-sensor cameras, LPR, and active deterrence in one solar-autonomous trailer. From $2,200/mo or $38,000 purchase.

### SOC / Security Operations Center

Staffed facility that monitors security events 24/7/365. VDS SOC is US-based, in-house, with under 60-second escalation and 97% false alarm reduction.

### SOC 2 / SOC 2 Type II

Service Organization Control 2 audit framework for service providers handling customer data. Evaluates security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy. VDS SOC 2 Type II audit is in progress.

### Solar-Autonomous

Powered entirely by solar panels with battery backup. No grid hookup or generator required for normal operation. VDS Sky Guard MSU has 600W solar input + 48+ hour battery autonomy.

### Sourcewell

Cooperative purchasing contract used by government agencies. VDS is available on Sourcewell.

### Speakable Schema

Schema.org property identifying the parts of a page voice assistants and answer engines should read aloud. A key AEO signal.

### Swift Deploy Trailer

VDS's most popular mobile surveillance trailer. HD PTZ with 30x zoom, dual-spectrum night vision, deploys in under 20 minutes by one person, no tools. From $1,500/mo.

## T

### TLS 1.3

Transport Layer Security version 1.3 — the encryption protocol used for AI VisionStream data in transit. Industry standard for modern web traffic.

### Time-of-Day Rules

AI VisionStream feature that applies different detection rules during configurable time windows. Example: an after-hours zone armed 6pm-6am triggers alerts immediately; the same zone is permissive during business hours.

## V

### Virtual Tripwire

AI analytic that triggers an alert when an object crosses a virtual line drawn on the camera view. Directional (e.g., entering only) or bidirectional.

### VMS / Video Management System

Software that ingests, stores, and surfaces video from cameras. AI VisionStream is a cloud VMS — no on-site DVR or NVR required.

## W

### WCAG / Web Content Accessibility Guidelines

W3C accessibility standard. VDS targets WCAG 2.1 AA — color contrast ≥4.5:1, keyboard navigation, alt text on images, captions on video.

body:
## Why this comparison matters

"Mobile surveillance" is a fragmented category. Buyers searching for a trailer or a remote-monitoring contract land on at least three different product types: solar-autonomous mobile surveillance units (MSUs), enterprise cloud VMS platforms, and managed remote video monitoring (RVM) services. Some vendors sell one. A few sell two. One sells all three under one roof.

This page is written by Vision Detection Systems. We are on the list. We disclose that up front. Where a competitor genuinely wins on a dimension, we say so.

Evaluation criteria, weighted in this order:

1. **Owns the hardware** — designs and builds the mobile unit, not just resells it.
2. **AI platform** — proprietary VMS with analytics (LPR, person/vehicle, intrusion), camera-agnostic via ONVIF/RTSP.
3. **24/7 US Security Operations Center** — in-house human operators, not outsourced abroad.
4. **NDAA Section 889 compliance** — no Hikvision/Dahua components, federal-eligible.
5. **US-only AWS data residency** — encrypted at rest (AES-256), TLS 1.3 in transit, US AWS regions only.
6. **Pricing transparency** — published starting price on the website.

## The comparison matrix

| Vendor | Owns Hardware | AI Platform | 24/7 US SOC | NDAA 889 | US-Only Data | Pricing Published | Scale Signal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Vision Detection Systems (VDS)** | Yes | Yes — AI VisionStream, 95%+ LPR <3s | Yes — <60s escalation, 97% false-alarm reduction | Yes | Yes — US AWS only | Yes — from $1,500/mo | 500+ deployments, 30+ states, est. 2017 |
| LiveView Technologies (LVT) | Yes | Partial — proprietary, hardware-locked | Yes — third-party SOC partnerships | Yes | Yes | No | ~5,000 units, largest US fleet |
| ECAM (Stealth + ECAMSECURE + GardaWorld) | Partial — some OEM | Partial | Yes | Mixed | Mixed | No | Largest US RVM service, 2025 brand merger |
| Flock Safety | Yes (fixed ALPR poles) | Yes — ALPR community network | Limited — alert-driven | Yes | Yes | No | 4,000+ cities, Jan 2026 67-camera exposure incident |
| WCCTV | Yes | No real AI layer | Yes — UK + US operators | Mixed (UK origin) | Mixed | No | "USA #1" claim, dated UX |
| Pro-Vigil | No — uses installer cameras | Partial | Yes — managed RVM | Mixed | Mixed | No | Large RVM operator; Glassdoor flags outdated tech |
| Verkada | Yes (fixed cameras only) | Yes | Limited | Yes | Yes | No — quoted | $2.95M FTC settlement Aug 2024; 2021 hack |
| Spot AI | No — software-only | Yes | No | N/A | Yes | No | Camera-agnostic VMS, no outdoor hardware |
| Deploy Surveillance | Yes | Limited | Limited | Mixed | Unclear | No | Small US mobile vendor |
| GoView | Yes | Limited | Limited | Mixed | Unclear | Partial | Small US rent/purchase vendor |

## Where each competitor wins

**LVT** wins on raw fleet scale. If your buying committee values "they have 5,000 units in the field," LVT will satisfy that test before anyone else. The trade-off is hardware-locked architecture and no published pricing.

**ECAM** wins on RVM headcount. After the 2025 Stealth + ECAMSECURE + GardaWorld merger they are the largest remote monitoring service in the US by operator seats. Brand churn is real and the platform story is still settling.

**Flock Safety** wins on the ALPR community network for municipal customers. The January 2026 public exposure of 67 camera feeds and the resulting 30+ city cancellations are a governance signal worth weighing.

**WCCTV** wins on UK and European references. In the US they market a "#1" position; the product UX has not been refreshed recently and there is no real AI inference layer.

**Pro-Vigil** wins on managed RVM contracts for retail and auto. They do not own outdoor hardware and Glassdoor reviews flag technology debt and operator turnover.

**Verkada** wins on enterprise office and school cloud VMS with a polished admin UI. The $2.95M FTC settlement (August 2024) and the 2021 breach where access was gained to 150,000 customer cameras are governance facts. Verkada is fixed-camera, not mobile.

**Spot AI** wins on software-only deployments where the customer already owns ONVIF/RTSP cameras and wants a modern VMS layer. No outdoor mobile hardware. No SOC.

**Deploy Surveillance** wins on smaller, simpler US mobile deals where the buyer wants a trailer and a basic feed, not a full platform.

**GoView** wins on lowest-end rent/purchase pricing where published.

## Where VDS wins

VDS is the only vendor on this list that combines all six criteria: owns the hardware (Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, Boundary Guard Pro), runs a 7-year-mature AI platform (AI VisionStream on AWS), operates a 24/7 US Security Operations Center under one roof, holds NDAA Section 889 compliance, stores all footage in US AWS regions only, and publishes starting prices.

If you are running an RFP and need a structured side-by-side, request the VDS comparison pack at /demo. Include your current vendor — we will populate the matrix above with your live SLA terms, retention policy, NDAA status, and SOC location.

faq.q: Who is the largest mobile surveillance company in the US?
faq.a: By unit count, LiveView Technologies (LVT) operates the largest US mobile surveillance fleet at roughly 5,000 units. By integrated capability — hardware plus AI platform plus 24/7 US SOC under one roof — VDS is the only vendor offering all three.

faq.q: Which mobile surveillance companies are NDAA Section 889 compliant?

faq.q: Why does NDAA compliance matter for a private-sector buyer?
faq.a: Federal contracts and federally-funded projects require Section 889 compliance. Insurance underwriters and large GCs increasingly require it for jobsite coverage even when no federal money is involved.

faq.a: Weight the six criteria by what your security committee actually cares about. Construction GCs usually weight hardware durability and SOC response. Municipalities weight data residency and NDAA. Retail weights AI alarm filtering and price per unit.

## Why this comparison matters

Zedcor and VDS are often shortlisted together by North American buyers — energy operators, national GCs, and retail chains with footprints on both sides of the border. The two companies serve different geographies and operate under different regulatory regimes. The right answer is rarely "pick one" — it is usually "pick the right one for each country, or run them together."

| Criterion | VDS | Zedcor |

**Oil and gas references.** Decade-plus of Alberta and Saskatchewan upstream and midstream deployments. If your project is a wellpad, lease site, or pipeline yard in western Canada, Zedcor has more references in the file than VDS does.

**Public-company governance.** TSX-V listing means audited financials, public quarterly disclosure, and a board structure that some procurement teams require for vendor approval.

**Canadian SOC operator nuance.** Local language coverage, Canadian law enforcement dispatch relationships, and provincial reporting familiarity.

## Where VDS wins

**NDAA Section 889 compliance.** Required for any US federal contract, federally-funded project, or large GC jobsite where the GC's master agreement flows down 889. Canadian operators are not built around this requirement.

**US AWS-only data residency.** All AI VisionStream footage is encrypted at rest with AES-256 in US AWS regions only. TLS 1.3 in transit. Immutable 12-month audit log. RBAC and MFA enforced.

**Published pricing.** Sky Guard MSU from $2,200/mo, Swift Deploy from $1,500/mo, Boundary Guard Pro from $1,800/mo. Sky Guard purchase from $38,000. Zedcor pricing is by quote.

**7-year AI platform maturity.** AI VisionStream is camera-agnostic (ONVIF/RTSP), 95%+ LPR accuracy in under 3 seconds, 30/60/90-day cloud retention options, and feeds the SOC's 97% false-alarm reduction.

**Hero case study with US numbers.** $28M Mid-Atlantic GC — 73% theft reduction, $0 insurance claims, $340,800 saved in 12 months.

**You are a Canadian buyer expanding into the US.** Run Zedcor in Canada; run VDS for US sites. We can structure a coordinated rollout with matching escalation procedures and a shared incident reporting format. Talk to /partners.

**You are a US buyer with Canadian sites.** Same logic reversed. VDS covers your US footprint with NDAA and US data residency. Zedcor covers Canada under PIPEDA. Procurement gets one shortlist; security gets full coverage.

**You are evaluating for a single-country deployment.** Pick the operator built for that regulatory regime. For US sites, that is VDS.

## Why this comparison matters

If you have searched "mobile surveillance" the brand names sometimes blur together. Deploy Surveillance is a real US vendor — they sell mobile units and serve real customers. VDS is also a real US vendor. The two companies are not the same shape. This page lays out the differences so you can choose on facts, not on a Google ad.

## The comparison matrix

| Criterion | VDS | Deploy Surveillance |

| Headquarters | Pikesville, Maryland | United States |
| Year founded | 2017 | Newer entrant |

## Where Deploy Surveillance wins

**Simplicity for smaller deals.** If you need one or two trailers on a single site, do not need a platform to manage 30 cameras across 15 sites, and want a straightforward rental contract, a smaller vendor like Deploy Surveillance can be the right fit. Less surface area means less software to learn.

**Lower coordination overhead.** Smaller operators sometimes move faster on a one-off custom request because there is less internal process.

**Direct phone line to the owner.** With smaller vendors you often talk to the principal directly. That has value for some buyers.

## Where VDS wins

**Scale signal.** 500+ deployments across 30+ states is a different field-data set than a smaller operator can offer. When something unusual happens at 2:47 AM at a remote site, the SOC has likely seen the pattern before.

**Real AI, not a marketing label.** AI VisionStream is camera-agnostic via ONVIF/RTSP, hits 95%+ LPR accuracy in under 3 seconds, and feeds the SOC the filtered signal that powers the 97% false-alarm reduction number. This is 7 years of model and ops iteration.

**24/7 in-house US SOC.** Not a third-party referral. VDS operators dispatch local law enforcement, run audio talk-down through the unit speaker, and escalate to a named site contact in under 60 seconds.

**NDAA Section 889 in writing.** Required for federal contracts, federally-funded projects, and most large GC master agreements. We hand you the bill of materials.

**Published pricing.** Sky Guard MSU from $2,200/mo. Swift Deploy from $1,500/mo. Boundary Guard Pro from $1,800/mo. Sky Guard purchase from $38,000. No quote-walls.

**Hero outcome data.** $28M Mid-Atlantic GC — 73% theft reduction, $0 insurance claims, $340,800 saved in 12 months. Numbers are the comparison.

## Switching from Deploy Surveillance to VDS

We have ported customers off other mobile surveillance vendors before. The migration usually looks like:

1. **Week 1** — VDS engineer reviews your site map, current footage retention, and existing camera assets. If you have ONVIF/RTSP cameras already, AI VisionStream can ingest them.
2. **Week 2** — Hardware swap or addition scheduled. SOC profile built for your sites, including escalation contacts and dispatch boundaries.
3. **Week 3** — Live. Old vendor demobilized. Historical footage exported to your storage if required.

No early-termination penalty applies on the VDS side; check your existing contract for the other side.

faq.a: No. Deploy Surveillance and Vision Detection Systems (VDS) are separate US companies. Different ownership, different products, different scale.

faq.q: Can I run both vendors in parallel during a transition?
faq.a: Yes. We can deploy VDS units alongside existing equipment and bring them live before the old units demobilize, so there is no coverage gap.

faq.a: Confirm directly with Deploy Surveillance. VDS operates a 24/7 in-house US SOC with sub-60-second escalation. If the SOC matters to your buying decision, ask each vendor for their SOC's location, staffing model, and false-alarm reduction rate.

The .ai TLD is a marketing signal. It is not a product signal. AI in mobile surveillance is judged on three things: how accurate the inference is in the field, how the SOC uses that inference to reduce false alarms, and how the data is governed. This page compares VDS and BIGView on those operational dimensions, not on web design.

seoTitle: VDS vs. Deep Sentinel — Different Buyers
metaDescription: Deep Sentinel is great for homes and small storefronts. VDS is built for commercial mobile, solar-autonomous coverage. Here is which one fits which buyer.
h1: VDS vs. Deep Sentinel
heroSubhead: Deep Sentinel sells AI-monitored fixed cameras with live talk-down agents — a strong product for homes and small storefronts. VDS sells solar-autonomous mobile surveillance for construction sites, utility substations, retail parking, and multi-acre commercial properties. Here is how to tell which one you actually need.
heroStats: Deep Sentinel: residential and small storefront
body:
## Why this comparison matters

Both companies advertise AI-driven monitoring with human operators in the loop. Buyers who search "AI security with live agents" can land on either site. The hardware, deployment model, and target customer are different enough that this page exists to route you correctly.

## The comparison matrix

| Criterion | VDS | Deep Sentinel |
|---|---|---|
| Primary buyer | Commercial, construction, utility, retail parking, municipal | Residential, single-storefront small business |
| Hardware form factor | Solar-autonomous mobile units (trailers and pole-mounted) | Fixed wired cameras + AI hub |
| Mobile / redeployable | Yes | No |
| Solar autonomous | Yes | No — wired |
| Deployment scale | Multi-acre sites, 30+ states, 500+ deployments | Single property, single building |
| AI live talk-down | Yes — operator-initiated via SOC | Yes — interactive AI agents + human |
| 24/7 monitoring | Yes — VDS in-house US SOC, <60s escalation | Yes — Deep Sentinel agents |
| LE dispatch | Yes — local relationships, named officer where possible | Yes |
| NDAA Section 889 | Yes — federal-eligible | Confirm |
| US-only AWS data residency | Yes | Confirm |
| Audit log | 12-month immutable | Confirm |
| RBAC, MFA | Yes | Limited at consumer tier |
| Camera-agnostic VMS (ONVIF/RTSP) | Yes — ingest existing cameras | No — proprietary cameras |
| Pricing tier | From $1,500/mo (Swift Deploy) to $2,200+/mo (Sky Guard) | Consumer plans well under $100/mo; small-business plans $200–$500/mo |
| Lowest entry price | $1,500/mo | Under $100/mo for residential |
| Time to deploy | Days to weeks | Hours (DIY install) |

## Where Deep Sentinel wins

**Homes.** A single-family home does not need a solar-autonomous trailer. Deep Sentinel's fixed AI cameras with live agent monitoring are well-priced and well-designed for that buyer.

**Single storefronts and small businesses.** A coffee shop, a small office, a single-bay auto shop. The Deep Sentinel hub plus 2-4 cameras and a monthly plan is the right shape and the right budget.

**DIY install and short install timelines.** Deep Sentinel ships, you mount cameras, you go live in hours. No site survey, no trailer transport.

**Sub-$500/mo budget.** If your monthly security spend is under $500 across the whole site, Deep Sentinel is a real fit. VDS is not optimized for that band.

**Interactive AI talk-down at the consumer tier.** Deep Sentinel's interactive agents are a thoughtful product for residential use.

## Where VDS wins

**Sites without power.** Solar-autonomous units mean construction sites, undeveloped land, utility substations, and remote yards get full coverage without trenching or a generator.

**Sites that move.** Construction projects relocate the active work zone every few weeks. Lay-down yards shift. Mobile units redeploy in hours. Fixed cameras do not.

**Multi-acre and perimeter coverage.** A 20-acre lay-down yard, a 40-acre solar farm, or a quarter-mile substation perimeter is not a fixed-camera job. Mobile units with elevated masts, pan-tilt-zoom cameras, and AI-driven detection cover that footprint with fewer assets.

**Commercial governance.** NDAA Section 889 in writing. US-only AWS data residency. AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit. 12-month immutable audit log. RBAC and MFA. These are the answers a commercial security committee, an insurance underwriter, or a federal-flow-down GC needs.

**Operator-driven SOC playbooks.** VDS' in-house US SOC builds a per-site escalation tree, named contacts, dispatch boundaries, and audio talk-down scripts. The 97% false-alarm reduction comes from that operator discipline, not just from the AI.

**Customer outcomes at commercial scale.** Hero case: $28M Mid-Atlantic GC. 73% theft reduction. $0 insurance claims. $340,800 saved in 12 months. That is a different math problem from a residential security plan.

## Pricing comparison

| Tier | Deep Sentinel | VDS |
|---|---|---|
| Residential | Under $100/mo | Not offered |
| Single storefront | $200–$500/mo | Not the right fit |
| Commercial mobile, single unit | Not offered | From $1,500/mo (Swift Deploy) |
| Premium MSU, single unit | Not offered | From $2,200/mo (Sky Guard) |
| Multi-site enterprise | Not offered | Quoted per program |

## Which one do you need?

- **You are a homeowner** — Deep Sentinel.
- **You run a single small business storefront** — Deep Sentinel.
- **You are a GC, utility, municipal site manager, retail park operator, or multi-site enterprise** — VDS.
- **You need to move the cameras every few weeks** — VDS.
- **You have a site with no electrical service** — VDS.
- **You need NDAA Section 889 documentation for a federal flow-down** — VDS.

faq.q: Is Deep Sentinel a bad product?
faq.a: No. Deep Sentinel is a good product for residential and small-storefront buyers. It is not designed for multi-acre commercial mobile deployments, which is what VDS does.

faq.q: Can VDS cover a single small business?
faq.a: We can, but the math rarely works out. If your site is under $500/mo of security spend and is a single fixed building, Deep Sentinel or a comparable fixed-camera service is usually a better fit.

faq.q: Can Deep Sentinel cover a construction site?
faq.a: Generally no. Construction sites typically need solar-autonomous, redeployable units because the active work zone moves and grid power is rarely available.

faq.q: Does VDS offer interactive AI talk-down?
faq.a: VDS does operator-driven audio talk-down via the unit speaker. A human operator decides when to engage. We do not currently route through a consumer-style AI conversational agent.

faq.q: Where is VDS data stored?
faq.a: US AWS regions only. AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, 12-month immutable audit log. Required for most commercial security programs.

finalCTAHeading: Not sure which one fits?
finalCTABody: Tell us about the site. If Deep Sentinel is the right answer we will say so on the call. No quota for routing buyers to the wrong product.
notes: Genuinely respectful tone. Deep Sentinel is a well-built product for its segment. Resist any temptation to imply otherwise. This page should pass the smell test of a Deep Sentinel employee reading it.

h1: Manufacturer vs. Integrator — Buying Direct vs. Buying through Security 101
heroSubhead: Integrators like Security 101 resell multiple brands and assemble them into one system. Manufacturers like VDS design, build, monitor, and support a single product line end-to-end. Both models work. Here is how to know which one fits your program.
body:
## Why this comparison matters

Security 101 is the most-recognized national US integrator. They resell Verkada, Avigilon, Genetec, and others, and assemble those products into a system for the buyer. VDS is a manufacturer — we design and build mobile surveillance hardware (Sky Guard, Swift Deploy, Boundary Guard Pro), run the AI VisionStream platform, and operate a 24/7 US SOC under one roof.

Neither model is automatically better. The right model depends on what you are buying.

## The comparison matrix

| Criterion | VDS (Manufacturer-Direct) | Security 101 / Multi-Brand Integrator |
|---|---|---|
| Product breadth | One specialized product line — mobile surveillance | Many brands — cameras, access control, intrusion, intercom, fixed VMS |
| Single pane of glass across 10+ vendors | No — we are one vendor | Yes — integrator's strength |
| Hardware ownership | Yes — VDS designs and builds | No — resells third-party hardware |
| Pricing transparency | Published — from $1,500/mo, $38,000 purchase | Integrator margin layered on top of MSRP |
| Manufacturer support | Direct — engineer to engineer | Through integrator |
| Warranty owner | VDS | Varies by reseller terms |
| SOC ownership | VDS in-house US SOC | Outsourced or third-party referral |
| NDAA Section 889 traceability | Direct from manufacturer | Through reseller chain |
| Brand lock-in risk | Single-brand dedicated program | Whatever the integrator resells |
| Change-order flexibility | Direct line to engineering | Through integrator's process |
| Geographic install reach | VDS field service + integrator partners | Integrator's footprint |
| Right for heterogeneous building security | Not the right fit | Yes |
| Right for mobile-surveillance program | Yes — direct manufacturer | Add markup, lose direct line |

## Where an integrator like Security 101 wins

**Heterogeneous environments.** A corporate campus with badge access control, intercoms, fixed surveillance from two brands, intrusion panels, and a parking gate system needs an integrator. Stitching those products together is the integrator's job and they are good at it.

**One-throat-to-choke across 10+ vendors.** If your security director wants one PO, one trouble ticket address, and one annual review covering everything, the integrator is the model.

**Existing relationship.** If Security 101 already installed your access control and your fixed surveillance, adding the mobile surveillance trailer through them is sometimes simpler than starting a parallel relationship.

**Geographic install density.** National integrators have install techs in markets where a single manufacturer may not.

## Where buying direct from VDS wins

**Mobile surveillance is a dedicated program.** If you are spending $50,000+ per year on mobile surveillance trailers across multiple sites, you are running a dedicated program. Buying it through an integrator adds margin without adding value.

**Manufacturer SOC and warranty.** When a unit fails at 3 AM, you want the manufacturer's SOC and the manufacturer's field service. Going through an integrator means the integrator opens a ticket with VDS — extra step, no benefit.

**Transparent pricing.** Published rates: Swift Deploy from $1,500/mo, Boundary Guard Pro from $1,800/mo, Sky Guard from $2,200/mo, Sky Guard purchase from $38,000. An integrator quote layers margin on top of MSRP. You are paying for the relationship.

**NDAA Section 889 traceability.** When the GC's federal flow-down audit lands on your desk, you need a component bill of materials. Direct from manufacturer is one document. Through an integrator is two paper trails and a phone call.

**Direct engineering line.** Site-specific deployment questions get answered by the engineer who designed the unit, not by a sales rep who resells the unit.

## Pricing comparison

| What you pay | Direct from VDS | Through an integrator |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware MSRP | List | List |
| Integrator margin | $0 | 10–30% typically |
| Annual service | Published rate | Marked up |
| Change orders | Direct billing at engineering rate | Marked up |

Numbers vary by integrator and by deal size. Ask any integrator for the manufacturer's MSRP alongside the integrator quote. If they will not show it, that itself is information.

## A note on integrator partners

VDS works with security integrators through our /partners program. If you are an integrator reading this — we are not trying to cut you out. We are trying to be honest with end-buyers about when a manufacturer-direct purchase is the better answer. Where the integrator relationship adds real value (heterogeneous environments, multi-vendor stitching, geographic install reach), we partner. Where it adds only margin, we encourage direct.

## Decision framework

**Buy through an integrator if:**
- You are buying mobile surveillance as one piece of a broader multi-vendor security system.
- You have an existing integrator relationship and the marginal install volume is small.
- You want one PO covering access control, fixed cameras, intrusion, and mobile.

**Buy direct from VDS if:**
- Mobile surveillance is a dedicated program with its own budget line.
- You need manufacturer-direct SOC, warranty, and engineering support.
- You need NDAA Section 889 traceability in one document.
- Your security committee values published pricing and no margin layer.
- You want the engineer who built the unit on the call when something needs to change.

faq.q: Does VDS sell through Security 101?
faq.a: We have partner relationships with integrators including some Security 101 franchises through /partners. Direct sales are also available and often the better path for dedicated mobile surveillance programs.

faq.q: Is buying through an integrator always more expensive?
faq.a: Usually yes, because integrators layer margin on MSRP. The trade-off is consolidation across multiple vendors. If that consolidation has value to your program, the margin is worth it. If you are running a dedicated mobile surveillance program, it usually is not.

faq.q: Can I get VDS hardware from Verkada or Avigilon dealers?
faq.a: No. VDS hardware is sold by VDS direct or through approved /partners. Verkada and Avigilon do not resell our mobile surveillance hardware.

faq.q: What is in VDS' partner program?
faq.a: Integrator referrals, co-quoted opportunities, install support, and SOC integration into the integrator's existing operations. See /partners.

faq.q: Will VDS work alongside my existing integrator?
faq.a: Yes. We have closed deals where the integrator handles fixed surveillance and access control while VDS runs the mobile program directly. The integrator stays in the relationship; VDS owns the mobile piece end-to-end.

finalCTAHeading: Mobile surveillance is its own program
finalCTABody: If you are buying $50K+ a year of mobile surveillance, buy it direct. If you are an integrator, partner with us at /partners. Either way, get a real quote.

body:
## Why this comparison matters

Type "mobile surveillance" into Google and the first page returns vendors selling completely different products. A construction GC and a sheriff's deputy both use the words "mobile surveillance" to describe the thing they need. They need different things.

This page exists to route you to the right category before you spend a quarter chasing the wrong vendor.

## The two markets

| Dimension | Fixed-Site Mobile Surveillance | Fleet / In-Car / Body-Worn Video |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Solar-autonomous surveillance trailers and pole-mounted units that deploy to a site for weeks or months | Video cameras mounted in vehicles or worn by personnel that record continuously while the asset is in motion |
| Where it lives | At a site — construction yard, lay-down area, utility substation, retail parking, remote property | Inside or on a vehicle or person — patrol car, transit bus, delivery truck, officer's chest |
| Mobility model | Redeployable between sites; static while on-site | Always moving with the vehicle or person |
| Power model | Solar autonomous, optional grid | Vehicle 12V or worn battery |
| Primary buyer | Construction, utility, retail, municipal, energy, federal sites | Law enforcement, transit, public works fleets, delivery, trucking |
| Primary use case | Theft deterrence, perimeter monitoring, post-incident evidence, remote site oversight | Officer accountability, fleet incident review, body-worn evidence chain, dashcam claims defense |
| Storage and chain of custody | Cloud-first, immutable audit log, RBAC, MFA | DEMS-style chain of custody, court-admissible export, prosecutor handoff |
| 24/7 monitoring | Often — VDS SOC runs this | Rarely — assets are mobile and operator-led |
| AI focus | LPR, person/vehicle/intrusion at perimeter | Driver behavior, collision detection, body-cam event flags |
| Procurement model | Rental or purchase per site / per unit | Per-vehicle or per-officer license, often multi-year contract |

## Leading vendors in fleet / in-car / body-worn video

VDS does not sell in this market. If you got here looking for in-car or body-cam video, here are the named vendors most US buyers shortlist:

- **Axon** — The dominant US body-worn camera vendor. Integrated with Axon Evidence (cloud DEMS) and Taser. Strong law enforcement footprint.
- **Apollo Video Technology** — Mobile DVR systems for transit buses, school buses, paratransit, and rail. Strong public-transit references.
- **Safety Vision** — Mobile video for school buses, transit, law enforcement vehicles, and commercial fleets. Long US history.
- **AngelTrax** — School bus and pupil transportation video systems. Strong K-12 references.
- **Digital Ally** — In-car video and body cameras for law enforcement. Publicly traded.
- **Utility** — In-car and body-worn video with integrated wireless upload and cloud DEMS.
- **TSI Video** (Transit Safety Inc.) — Transit and commercial fleet mobile video.

This is not a ranking and it is not exhaustive. It is a starting shortlist so you can route yourself out of the fixed-site mobile surveillance category and into the right RFP.

## Leading vendors in fixed-site mobile surveillance

If you got here looking for solar-autonomous surveillance trailers, the shortlist is on /compare/top-mobile-surveillance-companies. The vendors are LVT, ECAM, Flock Safety, WCCTV, Pro-Vigil, Verkada, Spot AI, Deploy Surveillance, GoView, and VDS.

## How to tell which market you need

Answer these three questions:

1. **Does the camera need to move continuously with a vehicle or person?**
   - Yes → fleet / in-car / body-worn. Talk to Axon, Apollo, Safety Vision, AngelTrax, Digital Ally, Utility, or TSI Video.
   - No → fixed-site mobile surveillance. Talk to VDS.

2. **Will the camera sit at a fixed location for weeks or months, then redeploy to a new site?**
   - Yes → fixed-site mobile surveillance. This is VDS.
   - No → not VDS.

3. **Is your primary use case officer accountability, court-admissible body-cam evidence, or fleet driver behavior?**
   - Yes → fleet / in-car / body-worn.
   - No, your use case is theft deterrence, perimeter monitoring, and remote site oversight → fixed-site mobile surveillance.

## Where the two markets sometimes overlap

A utility operator might use VDS at a substation perimeter AND Apollo Video on their service trucks. A municipality might run Flock Safety ALPR poles in city neighborhoods AND Axon body cameras on the patrol force. The two markets serve adjacent buyers and sometimes the same buyer for different jobs.

The key is that the procurement, RFP language, evaluation criteria, and vendor lists are different. Buying body-worn cameras from a mobile surveillance trailer vendor is a category error. Buying mobile surveillance trailers from a body-cam vendor is also a category error.

## Where VDS wins inside fixed-site mobile surveillance

500+ deployments across 30+ states. Three product lines (Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, Boundary Guard Pro). AI VisionStream — camera-agnostic ONVIF/RTSP, 95%+ LPR at sub-3-second match. 24/7 in-house US SOC with sub-60-second escalation and 97% false-alarm reduction. NDAA Section 889 compliant. US AWS-only data residency. Published pricing from $1,500/mo (Swift Deploy) and from $38,000 purchase (Sky Guard).

Hero case study: $28M Mid-Atlantic GC — 73% theft reduction, $0 insurance claims, $340,800 saved in 12 months.

faq.q: Does VDS make in-car police cameras?
faq.a: No. For in-car law enforcement video, look at Digital Ally, Utility, or Axon.

faq.q: Can VDS provide cameras for school buses or transit fleets?
faq.a: No. For school bus, transit, or fleet video, look at Apollo Video Technology, Safety Vision, or AngelTrax.

faq.q: Why do these markets both call themselves "mobile surveillance"?
faq.a: Historical naming. The fixed-site mobile surveillance category emerged from camera trailers that move between sites. The fleet / in-car category emerged from cameras mounted on moving assets. Both use "mobile." Procurement teams should specify "mobile surveillance trailer" or "fleet / body-worn video" to disambiguate.

After-hours liability is rising in parallel — premises security litigation against property owners has expanded significantly over the past decade.

VDS combines automated detection with human intervention. AI VisionStream runs time-of-day rules — after-hours zones arm automatically based on site schedule. The rule set includes person-on-site detection, vehicle loitering, fence-line breach, and perimeter approach. Thermal imaging on Sky Guard MSU detects body heat in low light, through brush, and behind cover. Radar detects movement at the property line before a breach.

When a rule fires, the alert reaches a US SOC operator's console in seconds. The operator pulls live video, classifies the threat, and acts: live audio talk-down through the on-unit speaker, LE dispatch with GPS and direction of travel, evidence preservation. 97% false alarm reduction through AI pre-filtering means the alerts that reach a human are real.

## What vandalism looks like in 2026

Vandalism is rarely random. Construction sites get hit because they're empty after 6pm and the materials are tempting. Retail strip centers get tagged because the rear loading bay is unwatched. Schools get hit on weekends and breaks. Parks get hit overnight. The repair cost runs $500 for a graffiti cleanup, $1,500 to $5,000 for broken glass and signage, and $10,000+ for sabotage to equipment, HVAC condensers, or fire suppression systems.

The reputational cost is harder to quantify but real. A vandalized storefront signals neglect. A tagged construction site signals an unmonitored project to the entire neighborhood — and once a site is identified as soft, the pattern repeats. One incident becomes a cluster. A school with weekend graffiti loses parent confidence. A retail property with broken windows loses tenant interest.

Vandalism is a loitering crime. Suspects approach, assess the site, position themselves, and then act. That approach window — typically 30 seconds to 4 minutes — is where prevention happens.

## How VDS prevents vandalism

VDS targets the loiter window. AI VisionStream loitering detection rules fire when a person remains in a zone for more than a threshold (typically 60 to 120 seconds) during after-hours periods. Thermal imaging on Sky Guard MSU detects the suspect in low light or behind cover. Swift Deploy PTZ pulls in tight on the activity zone — most-vandalized corners, loading docks, rear walls, dumpster enclosures.

The SOC operator sees the live alert in seconds and initiates audio talk-down: "You are being recorded. Police have been dispatched. Leave the property now." This ends the attempt in the majority of cases before the spray, the rock, or the tool comes out. When it doesn't, plate capture and live video go to dispatched officers, and the incident package goes to your insurance and law enforcement contacts.

Repeat offender identification is part of the value. VDS preserves evidence across multiple incidents, builds a pattern file, and supports prosecution that breaks the cluster.

seoTitle: Mobile Surveillance in Canada: Regulatory & Operational
metaDescription: A practical guide to mobile surveillance in Canada — PIPEDA, provincial privacy law, cold-weather operations, NDAA equivalence, and vendor selection.
h1: Mobile Surveillance in Canada — Regulatory and Operational Guide
heroSubhead: How mobile surveillance operates in Canada, what the privacy frameworks require, how cold weather and solar interact, and what to ask any vendor — Canadian or US-based — before signing.

heroCTAPrimary.label: Talk to us about cross-border coverage

heroStats: PIPEDA • Quebec Law 25 • AB PIPA • BC PIPA • -20F operating range
body:
This guide is written for Canadian security and operations buyers evaluating mobile surveillance — whether the eventual vendor is Vision Detection Systems, a Canadian operator like Zedcor, or someone else entirely. We deploy across 30+ US states and are planning a Canadian launch. The framing below reflects what we've learned operating at scale and what Canadian operators have taught us about their market.

## How mobile surveillance differs in Canada

Canadian mobile surveillance has a few structural differences from the US market:

- **Cross-border data is a contract-level question.** Many Canadian buyers — especially Crown corporations, regulated utilities, and Quebec-based organizations — require Canadian data residency. A US vendor running US-region cloud infrastructure will not pass these reviews without a Canadian data plane.
- **Provincial privacy law adds a layer.** PIPEDA is the federal default, but Alberta, British Columbia, and Quebec each operate substantially similar provincial regimes that take precedence in their jurisdictions. Quebec Law 25 is the strictest and now includes meaningful penalties.
- **Bilingual support is jurisdiction-specific.** Quebec deployments typically require French-language operator and SOC capability. Most provinces don't, but the major Canadian operators offer bilingual coverage as table stakes.
- **Hardware logistics span vast distances.** A unit deployed in Northern BC or Northern Ontario may be a 10-hour drive from the nearest service tech. Service-level agreements need to reflect that geography honestly.

## PIPEDA and provincial privacy frameworks

A mobile surveillance program in Canada has to handle personal information lawfully under PIPEDA at minimum. The relevant questions for a buyer:

- **Notice.** Are you posting visible notice at the deployment site that video monitoring is in effect, with contact information for inquiries?
- **Purpose limitation.** Is footage retained only as long as the stated business purpose requires? 30–90 days is the typical defensible range absent a specific incident.
- **Cross-border disclosure.** If footage leaves Canada — even to a US-based SOC for review — your privacy notice must say so, and your contracts must address it.
- **Quebec specifically.** Law 25 requires a designated privacy officer, mandatory breach notification, and Privacy Impact Assessments for projects involving personal information. A Quebec deployment is not a copy-paste of an Ontario deployment.

Alberta PIPA and BC PIPA each have their own breach notification triggers and operator-of-record rules. Treat them as separate compliance reviews, not as PIPEDA clones.

## Cold-weather and solar performance in Canada

Solar-autonomous mobile surveillance works in Canada, including in winter. Three caveats:

- **Operating temperature.** Sky Guard MSU is rated to -20F (-29C). That covers the vast majority of Canadian populated regions year-round. Extreme cold beyond that range is a hardware spec question, not a "does it work" question.
- **Solar irradiance in winter.** Short December days at northern latitudes mean battery sizing matters more than panel wattage. A well-sized system rides through 5–7 day overcast stretches at Vancouver or Toronto latitudes. Further north, sizing changes.
- **Snow load and panel orientation.** Steeper panel angles shed snow better. This is a deployment-time configuration, not a hardware redesign.

Cold weather is not the reason VDS isn't in Canada yet. Operations and compliance are.

## NDAA equivalence and Canadian government procurement

Section 889 of the US NDAA prohibits certain Chinese-manufactured surveillance equipment in federal contracts. It is a US statute and does not apply in Canada.

Canada's federal procurement uses different supply-chain integrity tools, including the Policy on Government Security, the Integrated Cyber Security Risk Management Framework, and case-by-case national security reviews. There is no single "Canadian NDAA." Crown procurement increasingly asks vendors to attest to supply chain provenance, and major Canadian operators have responded accordingly.

If you are buying for a Canadian federal department or Crown corporation, the procurement instrument — not a generic compliance certificate — defines the bar.

## What to ask any mobile surveillance vendor in Canada

Use these questions on every vendor call, ours included:

1. Where is video stored, and in which cloud region?
2. Where is the SOC physically located, and what languages do operators speak?
3. What is the retention policy, and can it be configured per site?
4. How do you handle a PIPEDA data-subject access request?
5. What is your mean response time for a verified intrusion alert, and how is that measured?
6. What is the solar autonomy window for the configuration you're quoting at this site's latitude?
7. Who owns the hardware at end of term, and what is the removal process?
8. Can you provide three Canadian references in the same vertical at similar scale?

## When to choose a Canadian operator vs a US operator with Canadian partners

A pure Canadian operator (Zedcor, A&B, SureSite, Spotter, LotCop) is the right fit when your program is Canada-only, your sites are within their service geography, and your compliance posture demands a Canadian-resident operator with Canadian data residency.

A US operator with Canadian partners is the right fit when your program spans both countries, you want consolidated reporting, and you can accept a Canadian operator handling the Canadian sites under a coordinated structure. This is the model VDS uses today for cross-border buyers.

A direct US operator with no Canadian partner is rarely the right fit for a Canadian deployment today. Compliance and data residency gaps tend to surface during procurement review, not after.

faq.q: Does PIPEDA apply to video surveillance?
faq.a: Yes. Identifiable individuals captured on video are personal information under PIPEDA, and the standard collection-use-disclosure rules apply.

faq.q: Can a US-based SOC review Canadian footage?
faq.a: Legally, often yes, with appropriate notice and contractual protections. Practically, many Canadian buyers — especially government, healthcare, and Quebec-based organizations — will require Canadian SOC coverage regardless.

faq.q: Is NDAA Section 889 relevant to a Canadian buyer?
faq.a: Only if the buyer also sells into US federal contracts. NDAA is a US procurement statute. Canadian procurement uses its own supply-chain integrity frameworks.

faq.q: What's a reasonable retention period for mobile surveillance footage in Canada?
faq.a: 30–90 days is the typical defensible range for most commercial use cases. Longer retention requires a documented business justification.

faq.q: Do solar-powered units work through a Canadian winter?
faq.a: Yes, with appropriate battery sizing and panel orientation. Operating range to -20F covers most populated Canadian regions year-round.

faq.q: Why is VDS publishing this guide if it doesn't yet operate in Canada?
faq.a: Because Canadian expansion is on our roadmap, and we'd rather earn trust by writing accurately about the market now than over-promise capability we don't yet have.

## The warehouse cargo theft problem in 2026

Cargo theft has shifted from the highway to the yard. The dominant attack pattern in 2025-2026:

- **Strategic / fictitious pickup** — a thief poses as a legitimate carrier, presents fraudulent paperwork at the gate, hooks up the wrong trailer, and drives off. Loss visibility lags 24-72 hours.
- **Unauthorized trailer hookups** — after-hours bobtail arrival, no scheduled pickup, hookup and exit. The yard fence and a paper gate log are the only controls.
- **Pilferage at the dock** — partial-load theft from staged trailers, often involving inside collusion.
- **Full trailer theft** — bobtail arrives, hooks a loaded trailer, leaves. Often inside knowledge of which trailer carries which load.

CargoNet's 2024 data: average loss per incident exceeded $200,000. Electronics, pharmaceuticals, food, and household goods are the top categories. Recovery rates trail behind heavy equipment.

The gate guard plus a chain-link fence plus paper BOLs is no longer adequate, and shippers are starting to require monitored yard security in vendor contracts.

## The festival and event security problem in 2026

The promoter or producer typically owns five overlapping security challenges in parallel:

1. **Build-out period (3-14 days pre-event)** — equipment, AV, staging, vendor inventory arriving and sitting overnight on an unfenced or lightly-fenced site
2. **Ingress / egress** — credentialed vehicle and personnel access at multiple points, with VIP, vendor, talent, crew, and patron categories
3. **In-event perimeter** — fence-line and back-of-house monitoring during operating hours
4. **Vendor zone protection** — high-value vendor inventory (alcohol, merchandise, electronics) targeted during operating hours and overnight
5. **Strike / load-out (1-7 days post-event)** — equipment and staging on the ground while the event is mostly empty

Permanent CCTV is not the answer — the event will be gone in days or weeks. Standard event security (guards + radios + fencing) doesn't produce documentation, doesn't run after hours efficiently, and doesn't capture credentialed vehicle plates at the gate.

## How VDS covers festival and event security

The deployment matches the event timeline:

**Pre-event build-out:** Sky Guard MSU and Swift Deploy units arrive on site within 72 hours of contract. Solar-autonomous — no power tie-in needed. Operational the same day they roll off the trailer.

**Main entry credential check:** Swift Deploy with LPR at the credentialed-vehicle entry. Every VIP, vendor, and crew vehicle plate captured. Hot-list and credential-list integration runs in real time. The gate guard sees the LPR confidence pop on their tablet as the vehicle approaches.

**Vendor zone and back-of-house:** Swift Deploy or pole cameras at the vendor compound, AV village, and back-of-house service road. AI VisionStream classifies after-hours intrusion.

**Overnight asset protection:** Sky Guard MSU at the equipment compound. Thermal sees a person at 1,200ft during the dark hours when the crew has cleared the site. SOC talk-down on intrusion.

**Strike / load-out:** Coverage stays in place until the last truck leaves the site. We demobilize on agreed schedule.

**24/7 US SOC** runs the entire event window. Operator awareness of event-specific protocols (talent compound, patron-vs-trespasser distinction, alcohol vendor protocol).

A 3-day, 65,000-attendee festival in the Mountain West deployed VDS across the build, event, and strike: **3 attempted equipment thefts overnight pre-event (all intercepted at SOC talk-down), 1 vendor compound break-in attempted overnight day 2 (stopped, plate captured, prosecution pursued), 11 credentialed-vehicle plate flags resolved in real time at the gate, 0 loss events during operating hours.** Producer reordered for the next year.

Event pricing is quoted per event. Single-day events from $5,000. Multi-day festivals typical $18,000-$45,000 depending on site complexity. Multi-month event runs use a hybrid term + monthly model. Insurance and risk-management documentation included.

metaDescription: AI VisionStream connects to Genetec, Milestone, Lenel, Brivo, Immix, Bold, Stages, ServiceNow, and Axon-Fusus via ONVIF, REST API, and webhooks.
h1: AI VisionStream works with the systems you already trust.
heroSubhead: VDS is camera-agnostic and platform-agnostic. ONVIF/RTSP on the device side, REST API and webhooks on the data side. If your team already runs a VMS, an access control head-end, a central station, or an ITSM queue, we plug into it — not around it.
heroStats: ONVIF Profile S/T · REST API · Webhooks (HTTPS POST) · NDAA Section 889 · TLS 1.3 / AES-256
body:
VDS does not ask customers to rip and replace. AI VisionStream sits in the middle of the stack: it pulls feeds off ONVIF/RTSP cameras (ours or yours), runs detection models on AWS in US-only regions, and pushes events out to whichever VMS, access platform, central station, or ITSM tool your operations team already uses.

Three categories cover most enterprise security architectures. Pick the one closest to your stack.

## Access Control

Tie perimeter intrusion detection to door and gate logic. When VDS classifies a person crossing a defined zone after hours, the event fires a webhook into your access control platform within 400 ms — fast enough to drive an automated lockdown, an elevator recall, or a credentials-required override before the intruder reaches an interior door.

- **[Lenel S2 / OnGuard + NetBox](/integrations/lenel)** — Carrier-owned access control standard at federal, healthcare, and higher-education sites. VDS events trigger Lenel input points; Lenel door events appear on the VDS timeline.
- **[Brivo Access](/integrations/brivo)** — cloud-native access control common in commercial real estate, multi-family, and retail. Bidirectional: VDS triggers Brivo lockdowns, Brivo unlock events log into the VDS chain-of-custody record.

## Unified VMS

If your security operations center already runs a unified VMS, VDS cameras and SOC-generated events show up alongside everything else — same timeline, same search, same export tools your analysts use today.

- **[Genetec Security Center](/integrations/genetec)** — VDS cameras stream via ONVIF; SOC alerts POST into Security Center as bookmarks and alarms. Native plugin available.
- **[Milestone XProtect](/integrations/milestone)** — VDS feeds and trailer-generated metadata ingest as Milestone drivers; VDS LPR reads display on the Milestone timeline. Bidirectional alerting.

## Central Station, ITSM, and Law Enforcement Sharing

For organizations whose alerts flow into a monitoring company, an IT ticketing queue, or a real-time crime center, VDS forwards signals out of the SOC with full video and metadata attached.

- **[Immix CC](/integrations/immix)** — central station automation. VDS forwards verified alerts with video to your Immix-running monitoring partner.
- **[Bold Group Manitou](/integrations/bold)** — central station automation, same pattern as Immix.
- **[Stages Software](/integrations/stages)** — alarm receiver and CS automation. VDS events flow as signals.
- **[ServiceNow ITSM](/integrations/servicenow)** — VDS critical alerts auto-open ServiceNow incidents so ITSM teams close them in their own queue with full SLA tracking.
- **[Axon-Fusus](/integrations/axon-fusus)** — opt-in, per-incident clip sharing with law enforcement real-time crime centers. Not standing access — your team decides which incident, which clip, which agency, every time.

## Don't see your system?

If you run something custom or something on this page is not listed, the same primitives are available to you directly: REST API, signed webhooks, and a documented event schema. Most one-off integrations take a sprint or less on the customer side. VDS engineering scopes integration work as part of enterprise onboarding at no additional cost.

[Read the API + SDK documentation](/platform/api-sdk-access) or [book a 30-minute integration scoping call](/contact).

faq.a: Yes. VDS is cloud-native on AWS, so it runs in parallel with on-prem VMS deployments. Cameras can stream to both, or VDS can forward events into the on-prem VMS via webhook.

body:
Genetec Security Center is the dominant unified-platform VMS at airports, transit authorities, ports, and large enterprise campuses. VDS does not compete with it. AI VisionStream feeds Security Center the two things it cannot generate on its own at a remote, off-grid perimeter: solar-autonomous camera feeds and human-verified SOC alerts.

## How it works

VDS solar trailers and fixed cameras stream H.264 / H.265 over ONVIF Profile S directly into Security Center as standard video units. Existing operators see them in the same camera tree, the same map, and the same investigation tools they already use.

In parallel, AI VisionStream runs detection in AWS. When the VDS SOC verifies a critical event — intrusion, loitering after hours, an LPR hit on a watch-listed plate — the event POSTs to Security Center as a Genetec alarm with:

- Pre-event and post-event video clip URLs (signed, time-limited)
- Detection class, confidence, zone name, and SOC analyst ID
- A bookmark on the corresponding Security Center camera timeline
- A correlation ID matching the immutable VDS 12-month audit log

The webhook payload is HMAC-SHA256 signed. TLS 1.3 end-to-end.

## What you get

- One pane of glass for SOC analysts already trained on Security Center
- Genetec-side alarm acknowledgement workflows trigger VDS SOC actions (talk-down, LE dispatch) via the reverse webhook
- LPR reads from VDS feed into Security Center AutoVu timelines
- VDS audit log remains the cryptographic record of truth for evidentiary use

## Setup time

For a customer already running Security Center 5.10 or later: 2 to 5 business days from kickoff to first verified alarm in the operator console. Required on customer side: a service account with bookmark and alarm-write permissions, plus a reachable webhook receiver. VDS handles plugin installation and field testing.

## A sample workflow

03:14 — A person crosses the east-fence detection zone at a remote substation. VDS edge classification fires.
03:14 — AI VisionStream confirms in cloud; SOC analyst opens the event.
03:14 — 8 seconds after first detection, the analyst verifies a real intrusion (not wildlife) and triggers audio talk-down.
03:14 — Webhook fires into Security Center. Alarm appears on the operator workstation with linked video.
03:15 — Talk-down does not deter; SOC dispatches local LE while Security Center operator coordinates with internal response.
03:27 — LE on-scene. Event closed in both systems. Audit log signed and sealed.

## Pricing

The Genetec integration is included with any AI VisionStream subscription tier. There is no per-camera connector fee on the VDS side. Genetec licensing (camera connections, AutoVu, Federation) follows standard Genetec channel pricing — VDS does not resell it.

faq.q: Which Security Center versions are supported?
faq.a: 5.10 and later. Earlier versions can be supported via a generic ONVIF-only path without the alarm-POST plugin.

faq.q: Does this work with Security Center Federation across multiple sites?
faq.a: Yes. VDS alerts route to whichever Federated server you specify per camera or per zone.

faq.q: Do we need to run Streamvault or other Genetec hardware?
faq.a: No. VDS does not require any Genetec appliance. Streaming is direct from camera to Security Center over IP.

faq.q: Can we keep VDS as the SOC and Genetec as the local view?
faq.a: That is the common deployment. VDS SOC handles 24/7 monitoring and dispatch; Genetec operators have full visibility and can take over on demand.
