body:
LenelS2 is the access control system of record at thousands of federal sites, hospitals, universities, and Fortune 500 campuses. The integration with VDS is built around one premise: a verified person-in-zone detection at the perimeter should mean something to the doors 200 feet behind it.

## How it works

AI VisionStream pushes critical detections to LenelS2 via the OnGuard OpenAccess API (REST) for OnGuard 8.0 and later, or via the NetBox REST API for NetBox 5.5 and later. The VDS event maps to a virtual input point in the access control panel hierarchy. From there, standard Lenel programming — input-triggered macros, area lockdowns, credential-required overrides — runs exactly as it does for any wired alarm input.

In the reverse direction, Lenel door events (forced door, door held open, access denied, anti-passback violation) POST to VDS via webhook and appear as correlated entries on the AI VisionStream incident timeline. An analyst reviewing a perimeter event sees the door activity that followed it without leaving the VDS console.

## What you get

- Sub-second perimeter-to-door logic at sites where wired sensors are not practical (solar trailers, temporary deployments, large parking footprints)
- Lockdown, mantrap re-arm, and elevator recall driven by AI-verified events, not motion sensors
- Single forensic timeline that includes both video and door history
- NDAA Section 889 compliant camera-side hardware for federal sites

## Setup time

For a customer already running OnGuard 8.0+ or NetBox 5.5+ with OpenAccess licensed: 3 to 7 business days. Required on customer side: an OpenAccess service account, the integration certificate, and a list of input-point mappings (which VDS zones map to which Lenel inputs). VDS integration engineers handle the connector configuration and joint validation.

## A sample workflow

22:47 — VDS detects a person scaling the south fence of a pharmaceutical campus.
22:47 — SOC analyst confirms in 6 seconds.
22:47 — Webhook to OnGuard fires virtual input "Perimeter South — Verified Intrusion."
22:47 — OnGuard macro re-locks all exterior doors on Building 3, holds elevators on lobby, and pages the on-duty security supervisor.
22:48 — VDS audio talk-down begins. Intruder reverses course.
22:51 — Supervisor reviews on VDS console; sees the door re-lock events from OnGuard inline with the video. Decides not to dispatch.
22:53 — Event closed. Audit record retained in both systems.

## Pricing

The Lenel integration is included with any AI VisionStream enterprise subscription. OnGuard OpenAccess licensing and NetBox API access follow standard LenelS2 channel pricing.

faq.q: Does this work with OnGuard on-prem or cloud?
faq.a: Both. The OpenAccess API surface is identical. Cloud OnGuard requires the standard outbound webhook allow-list.

faq.q: What about older Lenel systems without OpenAccess?
faq.a: A dry-contact relay bridge is available for legacy panels. Slower (sub-2-second instead of sub-second) but functional. Talk to us for site-specific scoping.

faq.a: Yes on OnGuard via OpenAccess CommandReader interfaces. NetBox supports input-driven macros that can lock or relock specific portals.

faq.a: VDS uses LenelS2's published OpenAccess and NetBox REST surfaces. Certification status varies by program tier — confirm current status with VDS sales.

h1: VDS + Milestone XProtect

body:
Milestone XProtect is open by design. The MIP SDK and the ONVIF driver model make it the easiest enterprise VMS to integrate against, which is exactly why customers running it tend to keep running it. VDS treats XProtect as a peer system, not a target to displace.

## How it works

VDS cameras stream into XProtect over ONVIF Profile S and Profile T (for edge metadata). On the analytics side, AI VisionStream events flow into XProtect via the MIP SDK as analytics events, with two outputs:

1. **Bookmarks** on the corresponding camera timeline, with a thumbnail and a deep-link back to the VDS console for full incident detail.
2. **Generic events / alarms** that can drive XProtect rules — for example, automatically pop the camera to an operator workstation, trigger a recording-quality boost on adjacent cameras, or fire an output to a connected access platform.

LPR reads from VDS LPR cameras populate XProtect as searchable plate-read metadata, queryable by plate, partial plate, time, and camera.

In reverse, XProtect rule outputs can POST back to VDS via webhook to escalate the event to the VDS SOC for human verification and dispatch.

## What you get

- AI-verified events native in the XProtect Smart Client
- LPR data unified with existing XProtect plate-read databases
- VDS-monitored solar trailers extending XProtect coverage to remote and temporary sites without trenching power or fiber
- Two-way bridge: customer operators on XProtect, VDS SOC on AI VisionStream, same events on both sides

## Setup time

XProtect Corporate or Expert 2020 R3 or later: 3 to 5 business days. Required on customer side: an XProtect service account with analytics-event permission and a reachable MIP endpoint. VDS engineering provides the MIP plug-in and the ONVIF camera configuration.

## A sample workflow

02:08 — VDS LPR camera at a logistics yard reads a plate on a vehicle entering after hours. Plate matches a watch-list.
02:08 — AI VisionStream classifies, SOC analyst confirms in 9 seconds.
02:08 — Analytics event fires into XProtect. The operator workstation on the customer side auto-pops to the camera with a bookmark, plate text overlaid.
02:09 — VDS SOC initiates audio talk-down requesting the driver leave. Vehicle remains.
02:11 — VDS dispatches LE. XProtect rule has already promoted adjacent cameras to high-bitrate recording.
02:24 — LE arrives, recovers the vehicle (reported stolen). Both timelines retain the synchronized record.

## Pricing

The Milestone integration is included with any AI VisionStream enterprise subscription. XProtect licensing (device licenses, Care, MIP) follows Milestone channel pricing.

faq.q: Which XProtect editions are supported?
faq.a: Corporate and Expert. Professional+ supports the ONVIF path but not the full MIP analytics-event integration. Essential+ is not supported.

faq.q: Does VDS pass through full-resolution video or just events?
faq.a: Both. ONVIF Profile S streams full video. The MIP path adds analytics metadata on top.

faq.q: Can XProtect be the system of record and VDS the AI overlay?
faq.a: Yes. Many customers run it that way. VDS still maintains its own immutable 12-month audit log for the events it generates.

faq.q: Does this work with XProtect hosted on Milestone Customer Dashboard / cloud?
faq.a: Yes, with standard outbound webhook and ONVIF reachability. Confirm specifics with VDS during scoping.

Brivo is the de facto cloud access control standard in commercial real estate, multi-family residential, and multi-site retail. The integration with VDS works the way both products are built — cloud to cloud, REST over HTTPS, no on-prem bridge required.

## How it works

VDS events POST to the Brivo API using OAuth 2.0 client credentials. Each AI VisionStream alert maps to an action on Brivo: lock a specific door, lock all doors on a site, switch a schedule, or fire a Brivo event that downstream automations subscribe to.

Brivo events stream back to VDS via Brivo's webhook subscription model. Door unlocks, access-denied attempts, propped-door alarms, and schedule changes appear on the AI VisionStream incident timeline correlated to the camera covering that door.

## What you get

- Cloud-to-cloud architecture — no panel programming, no on-prem appliance
- Verified-event lockdown that does not fire on a raccoon walking past a motion sensor
- Brivo door history on the VDS timeline for chain-of-custody investigation
- Site-level and door-level granularity on which VDS zones drive which Brivo actions

## Setup time

For a customer with an active Brivo account: 2 to 4 business days. Required on customer side: a Brivo API key (admin-level for door control), the list of doors and zones, and a webhook destination on the VDS side (provided). VDS engineering configures the connector and runs joint validation.

## A sample workflow

01:33 — VDS detects a person climbing a loading dock fence at a multi-tenant industrial property.
01:33 — SOC analyst verifies in 7 seconds.
01:33 — Webhook to Brivo fires. The four roll-up doors and the personnel door on that bay re-lock and switch to credentials-required schedule.
01:34 — VDS audio talk-down begins. Intruder leaves the dock.
01:35 — Tenant security manager opens the VDS app on iPhone. Sees the video, the talk-down audio log, and the Brivo door-state changes on one timeline.
01:38 — Manager unlocks the personnel door from Brivo to let arriving private security in. Unlock event lands on the VDS timeline automatically.

## Pricing

The Brivo integration is included with any AI VisionStream enterprise subscription. Brivo licensing follows standard Brivo pricing — VDS does not resell.

seoTitle: VDS + Immix CC Integration | Central Station Automation
metaDescription: VDS forwards verified alerts with video and metadata to your Immix-running central station. Operators dispatch from one console.
h1: VDS + Immix CC
heroSubhead: For customers whose alerts are monitored by a central station running Immix CC, VDS forwards verified events with pre/post video clips and full metadata. The Immix operator dispatches from one console with everything attached.
heroStats: Immix CC integration · Video + metadata forwarding · HTTPS POST · HMAC signed
body:
A lot of enterprise customers do not staff their own monitoring center. They contract that work to a UL-listed central station whose operators run Immix CC across hundreds of accounts. VDS plugs into that model without forcing a workflow change on either side.

## How it works

When the VDS SOC verifies a critical event — or when a customer has elected to bypass the VDS SOC and route events directly to their central station — the event posts into Immix CC as a verified alarm signal with:

- A linked pre-event and post-event video clip (signed, time-limited URLs)
- Detection class, zone name, GPS coordinates of the camera or trailer
- Confidence score and SOC analyst verification ID (when VDS SOC handled the event)
- Site contact and dispatch instructions

The Immix operator sees the event in their normal queue. Standard Immix workflows — contact tree, dispatch decision, customer notification — proceed without modification.

## What you get

- Use your existing monitoring partner. No need to switch central stations.
- Video and metadata travel with the alarm — operators do not log into a second portal.
- Verified events only, which means the central station bills less time per account and your false-alarm fees stay down.
- Optional dual-path: VDS SOC handles first response, Immix-running CS handles escalation, or the reverse.

## Setup time

For a central station already running Immix CC: 3 to 5 business days. Required on customer side: written authorization to share account data with the CS, the CS's Immix tenant identifier and account-mapping document. VDS engineering coordinates directly with the central station to configure the integration.

## A sample workflow

23:51 — VDS detects loitering at the rear of a retail location after closing.
23:51 — VDS SOC analyst verifies in 11 seconds. The customer's account is configured to route to a contracted Immix-running central station.
23:51 — Event posts to Immix CC. The CS operator sees the signal with linked video.
23:52 — Operator reviews the 30-second pre-event clip, confirms the behavior matches a loitering pattern previously associated with break-in attempts at this chain.
23:53 — CS operator dispatches local LE per the customer's response plan and notifies the store manager via SMS using the Immix contact tree.
23:54 — LE en route. VDS continues audio talk-down. Both systems retain a synchronized audit record.

## Pricing

The Immix integration is included with any AI VisionStream enterprise subscription. The central station's Immix licensing and the customer's monitoring contract are separate commercial relationships not touched by VDS.

faq.q: Does our central station need to do work on their side?
faq.a: Yes — they configure VDS as a video receiver / signal source in their Immix tenant. Most stations have done this for other video providers and the setup is routine.

faq.q: Can the central station talk-down through VDS cameras?
faq.a: Yes, with the right account configuration. Talk-down audio is initiated from the VDS console; central station operators get console access scoped to the accounts they monitor.

faq.q: Is this UL listing-relevant?

body:
For organizations whose security operations team and IT operations team share a ticketing queue, VDS sends events where the work actually happens: ServiceNow. Every critical AI VisionStream alert becomes a properly classified, properly assigned, properly tracked incident.

## How it works

VDS uses the ServiceNow Table API (REST) with OAuth 2.0 to create Incident records when a critical event is verified. Each record includes:

- Short description and detailed description with SOC analyst notes
- Linked video clip URLs (signed, time-limited) attached or referenced
- Detection class, zone, GPS coordinates, and customer site code
- CMDB CI reference if the camera or trailer is registered as a configuration item
- Priority, assignment group, and category mapped per the customer's ITSM schema

The default mapping ships sensible — critical intrusion → P1, after-hours loitering → P3 — and is customizable per site or per zone. Updates flow both ways: a state change in ServiceNow (acknowledged, in progress, resolved) reflects on the VDS incident timeline via the ServiceNow Business Rule webhook back to VDS.

## What you get

- Security events tracked in the same system as IT incidents — one SLA, one auditor view
- CMDB-aware tickets so an asset team can see when a camera or trailer needs maintenance because of a tamper or offline event
- VDS critical alerts never get lost in email; they exist as tickets with owners
- Bidirectional state sync, so closing in ServiceNow closes in VDS

## Setup time

For a customer with an existing ServiceNow instance and an OAuth application registration capability: 3 to 7 business days. Required on customer side: a ServiceNow service account with itil and rest_service roles, an OAuth client, the target table (typically incident), and the field-mapping document. VDS engineering provides the integration configuration and joint testing.

## A sample workflow

20:18 — VDS detects perimeter intrusion at a regional data center.
20:18 — SOC analyst verifies in 7 seconds; talk-down initiated.
20:18 — ServiceNow Incident INC0042319 auto-created: P1, assigned to "Physical Security Operations" group, linked to CI dc-perimeter-cam-07, video clip attached, SOC analyst note in the work-notes field.
20:19 — On-call physical security engineer acknowledges in ServiceNow. State change webhooks back to VDS; VDS timeline shows "acknowledged by J. Patel."
20:24 — LE on-scene, intruder gone. Engineer resolves the ServiceNow incident with notes; resolution syncs back to VDS.
20:25 — Both systems hold the closed record with full SLA timing.

## Pricing

The ServiceNow integration is included with any AI VisionStream enterprise subscription. ServiceNow licensing follows standard ServiceNow pricing — VDS does not resell.

faq.q: Which ServiceNow editions are supported?
faq.a: ITSM and ITOM. Most modern releases (Vancouver, Washington, Xanadu) are supported. The integration uses standard Table API surfaces.

faq.q: Can we route different VDS event types to different assignment groups?
faq.a: Yes. The mapping is configurable per site, per zone, and per detection class.

faq.q: Will this create ticket spam?
faq.a: No. Only verified critical events generate tickets by default. Routine VDS activity (system health, low-confidence detections) stays in the VDS console unless you opt to surface it.

faq.q: What about non-ITSM tools — Jira, PagerDuty?
faq.a: Same webhook pattern works for any system with an HTTPS endpoint. Jira and PagerDuty connectors are available on the same enterprise tier; talk to us for current status.

seoTitle: VDS + Axon-Fusus Integration | Opt-In Per-Incident LE
metaDescription: VDS customers share specific incident clips with local law enforcement running Axon-Fusus. Opt-in per incident — never standing access to your cameras.
h1: VDS + Axon-Fusus
heroSubhead: Share the clip law enforcement needs — and nothing else. VDS customers can opt-in per incident to push a specific video segment to a local Axon-Fusus real-time crime center. There is no standing camera access, no always-on feed, no exception.
heroStats: Per-incident opt-in · No standing access · Customer-controlled · TLS 1.3
body:
Axon-Fusus (acquired by Axon in 2024) is the leading real-time crime center platform for US law enforcement agencies. It can ingest live and recorded video from private cameras the property owner has elected to share. VDS supports that elective sharing — and only that. The integration is built around an explicit privacy principle: per-incident, opt-in, narrowly scoped.

## How it works

When a VDS customer has a clip relevant to an active LE investigation — a break-in, a hit-and-run, a missing person — an authorized user on the customer side opens the VDS console, selects the relevant time window from the camera in question, and chooses **Share with LE (Axon-Fusus)**.

That action does three things:

1. Generates a signed, time-limited video clip URL scoped to that single segment from that single camera.
2. Posts the clip into the specified Axon-Fusus tenant for the specified agency, with the customer's case reference and contact information.
3. Logs the share event to the VDS immutable audit record — who shared, what was shared, when, with which agency.

There is no live feed published. No agency-managed access to your cameras. No "subscribe to this property" toggle on the LE side. Every share is a discrete event initiated by your team, recorded against your name.

## What you get

- A documented, auditable path for cooperating with active law enforcement investigations
- Bounded sharing — agencies see the clip you sent, not your camera tree
- Full audit record of every clip shared, retained for the standard VDS 12-month window
- A clear answer for tenants, employees, and the general public when they ask: "Do the police have access to your cameras?" The answer is no, with a documented mechanism that backs it up.

## Setup time

2 to 4 business days. Required on customer side: the Axon-Fusus tenant identifier(s) for the agencies you want to be able to send to, a written policy on who in your organization is authorized to initiate a share, and an internal approver if your policy requires two-person rule. VDS engineering provisions the integration and applies your authorization rules to the console.

## A sample workflow

14:22 — A vehicle strikes a pedestrian in the parking lot of a customer's retail location and leaves the scene.
14:30 — Local PD opens an investigation and contacts the customer's loss prevention lead.
14:34 — LP lead reviews VDS footage, locates the relevant 90-second segment showing the vehicle and plate.
14:35 — LP lead clicks **Share with LE (Axon-Fusus)**, selects the local PD's Fusus tenant, enters the police case number.
14:35 — Clip posts into the agency's Fusus environment. VDS audit log records: "Shared 14:33:10–14:34:40 of Camera Lot-7 with [Agency] case 26-04829 by [User]."
14:38 — Detective reviews the clip in Fusus alongside other case material. The customer's broader camera footprint remains private.

## Pricing

The Axon-Fusus integration is included with any AI VisionStream enterprise subscription. Axon-Fusus licensing on the agency side is separate and is not paid by the customer or by VDS.

## On the privacy principle

A lot of community-camera programs operate on a standing-access model: an agency, once authorized, can view a property's cameras at any time. VDS does not support that model on Axon-Fusus or anywhere else. Two reasons. First, it muddies legal questions about reasonable expectation of privacy for tenants, employees, customers, and visitors. Second, it makes the property owner's policy ambiguous in a way that produces avoidable complaints. Per-incident opt-in is clearer for everyone — including the responding officer, who arrives with a clean evidentiary chain.

faq.q: Can law enforcement request standing access through this integration?
faq.a: No. The integration only supports per-incident, customer-initiated sharing. There is no standing-access mode and no plan to add one.

faq.q: What if LE has a subpoena or warrant?
faq.a: Subpoena and warrant responses go through your normal legal process. VDS supports lawful evidentiary requests with full chain-of-custody export — that is separate from the Axon-Fusus integration, which is for voluntary, expedited sharing of a specific clip.

faq.q: Who in our organization can initiate a share?
faq.a: Whoever you authorize. Most customers limit it to a named loss prevention or security lead and require a second approver for non-emergencies.

faq.q: Does the shared clip include metadata identifying our location, cameras, or people?
faq.a: The clip is shared as a video file with the case context your team enters. No camera ID, customer ID, or system metadata is exposed to the agency beyond what you choose to include in the case reference.

finalCTAHeading: Cooperate with law enforcement without giving away your camera tree.
finalCTABody: A 30-minute call covers your sharing policy, your authorized users, and the agencies you want to be able to send to. You leave with a written authorization document and a setup-time estimate.

body:
## Three deployment tiers, mapped to drive time from staging

VDS operates a hub-and-spoke logistics model anchored at our Pikesville, Maryland headquarters with regional staging in Texas and additional secondary sites added as deployment density warrants. Trailer dispatch SLA is a function of distance from staging, permitting requirements, and current fleet utilization — not a marketing tier.

### Same-day deployment (under 12 hours from contract)

Available in Maryland, Washington DC, Northern Virginia (Loudoun, Fairfax, Prince William, Arlington, Alexandria), and Southern Pennsylvania (Lancaster, York, Chester, Delaware, Philadelphia, Bucks, Montgomery counties).

For sites inside this radius, a Sky Guard MSU or Boundary Guard Pro trailer can be on the ground, solar-aligned, cellular-connected, and registered with the 24/7 SOC inside 12 hours of contract signature. We hold standing inventory at the Pikesville depot specifically to support same-day calls.

### 24-72 hour deployment

Available across the rest of the Eastern Seaboard (NY, NJ, CT, MA, RI, NH, VT, ME, DE, WV, NC, SC, GA, FL), the Midwest corridor (OH, IN, MI, KY, TN), and all of Texas (Dallas, Houston, San Antonio, Austin, El Paso metros).

These deployments dispatch via flatbed from the closest staging hub. We commit to a 72-hour ceiling and average 41 hours from PO to operational across this footprint based on 2025 deployment data.

### Standard deployment (5-10 business days)

Available across the remaining states we serve: AL, MS, LA, AR, OK, MO, IL, WI, MN, IA, KS, CO, AZ, NV, UT, NM, plus pilot footprint in CA and WA.

Standard scheduling reflects long-haul transport, permit lead times in some jurisdictions, and pre-deployment site survey scheduling. Quoted in business days, tracked in your customer portal from PO through GPS arrival ping.

## What "deployment" actually means at VDS

A deployment is not a drop-and-leave. Every trailer arrival includes:

- Site survey verification against the pre-deployment design
- Solar panel orientation and tilt set against latitude
- Cellular signal validation (we require >-95 dBm RSRP for primary carrier)
- Camera azimuth and detection-zone calibration
- SOC handshake — analytics live, talk-down audio tested, escalation tree confirmed
- Customer portal account provisioning with RBAC roles assigned

Deployment is not complete until the SOC dashboard shows the unit green and the first test alert routes correctly.

## Don't see your state?

We expand based on demand. If you operate a multi-site program in a state outside the current 30+ footprint, our deployment engineering team will scope what regional staging and dispatch logistics would cost for your portfolio.

Three of our current standard-tier states were added in 2024-2025 because a single enterprise customer asked. We are not interested in symbolic national coverage — we add states when the operational math works.

faq.q: Can VDS deploy across state lines for a single program?
faq.a: Yes. Multi-state portfolios are common — a GC running projects in MD, VA, and NC can run all three sites on one master service agreement, one SOC dashboard, one invoice.

faq.q: Does VDS handle deployments in Canada or Mexico?
faq.a: Not currently. Our hardware is NDAA Section 889 compliant and our SOC is US-based. International expansion is on the 2027 roadmap pending regulatory review.

faq.q: How is "same-day" measured?
faq.a: Contract countersignature to first SOC alert acknowledgement on the deployed unit. We post the actual median weekly inside the customer portal.

faq.a: We carry dual-carrier modems (Verizon + AT&T) and have deployed Starlink-equipped trailers for sites under -110 dBm on both carriers. Quoted as an upgrade line item.

metaDescription: Emergency response, post-incident surge coverage, severe-weather redeployment, special events, government temporary operations
h1: Tactical Deployments
heroSubhead: Mobile surveillance trailers on-site in 24-72 hours for incident response, weather redeployment, special events, and government temporary operations. Weekly or event-based billing — no 12-month contract required.
body:
## This is not the steady-state product

Most VDS deployments are 12-month or longer programs — a construction site through completion, an auto dealership year-round, a utility substation indefinitely. Tactical is the opposite use case: short-duration, time-critical, often unpredictable.

We built the tactical practice because customers kept calling us. A retail district had three smash-and-grab incidents in a week and needed cameras up by Friday. A municipality needed surge coverage after a homicide cleared an evidence radius. A utility had to redeploy crews and equipment to a substation after Hurricane Helene took out two of theirs.

The hardware is identical to our steady-state fleet. The operating model is different.

## What tactical deployments cover

### Post-incident surge coverage
A theft, vandalism, assault, or other documented incident has occurred. The customer needs visible deterrent and forensic coverage at the affected site within days, not weeks. Typical duration: 30-90 days, sometimes longer if criminal proceedings extend the evidence window.

### Severe weather and disaster response
Hurricanes, wildfires, ice storms, and tornadoes displace assets, open security gaps, and create staging areas that didn't exist 48 hours earlier. VDS has deployed mobile units for utility mutual-aid staging, FEMA contractor camps, and temporary materials laydown yards after major weather events. Solar-autonomous matters here — grid power may be out for weeks.

### Special events
Festivals, large public gatherings, sporting events, political conventions. Cameras need to be up the day before crowds arrive and gone the day after. Permitting is usually handled by the event host; we plug into the existing security command structure.

### Government and law enforcement temporary operations
Task force operations, surge deployments to high-incident corridors, temporary checkpoints, evidence-recovery perimeters. LE customers get a dedicated channel to our SOC and direct radio integration with on-scene units when operationally appropriate. NDAA Section 889 compliance matters here — many of these contracts require it.

### Construction phase coverage gaps
A long project has a 60-day window where the permanent system is being retrofitted, or a phase hand-off creates a temporary blind spot. Tactical fills it without restructuring the master agreement.

## How tactical billing works

Tactical deployments are quoted at a weekly rate or an event-based fixed fee — not the monthly subscription pricing on our steady-state product pages. Typical structures:

- **Weekly trailer rate** — flat per-week through end of deployment, minimum two weeks
- **Event fixed fee** — agreed up front for a defined start/end window
- **Emergency surge pricing** — applies when deployment is requested inside 24 hours

The 24/7 SOC, AI VisionStream analytics, audio talk-down, and LE dispatch are included on every tactical deployment. Cloud retention defaults to 30 days; longer retention available as an upgrade if evidentiary preservation is a known requirement.

## What we will and won't accept

We accept tactical engagements where the operating profile is clear, the site is accessible to a flatbed delivery, and there is a documented stakeholder on the customer side empowered to authorize SOC escalation protocols.

We decline tactical engagements that are functionally surveillance of identified individuals without legal process, deployments to private property without verified authorization, or anything that would put our SOC operators in a position of making law enforcement judgment calls. The SOC follows escalation trees — it does not improvise.

faq.q: How fast can you really deploy?
faq.a: Inside our same-day footprint (MD/DC/N.VA/S.PA), under 12 hours from PO. Nationwide ceiling is 72 hours. Median over 2025 for tactical calls was 38 hours.

faq.q: Can I extend a tactical deployment into a steady-state contract?
faq.a: Yes — and it's common. About 30% of tactical deployments convert to monthly subscription before the initial window ends.

faq.q: Do you require a site survey before tactical deployment?
faq.a: We do a remote survey using satellite imagery and customer-provided site photos. Physical pre-deployment survey is waived for tactical to compress timelines; final positioning is set on arrival.

faq.q: What's the minimum tactical engagement?
faq.a: Two weeks. Shorter windows are not operationally efficient on either side.

finalCTAHeading: Need a Trailer on Site This Week?
finalCTABody: Tell us the site, the trigger, and the timeline. Tactical engagements get a same-business-day quote and a deployment-ops point of contact assigned within the hour.

heroSubhead: One trailer, one site, 30 days. Full SOC monitoring, AI VisionStream analytics, audio talk-down, LE dispatch — all included. No setup fee. Qualifying multi-site programs only.
body:
## A pilot is the only honest sales process for this product

Mobile surveillance is operational hardware. You can't evaluate it from a PDF or a demo. The question is whether the trailer goes up, the analytics fire correctly on your specific site conditions, the SOC routes alerts the way your team needs them, and the 30-day data confirms or contradicts the case we're making.

VDS runs structured pilots for qualifying programs because we'd rather lose a deal in 30 days at one site than lose a deal at 12 months across a portfolio.

## What's in a pilot

**Hardware:** One Sky Guard MSU, Swift Deploy, or Boundary Guard Pro — chosen against your site profile by our deployment engineering team. Solar-autonomous, cellular-connected, NDAA Section 889 compliant.

**Monitoring:** Full 24/7 US-based SOC. <60-second escalation. AI VisionStream analytics. Audio talk-down. Law enforcement dispatch when authorized. Customer portal access for your team.

**Data:** 30-day cloud retention. Weekly metrics report. Final pilot review at day 30 with measured outcomes — alert volume, false-alarm rate, deterrent events, response timing.

**What you don't pay:** Setup, deployment logistics, SOC monitoring fees, analytics, software. You pay the trailer-month rate only — $2,200 for Sky Guard MSU, $1,500 for Swift Deploy, $1,800 for Boundary Guard Pro. One month. That's it.

## Qualifying criteria

We run a finite number of pilots each quarter and prioritize programs where a successful pilot converts to a multi-site engagement.

### What we look for

- **Enterprise multi-site potential** — three or more sites would convert if the pilot performs
- **Vertical fit** — construction (GCs, developers, materials yards), utilities (substations, equipment laydown), auto (dealerships, fleet lots), retail (lots, distribution centers), critical infrastructure
- **Geographic fit** — site inside our 30+ state footprint with a defined deployment tier
- **Authorized buyer engaged** — pilot stakeholder has authority to convert to contract if outcomes meet criteria
- **Defined success metrics** — we agree what "successful pilot" means before the trailer arrives

### What disqualifies a pilot

Single-site small business, residential, sites outside our service area, requests for free product without a defined conversion path. We are not a free demo service.

## How the pilot runs

**Week 1 — Deployment and tuning.** Trailer arrives, solar and cellular validated, analytics calibrated to your site. SOC escalation tree built with your team. First baseline metrics captured.

**Weeks 2-3 — Operational data collection.** SOC operates the site under live conditions. Weekly metrics report delivered every Friday. Pilot engineer available for tuning, threshold adjustments, escalation tree refinements.

**Week 4 — Review and decision.** Day-30 report compares pilot outcomes against the agreed success metrics. Pilot engineer walks your team through alert volume, false alarm rate, deterrent events, and any LE dispatch incidents.

If outcomes meet criteria, we move to multi-site contract conversation. If not, the trailer demobilizes — no obligation, no extended commitment. You keep the data and the report.

## What pilots have produced

A Mid-Atlantic GC piloted one Sky Guard MSU at a $28M project in 2023. Over the 12-month engagement that followed, theft incidents dropped 73%, insurance claims went to zero, and the customer documented $340,800 in saved losses. That portfolio has since expanded to multiple active sites under the same MSA.

Not every pilot converts. The ones that don't usually fail the site-fit test in week one — wrong camera positions, wrong analytics profile, wrong customer expectations. Pilots are how we surface those failures before contracts get signed, not after.

Construction theft and vandalism losses crossed $1B annually in the US in 2024 by NICB tracking — and that's the reported, claimed figure, not the full operational loss. Builder's risk, commercial property, inland marine, and fleet lines all carry the exposure. Auto dealership open-lot coverage is its own conversation.

Most carriers' risk engineering teams already have a position on "site monitoring credit" — what they don't always have is a vendor that produces the documentation their underwriters will actually accept at portfolio scale.

VDS works with carriers and brokers to fill that gap.

## What carriers and brokers get from a VDS partnership

### Documented site monitoring evidence

Every VDS deployment produces a verifiable monitoring footprint: deployment date, trailer GPS location, SOC monitoring confirmation, AI VisionStream analytics record, alert log, audio talk-down event count, LE dispatch records. This is the documentation underwriters need to approve a premium credit and that claims adjusters use during loss investigation.

### A vendor your risk engineering team can field-validate

Risk engineers can run a deployment pilot at a representative insured site — same 30-day structure as our standard pilot — and validate that the operational performance matches the underwriting assumption. Field-validated, not assumed.

### NDAA Section 889 compliance for federal-adjacent insureds

Carriers writing federal contractors, defense suppliers, or grant-funded infrastructure projects need vendors whose hardware clears Section 889. VDS attests to that compliance. AWS US-only data residency closes the loop for carriers with data sovereignty requirements.

### Single-vendor coverage across the 30+ state footprint

Insureds operate across state lines. A carrier program that names VDS gets one vendor, one MSA structure, one SOC, and consistent monitoring evidence regardless of which state any given insured site sits in.

## The buyer profiles we work with

### Carrier risk engineering teams

National accounts and construction practice risk engineers at carriers including (we work with carriers comparable to) Travelers, Zurich, Liberty Mutual, AIG, Chubb, Sompo, Berkley, and others. The conversation starts with whether your team has a documented monitoring credit on the line you write, and whether VDS can be specified or recommended within that program.

### Wholesale and retail brokers with portfolio exposure

Brokers placing builder's risk for a GC with 40 active projects, or commercial property for a dealer group with 18 lots, or fleet for an interstate logistics operator. VDS becomes the recommended monitoring vendor inside the broker's stewardship program — the insured gets a credit, the broker delivers value, the carrier gets risk reduction documented in the file.

### Captive insurers and risk retention groups

Construction and trade-association captives often have more flexibility to structure monitoring requirements directly into coverage terms. VDS works with captive risk managers to scope program economics.

## What a carrier program partnership looks like operationally

We do not pay referral fees, kickbacks, or commissions. Carrier program partnerships are structured around:

- Documented endorsement or recommendation pathway from carrier or broker to insured
- Standardized deployment package and pricing for program-eligible insureds
- Risk engineering field validation at representative sites
- Monthly portfolio reporting to the carrier or broker on deployed sites, monitoring events, and loss-avoidance documentation where available

Insureds remain the contracting customer of VDS. The carrier or broker drives recommendation, not procurement.

A $28M Mid-Atlantic GC project deployed Sky Guard MSU under SOC monitoring. Twelve-month outcomes documented:

- 73% reduction in theft and vandalism incidents versus the customer's prior-project baseline
- Zero insurance claims filed across the deployment window
- $340,800 in documented loss avoidance, audited by the customer's controller

That's one project, one trailer, one carrier whose claims line never saw the case. Multiplied across a portfolio program, the underwriting math is straightforward.

seoTitle: VDS Cybersecurity — TLS 1.3, AES-256, MFA, SAML SSO
metaDescription: Vision Detection Systems cybersecurity controls: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, RBAC with MFA, SAML/OIDC SSO, IP allowlisting
h1: Cybersecurity Controls
heroSubhead: The technical controls that govern how VDS protects video, metadata, customer accounts, and SOC operations against unauthorized access and modification.
body:
## Encryption

### In transit
All traffic between deployed VDS hardware, the AI VisionStream cloud platform, the customer portal, and SOC operator workstations runs over TLS 1.3. We do not accept TLS 1.0 or 1.1 connections at any tier. Cipher suite selection follows current NIST and IETF guidance — forward secrecy is required, RC4 and 3DES are blocked, weak Diffie-Hellman groups are blocked.

Cellular uplink from trailer to AWS ingress uses dual-encryption: the carrier's LTE/5G link encryption plus our application-layer TLS 1.3 wrapper. We do not depend on carrier link encryption alone.

### At rest
All stored video, analytics output, audit log entries, and customer metadata are encrypted at rest with AES-256. Encryption keys are managed in AWS KMS under customer-isolated key hierarchies. Key rotation runs on a defined schedule and on-demand if a compromise is suspected. No customer data sits unencrypted on any VDS-controlled storage at any point.

## Authentication and access control

### Role-based access control (RBAC)
Every customer portal account is assigned a role: Account Owner, Site Manager, Operator, Read-Only, Auditor. Each role maps to a defined permission set covering camera access, alert acknowledgement, video export, user management, and audit log visibility. Roles are configured by the customer's Account Owner — VDS does not assign portal roles inside customer tenants.

### Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
MFA is required for all administrative roles and available for all roles. TOTP (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password) is supported standard. WebAuthn / FIDO2 hardware keys are supported and recommended for Account Owner accounts.

### Single sign-on
Enterprise customers can federate the VDS portal to their identity provider via SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect. We have completed integrations with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Ping Identity, and JumpCloud. Just-in-time provisioning and SCIM user lifecycle management are supported on enterprise plans.

### IP allowlisting
Customer portal access can be restricted to defined IP ranges or CIDR blocks at the tenant level. SOC operator access is always restricted to VDS-managed network egress; we do not allow SOC operations from arbitrary IPs.

## Audit log

Every authentication event, configuration change, video access event, alert acknowledgement, and administrative action is written to an immutable audit log retained for 12 months minimum. The log is append-only — there is no operator function that can edit or delete entries.

Customers can export the audit log to CSV or stream it via webhook to a SIEM. We have customers feeding the log into Splunk, Datadog, and Microsoft Sentinel.

## Penetration testing

VDS contracts an independent third-party penetration test annually, covering the AI VisionStream cloud platform, customer portal, mobile applications, and deployed trailer ingress. Test methodology follows OWASP ASVS Level 2 minimum and NIST SP 800-115 process guidelines. The most recent test was completed in Q4 2025; the next is scheduled for Q4 2026.

Findings are remediated on a severity-based schedule: critical findings within 7 days, high within 30, medium within 90. The summary report is available under NDA to enterprise customers' security teams.

## Vulnerability disclosure

VDS operates a responsible-disclosure program for security researchers. Reports route to security@visiondetectionsystems.com with PGP encryption supported. We acknowledge inbound reports within two business days, triage to a severity within five, and commit to coordinated disclosure on a timeline appropriate to the finding.

We do not currently operate a paid bug bounty. We do credit researchers on a Hall of Fame page when they request public acknowledgement and the report meets quality criteria.

## Hardware and field operations

Deployed trailers run a hardened Linux operating system. Remote SSH is disabled by default; out-of-band management runs through a dedicated, mutually-authenticated channel. Firmware updates are signed, verified, and applied during defined maintenance windows. We do not push unsigned firmware. Ever.

Trailers do not store customer video locally beyond a short rolling buffer; primary storage is cloud-side under AWS US-only regions.

seoTitle: VDS Data Privacy — US-Only AWS, CCPA, BIPA-Friendly
metaDescription: How Vision Detection Systems handles customer data. AWS US-only residency, tenant isolation, no biometrics or facial recognition, CCPA-compliant
h1: Data Privacy and Handling
heroSubhead: How VDS collects, stores, processes, retains, and deletes customer video and metadata. Where the data lives. What we will and will not do with it.
body:
## Where customer data lives

All VDS customer data — video, analytics output, audit logs, account metadata — is stored exclusively in AWS US-East and US-West regions. We do not replicate, mirror, or back up customer data to any non-US AWS region or any non-AWS infrastructure.

This is a contractual commitment, not a default that can drift. The AWS account configuration enforces region restriction at the IAM and bucket policy level. A misconfigured deployment cannot accidentally land data outside the US footprint.

## Tenant isolation

Each customer operates in a logically isolated tenant. Customer A's video, analytics, and metadata are not accessible to Customer B's portal users, Customer B's SOC dashboards, or Customer B's API tokens — ever. Tenant boundaries are enforced at the application layer, the database layer (row-level security on shared tables, customer-specific keys on object storage), and the audit layer.

VDS internal personnel access to customer data is limited to SOC operators handling active alerts and the small set of platform engineering staff who maintain the underlying infrastructure. Every internal access event is logged to the customer's audit log if it touches their tenant.

## What VDS does not do with customer data

We do not share customer video, analytics output, or metadata with any third party without explicit customer authorization. This includes:

- We do not sell or license customer data for analytics, training, or any other secondary purpose
- We do not aggregate identifiable customer footage into training datasets for our AI VisionStream models — model training uses synthetic and licensed datasets
- We do not provide customer data to law enforcement absent a valid subpoena, court order, or customer authorization (and we notify the customer when we receive such a request unless legally prohibited)
- We do not use customer video for marketing, case studies, or promotional materials without an executed release

## Biometrics, facial recognition, and BIPA

VDS AI VisionStream performs object detection (person, vehicle), license plate recognition (LPR), behavior analytics (loitering, perimeter breach), and scene classification. It does not perform facial recognition, biometric identification, or biometric template generation.

This is a deliberate product position. It keeps VDS clear of Illinois BIPA exposure, Texas CUBI exposure, Washington WBPA exposure, and the patchwork of city-level facial recognition bans (Portland OR, San Francisco, Boston, others). It also reflects an operating principle: license plates and behavior patterns are tools we need, biometric identification is not.

If a customer requests facial recognition as a feature, the answer is no. We will not add it.

## CCPA, GDPR, and regulatory posture

### California (CCPA / CPRA)
VDS treats CCPA as a baseline for all US customers regardless of state. We honor verifiable consumer requests for access, deletion, and correction. We do not sell personal information as defined under CCPA. Service provider agreements are in place with all sub-processors.

### Other state privacy laws
VDS complies with comparable state privacy regimes including VCDPA (Virginia), CPA (Colorado), CTDPA (Connecticut), UCPA (Utah), and others as they come into force. We track the state-by-state landscape and update our practices ahead of effective dates.

### GDPR-adjacent practices
VDS does not currently offer services to EU-resident customers, but we follow GDPR-adjacent principles — purpose limitation, data minimization, lawful basis documentation, breach notification timelines — as a baseline. If you are a US-based enterprise with EU operations and need GDPR-equivalent documentation for a global program, talk to us.

## Retention and deletion

### Default retention
Video and analytics data: 30, 60, or 90 days based on customer plan. Audit logs: 12 months minimum, longer on enterprise plans or by contract. Account metadata: retained for the duration of the customer relationship plus the regulatory hold period.

### Customer-initiated deletion
Customers can request deletion of specific video segments, full site data, or full account data at any time. Deletion executes within 30 days, with cryptographic destruction of the underlying encryption keys to render any residual storage unrecoverable.

### Contract termination
On termination, customer data is exportable for 60 days. After 60 days, all customer data is purged from primary and backup storage within 30 additional days. Termination data destruction is logged and a destruction certificate provided on request.

faq.q: Can I get a copy of all data you hold on my organization?
faq.a: Yes — export is built into the customer portal for video, analytics, and audit log. Account metadata export is a support request, fulfilled within 10 business days.

faq.q: What happens if law enforcement requests our video?
faq.a: We require valid legal process. We notify the customer unless a court order specifically prohibits notification. We do not provide voluntary access.

faq.q: Do you have sub-processors?
faq.a: Yes — AWS for hosting, plus a small set of operational tools. Full sub-processor list is in the DPA and updated when changes are made.

seoTitle: VDS SLA — 99.9% Platform Uptime, <60s SOC Response
metaDescription: Vision Detection Systems service-level commitments: 99.9% AI VisionStream platform uptime, sub-60-second SOC alert acknowledgement, hardware MTTR targets
h1: Service Level Agreement and Uptime
heroSubhead: The service commitments VDS makes operationally and contractually — platform uptime, SOC response, hardware response, and what happens when we miss.
body:
## Platform availability

### Target: 99.9% monthly uptime
AI VisionStream cloud platform — the camera-agnostic VMS, analytics processing, customer portal, and API — runs to a 99.9% monthly uptime target measured against the customer portal availability endpoint.

99.9% per calendar month allows a maximum of approximately 43 minutes of accumulated downtime. Scheduled maintenance windows announced 7+ days in advance are excluded from the calculation; emergency maintenance is included.

### Measurement
Uptime is measured by an external synthetic monitor running from three geographically separated AWS regions at one-minute intervals. The public status page shows real-time and historical uptime against the SLA target. Customers receive monthly uptime reports automatically on enterprise plans; available on request on standard plans.

## SOC response

### Target: <60 seconds alert acknowledgement
Every AI VisionStream alert routed to the SOC is acknowledged by a live US-based operator in under 60 seconds, measured from alert arrival at the SOC queue to operator acknowledgement. This is the SOC's single most-tracked operational metric.

2025 full-year median: 14 seconds. 95th percentile: 38 seconds. 99th percentile: 71 seconds. The handful of >60-second events are post-incident reviewed and root-caused.

### Escalation timing
After acknowledgement, the operator follows the customer's defined escalation tree: video verification, audio talk-down where authorized, on-site contact notification, and law enforcement dispatch when criteria are met. Escalation timing depends on the action — talk-down is typically inside two minutes of alert, LE dispatch is a function of how fast PSAP answers.

## Hardware response

### Mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) on field issues
For trailer hardware issues — sensor fault, cellular degradation, solar performance, physical damage — VDS targets:

- **Critical (unit offline):** Remote diagnosis inside 2 hours, field response inside 24 hours
- **Major (degraded operation):** Remote diagnosis inside 4 business hours, field response inside 72 hours
- **Minor (non-impacting fault):** Remote diagnosis next business day, field response inside 10 business days

MTTR is measured from customer ticket open to issue resolution in the customer portal. Reported monthly on enterprise plans.

## Credit policy

### Platform uptime miss
If AI VisionStream monthly uptime falls below the 99.9% target, customers receive a service credit calculated against the affected service month:

- 99.0% - 99.9% uptime: 10% credit
- 95.0% - 98.99% uptime: 25% credit
- Below 95.0% uptime: 50% credit

Credits are applied to the following month's invoice automatically — no claim form required on enterprise plans. Standard plan credits are filed via support ticket.

### SOC response SLA miss
If SOC median monthly response exceeds the 60-second target, affected customers receive a 10% credit of the SOC service component for that month. Per-incident credits for individual late responses are not standard; pattern misses trigger the credit.

### Hardware response SLA miss
Hardware response misses are credited per-incident under enterprise plans; standard plan hardware response is best-effort against published targets.

## What's excluded from SLA

Following industry standard:

- Force majeure events (natural disasters, regional carrier outages outside our control)
- Customer-caused issues (network changes, account misconfiguration, denial of cellular service at the carrier level)
- Scheduled maintenance announced 7+ days in advance
- Beta or pilot features explicitly designated as not under SLA

faq.q: Where is the public status page?
faq.a: status.visiondetectionsystems.com — link in this page footer. Subscribe by email or RSS for incident notifications.

faq.q: How is the 60-second SOC target measured?
faq.a: Time from alert arrival at the SOC queue to live operator acknowledgement, captured in the SOC tooling and audited monthly.

faq.q: Can I get a higher uptime commitment on enterprise plans?
faq.a: 99.95% is available on enterprise plans by contract amendment. The underlying architecture supports it; the elevated target reflects different credit math and is priced accordingly.

faq.q: What counts as an incident?
faq.a: Any unplanned event that degrades or interrupts platform availability or SOC operations affecting one or more customers. Posted to the status page within 15 minutes of detection.

finalCTABody: Enterprise and prospect security teams get the contractual SLA document, historical uptime data, and the credit policy worked example.

## Compliance attestations

### NDAA Section 889 compliance
VDS hardware and operational stack comply with National Defense Authorization Act Section 889(a)(1)(A) and 889(a)(1)(B). We do not use covered telecommunications equipment or services as defined under the statute. Attestation documentation is available for federal contractors, defense suppliers, grant-funded programs, and any prime contractor requiring 889 representations from their vendors.

This is not a marketing claim — it's a documented attestation, refreshed annually and tied to specific hardware bills-of-materials and operational architecture.

### State-level procurement compliance
VDS hardware is also compliant with state-level procurement restrictions on specific Chinese-manufactured camera brands (Hikvision, Dahua) that exist in Florida, Texas, Georgia, and other states. The compliance overlap with NDAA 889 is substantial but not identical — attestation documentation distinguishes both.

## Industry recognition

### Press mentions
VDS work has been referenced in industry publications covering construction security, mobile surveillance technology, and physical security operations. Specific press mention list is maintained on the press kit page and refreshed as new coverage publishes.

If you are a journalist or industry analyst looking for context, source documentation, or executive commentary, the press kit is the right starting point.

## Why this page exists

Most awards-and-recognition pages are vanity. This one is a procurement enabler. The Sourcewell contract reduces a public-sector buyer's procurement cycle by months. The AWS partnership shortens enterprise security review. The NDAA 889 attestation is the gate for federal-adjacent work.

If you are a procurement professional, security director, or program owner who needs documentation against one of these credentials, the form below routes to the team that can deliver it inside one business day.

faq.q: What does "AWS Cloud Partner" actually mean?
faq.a: It's a validated AWS Partner Network designation reflecting our technical alignment with AWS architecture, security, and operational practices. Verifiable through AWS's partner directory.

body:
## What this portal is for

VDS appears in capital project security specifications, RFP responses, and federal/state construction documents because architects, engineers, and security consultants put us there. This portal provides the documentation, technical drawings, and reference materials those professionals need to write VDS into a spec accurately — without having to chase a sales rep for every artifact.

If you spec security systems into commercial, institutional, or government construction documents, this is the page bookmark.

## CSI MasterFormat references

VDS mobile surveillance trailers and the AI VisionStream cloud VMS fit into the CSI MasterFormat under:

### Division 28 — Electronic Safety and Security

- **28 23 23 — Video Surveillance Remote Monitoring and Control** — applies to AI VisionStream cloud VMS, the customer portal, SOC monitoring services, and the camera-agnostic ONVIF/RTSP integration layer
- **28 23 29 — Video Surveillance Remote Storage and Retrieval** — applies to AWS-hosted 30/60/90-day cloud retention, video export, and forensic retrieval workflows

For temporary or mobile deployments specifically, we provide language that overlays Division 01 (General Requirements) procurement and Division 28 technical content. Sample spec language is included in the downloadable pack below.

### Related divisions
- Division 26 (Electrical) — typically not relevant for solar-autonomous deployments
- Division 33 (Utilities) — applicable for permanent communication infrastructure if cellular is supplemented by site fiber
- Division 27 (Communications) — applicable for site integration of cellular/satellite uplink

## Available specifier resources

### Spec sheet pack
Single download containing:
- Sky Guard MSU technical data sheet (dimensions, power, sensor payload, environmental ratings)
- Swift Deploy technical data sheet
- Boundary Guard Pro technical data sheet
- AI VisionStream platform specification (analytics capabilities, integration protocols, API documentation summary)
- 24/7 SOC service specification

### Revit / CAD models
3D Revit family files and 2D CAD blocks for site-plan integration. Current release covers Sky Guard MSU and Boundary Guard Pro deployment footprints with solar panel orientation and exclusion zones called out.

Available on request — release via secure download link, not public CDN, to keep version control clean.

### Sample specification language
Editable Word documents with CSI MasterFormat-formatted specification sections for each product line. Drop into your project specification with appropriate edits for project-specific scope and procurement structure.

### A&E presentation deck
60-90 minute presentation covering mobile surveillance technology, the VDS product line, SOC operations, deployment logistics, and case studies relevant to the audience type (institutional, federal, commercial). Delivered live by VDS engineering leadership.

We deliver these as in-person, remote, or hybrid sessions and offer AIA CES credit for qualifying audiences pending program approval.

## Dedicated specifier support

VDS maintains a dedicated A&E channel staffed by sales engineering, not general sales. Specifier inquiries route to engineers who have written spec language, sat on bid clarifications, and walked construction administration submittals through approval.

The channel responds to:
- Spec language drafting and review for specific projects
- Pre-RFP technical Q&A and substitution submittals
- Bid clarification questions during open-bid windows
- Construction administration submittal preparation
- Site-survey walk-throughs for projects in design

Contact details are provided after the A&E presentation request below to keep the inbox clean from non-specifier inbound.

## Why specifiers choose VDS

This is the operational, not marketing, version:

- **NDAA Section 889 attestation** clears the gate for federal projects and most state-level public construction
- **Sourcewell awarded contract holder** simplifies public agency procurement
- **Camera-agnostic VMS** means VDS can integrate with cameras the project owner already prefers or has specified separately — no proprietary lock-in
- **AWS US-only data residency** satisfies the data sovereignty language in federal and many state specs
- **Documented case data** — 500+ deployments, 30+ states, hero-case 73% theft reduction — gives specifiers reference projects when bid clarifications ask for prior work

faq.q: Do you provide AIA CES credit?
faq.a: Pending program approval — current target is to offer one continuing education hour for the standard A&E presentation by Q3 2026. Status confirmed in the presentation booking.

faq.q: Can I get sole-source justification language for a specific project?
faq.a: Yes. Sole-source justification documents are drafted on a per-project basis by sales engineering, tied to specific project requirements that distinguish VDS technically and operationally.

faq.q: Can VDS attend pre-bid meetings?
faq.a: Yes. Sales engineering attends pre-bid meetings remotely or in-person for projects in active design or bid phase. Request via the specifier channel.

faq.q: Do you offer substitution submittals?
faq.a: When VDS is named as an approved equal or named in an alternates list. We do not chase substitution submittals where another mobile surveillance vendor is sole-specified.

faq.q: How does the Revit model handle solar panel orientation?
faq.a: Solar panel orientation is parametric — set latitude and the model adjusts tilt and azimuth. Exclusion zones for solar access are included as a separate layer.

finalCTABody: Live presentation by VDS engineering, scoped to your audience and project pipeline. Specifier resources delivered alongside.

Most security-vendor content is written by marketing copywriters working off an interview transcript and a content brief. Every published article on visiondetectionsystems.com carries a named author from the operating team. Bios are factual: role, tenure, specific operational experience, professional credentials where relevant. We do not list pet names, favorite books, or college mascots. The audience is here for technical and operational credibility, not personality.

## Editorial standards

VDS content follows a defined editorial process:

- **Named author accountability** — every published article carries a single named author responsible for technical accuracy

- **Correction policy** — errors are corrected in-place with a dated correction notice; substantive corrections are noted at the article footer

We do not run articles ghostwritten by contract agencies. We do not publish syndicated content under VDS bylines. If an article appears under a VDS author name, that author wrote it or directly edited it.

h1: State of Mobile Surveillance in North America — 2026 Report
heroSubhead: 47 pages of field-measured operational data, sourced market analysis, and forward-looking observations on where mobile surveillance is going in 2026 and 2027. Free download for security professionals, risk managers, procurement, and journalists.
body:
## What's in the 2026 report

The State of Mobile Surveillance is VDS's annual industry analysis. It's free, it's cited, and it's intentionally structured for the audience that actually procures and operates these systems — security directors, construction risk managers, federal procurement officers, insurance carrier risk engineering teams, and the journalists covering the space.

### 1. 2026 mobile surveillance market sizing
North American mobile surveillance market estimate by segment — construction, utilities, government and municipal, retail and commercial, critical infrastructure. Methodology disclosed: which third-party market research firms' baselines we triangulated, what assumptions we adjusted, where we disagree with consensus and why.

### 2. Organized retail crime trends (NRF data + VDS observations)
2025 NRF National Retail Security Survey figures on retail crime losses, organized retail crime (ORC) incidents, and the security technology adoption patterns retailers are actually executing. VDS field observations from 80+ retail deployment sites across 14 states overlay where our data agrees with — and contradicts — the NRF national picture.

### 3. Construction theft and vandalism economics (FBI UCR + NICB data)
FBI Uniform Crime Reporting and NICB data on construction site theft, vandalism, equipment theft, and copper-and-wire theft trends. Per-incident loss distribution. Geographic concentration. What's actually being stolen versus what construction professionals assume is being stolen — the gap is informative.

### 4. Mobile surveillance versus legacy alternatives — full cost and performance comparison
Line-by-line comparison of mobile surveillance against legacy security alternatives:
- Physical guard services ($35-65/hour, single-point coverage)
- Fixed CCTV with no monitoring (deterrent claim, no response)
- Owner self-monitoring (alert fatigue, inconsistent response)
- Hybrid guard + camera programs

Methodology and assumptions documented. Worked-example math for a hypothetical 4-site portfolio over 24 months.

### 5. VDS field observations from 500+ deployments
Operational data from the VDS deployment base across 30+ states:
- Median alert volume by vertical (construction, utility, retail, dealership)
- False alarm rate trend through 2025 (down to 3% — the 97% reduction figure)
- Talk-down event count and outcome distribution
- LE dispatch frequency by site type
- Most common detected incident types by quarter

All anonymized — no customer is individually identifiable. Aggregate data with methodology disclosure.

### 6. NDAA Section 889 and the camera supply chain
A look at how the regulatory environment around foreign-manufactured cameras has evolved through 2024-2026, what's now compliant versus not, and the practical implications for security buyers operating in federal-adjacent, defense, and grant-funded environments. Includes the state-level patchwork (Florida, Texas, Georgia, others).

### 7. AI in physical security — where the hype ends and the operational reality begins
A grounded view of what AI is actually doing in physical security in 2026 — license plate recognition accuracy benchmarks, behavior analytics false positive rates, the limits of facial recognition (and why some vendors deliberately don't deploy it), generative AI's role and non-role in alert triage.

### 8. 2027 predictions
Six specific, falsifiable predictions for 2027:
- Where the market will grow fastest
- Which regulatory shifts to plan for
- What the hardware roadmap looks like across the industry
- Where insurance and surveillance economics will converge
- Two predictions about what won't happen despite vendor hype

Predictions are testable. We'll grade them publicly in the 2027 report.

## Why this report exists

Mobile surveillance is a category that has been undersized in mainstream security industry research for the better part of a decade. Pro-Vigil's annual report is the most-cited reference precisely because nobody else publishes the operational data with methodology disclosed.

VDS publishes the State of Mobile Surveillance to do the same job for our part of the market — and to put on the record what 500+ deployments actually look like, not what marketing decks claim.

## Methodology and citation

This report cites every operational claim to a source: peer-reviewed research where available, government data (FBI UCR, NIBRS, NICB) for crime statistics, third-party market research (referenced by firm and report) for sizing, and VDS field data for our own observations with sample sizes disclosed.

The full methodology section in the report covers data collection, aggregation, anonymization, and the limits of what we are claiming. Journalists and researchers are encouraged to cite specific findings with attribution to the report.

## What you get when you download

- **Full PDF** — 47 pages, designed for screen and print
- **Data appendix** — CSV files of the underlying VDS field data aggregations (anonymized)
- **Citation pack** — pre-formatted citations for academic, journalism, and industry analyst use

Download requires email and company name. We do not require phone numbers, job titles, or "intent to purchase" form fields. We send the report and one follow-up email — nothing else unless you opt in.

faq.q: Is the report actually free, or is it a sales pitch dressed up as a report?
faq.a: Free. The report is content, not a sales document. The data and methodology are the point. If you want to talk to VDS sales after reading it, that's a separate conversation you initiate.

faq.q: Can I cite findings from the report in my own work?
faq.a: Yes — that's the point. Attribute to "Vision Detection Systems, State of Mobile Surveillance in North America 2026" with the page or section reference. A citation pack is included in the download.

faq.q: Will there be a 2027 report?
faq.a: Yes. The report is annual. Each edition grades the prior year's predictions publicly.

faq.q: Is VDS data verifiable by an independent third party?
faq.a: Aggregate field data methodology is documented. Specific customer-level data is not disclosed for privacy reasons but can be audited under NDA by analysts or researchers with credentials.

faq.q: Why is download gated?
faq.a: We track distribution so we know who finds the report useful and can deliver the next edition to them directly. Email and company name only — no other fields.

finalCTAHeading: Download the 2026 Report
finalCTABody: 47 pages, free, no phone-call qualification, no sales pitch in the PDF. Email and company name to receive the report and the data appendix.
